## `hypertask chat`

```text
Attach the logged-in agent session to in-app Agent Chat. Run hypertask chat listen in the background; answer with hypertask chat reply <chat-id> --text <text>.

Usage: hypertask chat <command>

Commands:
  listen
      Poll the agent inbox, send a fresh heartbeat, and print each new message once across restarts. Run hypertask chat listen in the background; answer with hypertask chat reply <chat-id> --text <text>. State is stored under ~/.hypertask/chat; it contains message IDs, never message text. Delivery is at-most-once: state is saved before stdout.
  reply
      Reply to the latest human message in this chat as the logged-in agent. The server deduplicates retries by message ID.

Example:
  hypertask chat listen --once

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask chat listen`

```text
Poll the agent inbox, send a fresh heartbeat, and print each new message once across restarts. Run hypertask chat listen in the background; answer with hypertask chat reply <chat-id> --text <text>. State is stored under ~/.hypertask/chat; it contains message IDs, never message text. Delivery is at-most-once: state is saved before stdout.

Usage: hypertask chat listen [options]

Options:
  --once
      Send one heartbeat and poll once, then exit (nonzero on error).
  --interval <s>
      Polling interval in whole seconds (1-60, default 5); errors back off exponentially up to 60 seconds.

Example:
  hypertask chat listen --once

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask chat reply`

```text
Reply to the latest human message in this chat as the logged-in agent. The server deduplicates retries by message ID.

Usage: hypertask chat reply <chat-id> [options]

Options:
  --text <text> (required)
      Plain-text reply (1-8000 characters).

Example:
  hypertask chat reply <chat-id> --text <text>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask comment`

```text
Manage comments and the agent log

Usage: hypertask comment <command>

Commands:
  list
      List comments on a task. Piped output is plain, tab-separated, complete, and machine-readable (no truncation, no color codes) - safe to parse directly without --json.
  add
      Add comment to task
A Question: comment that @mentions a person using a real mention shows up in their Inbox, split Decisions when enabled: https://app.hypertask.ai/inbox?split=Decisions.
  react
      Add an emoji reaction to a comment
  unreact
      Remove your emoji reaction from a comment
  update
      Update comment
  delete
      Delete comment

Example:
  hypertask comment list --project <id>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask comment add`

```text
Add comment to task
A Question: comment that @mentions a person using a real mention shows up in their Inbox, split Decisions when enabled: https://app.hypertask.ai/inbox?split=Decisions.

Usage: hypertask comment add <ticket-or-task-id> [text] [options]

Options:
  --project <id>
      Project ID; treats a numeric task reference as its board index
  --task <id-or-ticket>, --ticket <id-or-ticket>
      Ticket or task id, as an alternative to the positional argument
  --text <text>
      Comments and descriptions are HTML. Wrap content in block tags. Never embed images; attach files with --attach. Bare text is wrapped in paragraphs.
  --body <body>
      Alias for --text
  --file <path>
      Read comment text from a file; the file holds HTML, same as --text (add --markdown for Markdown)
  --kind <question|qa|done>
      Post a question, QA result, or completion comment for people; omitted kind leaves chatter routing to the server (agents may be saved to the log without notifications)
  --markdown
      Send the comment unchanged for server-side Markdown conversion
  --reply-to-comment-id <id>
      Invoking comment ID when an agent answers a direct comment mention
  --reply-to-invocation-id <id>
      Invocation notification ID when an agent answers a description mention
  --attach <path-or-url>
      Attach local file or http(s) URL to comment (repeatable)
  --improve
      Run the text through the AI writer before posting (default: improve-readability)
  --improve-command <name>
      Which AI rewrite to run with --improve: improve-readability (default), fix-spelling, summarize, make-shorter, or translate:<language>

Example:
  hypertask comment add <ticket-or-task-id> --project <id>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask feedback`

```text
File AI feedback with a kind and a short note, one note per call. There is no list command: filed feedback appears on the board as an ai-feedback ticket. The kind and the note are kept on the filed ticket for our own team's agents and dropped for customer agents. AI agents: run this on your own when a hypertask command fails unexpectedly. Never include task, board or comment content.

Usage: hypertask feedback [note] [options]

Options:
  --kind <bug|friction|missing|idea>
      What you saw: a bug, friction, something missing or an idea. Kept on the ticket for our own team's agents
  --category <value>
      Feedback category: call_failed, empty_result, unexpected_result, auth_failed, slow, user_reported_broken, other (default: other)
  --tool <command name>
      Hypertask command that failed
  --status <http status>
      HTTP status from 100 to 599
  --error-code <slug>
      Error code slug
  --error <message>
      Accepted for compatibility; free text is not stored
  --surface <cli|agent>
      Feedback surface (default: cli)
  --json
      Print the raw JSON response

Example:
  hypertask feedback --kind <bug|friction|missing|idea>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask fields`

```text
Manage custom fields (Number/Text/Select/Date) on a project's tasks

Usage: hypertask fields <command>

Commands:
  list
      List custom fields defined on a project. Piped output is plain, tab-separated, complete, and machine-readable (no truncation, no color codes) - safe to parse directly without --json.
  create
      Create a custom field on a project (idempotent by name)
  set
      Set a custom field's value on a task (auto-creates the field if missing)
  get
      Print a task's custom field values
  delete
      Delete a custom field (and all its values) — by --field-id, or --project + --name

Example:
  hypertask fields list --project <id>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask fields create`

```text
Create a custom field on a project (idempotent by name)

Options:
  --project <id> (required)
      Project ID
  --name <name> (required)
      Field name
  --type <type>
      Field type
  --options <json>
      JSON array of choices for --type Select, e.g. '["Low","Medium","High"]'

  hypertask fields create --project <id> --name <name>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask fields delete`

```text
Delete a custom field (and all its values) — by --field-id, or --project + --name

Options:
  --field-id <uuid>
      Field ID
  --project <id>
      Project ID (with --name, resolves the field id via list)
  --name <name>
      Field name (with --project, resolves the field id via list)

  hypertask fields delete --field-id <uuid>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask fields get`


## `hypertask login`

```text
Login to HyperTask via browser

Usage: hypertask login [options]

Options:
  --token <jwt>
      JWT token (skip browser auth)
  --code <code>
      Five-minute agent sign-in code
  --api-url <url>
      API URL

Example:
  hypertask login --token <jwt>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

### Guided start after token login

```bash
hypertask login --token <token> --human
```

```text
Signed in as Claude Code (agent of Maria Lopez)
Board: Product Launch
https://app.hypertask.ai/project?id=9142

Next steps your agent can run now:
  1. See the board:          hypertask task list --project 9142
  2. Create a first task:    hypertask task create --project 9142 --title "My first task"
  3. Read the board rules:   hypertask project playbook 9142

Or just ask your agent: "What's on my Hypertask board?"
```

Token login checks the token right away. On success, it shows who you are signed in as and the newest board across all boards the token can see. A missing title falls back to the short name. The example above uses a fictional write agent and board.

The CLI prints the server's steps: read-only agents get two steps, list and playbook, with no create step. If no board is available, `--human` says "No board yet. Create one in your Hypertask web app."

JSON is the default output. It keeps `success`, `saved`, and `configPath`, and adds:

| Field | What it contains |
|-------|------------------|
| `signedInAs` | The signed-in identity, including `name`. |
| `board` | The board's `id`, `title`, and `url`. |
| `nextSteps` | The server's suggested steps (three for write agents, two for read-only agents, none without a board), each with a CLI `command`. |
| `moreBoards` | A hint to run `hypertask project list` when the token can see several boards. |

The CLI waits at most about 1.5 seconds for the guide. If it times out or fails because of a network or server error, login still saves the token. It returns the previous saved-token output without the guided start. Saving a token does not mean the check passed.

## `hypertask pages`

```text
Manage task pages

Usage: hypertask pages <command>

Commands:
  create
      Create a page
  get
      Get a page
  append
      Append content to a page; keep the existing content type unless --canvas, --html or --markdown is passed
  update
      Update a page; keep the existing content type unless --canvas, --html or --markdown is passed
  list
      List pages by task or project
  archive
      Archive a page (soft delete)
  history
      List a page's saved versions
  restore
      Restore a page from a saved version
  search
      Search pages

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask pages append`

```text
Append content to a page; keep the existing content type unless --canvas, --html or --markdown is passed

Usage: hypertask pages append <id> [options]

Options:
  --content <content>
      Content to append
  --markdown-file <path>
      Read content to append from a file
  --content-file <path>
      Read content to append from a file, any type
  --html-file <path>
      Read HTML content to append from a file
  --html
      Treat content as HTML
  --canvas
      Treat content as an HTML canvas page (html_canvas)
  --markdown
      Treat content as Markdown (explicitly change the page type)
  --title <title>
      New page title
  --if-version <n>
      Only update this page version
  --note <text>
      Update note

Example:
  hypertask pages append <id> --content <content>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask project`

```text
Manage projects/boards

Usage: hypertask project <command>

Commands:
  list
      List all projects. Piped output is plain, tab-separated, complete, and machine-readable (no truncation, no color codes) - safe to parse directly without --json.
  show
      Show project metadata, ticket prefix, sections, and labels. Piped output is plain, tab-separated, complete, and machine-readable (no truncation, no color codes) - safe to parse directly without --json.
  update
      Rename a project/board
  manifest
      Show a project's ordered columns and transition policy
  playbook
      Show or replace a project's working rules and definition of done
  instructions
      Show or set a project's custom AI instructions
  members
      List project members. Piped output is plain, tab-separated, complete, and machine-readable (no truncation, no color codes) - safe to parse directly without --json.
  sections
      List sections in a project (alias: section list --project <id>). Piped output is plain, tab-separated, complete, and machine-readable (no truncation, no color codes) - safe to parse directly without --json.
  invite
      Invite user/agent to the board
  labels
      List available labels for a project. Piped output is plain, tab-separated, complete, and machine-readable (no truncation, no color codes) - safe to parse directly without --json.
  label
      Manage labels
  archive
      Archive a board you own (use --restore to put it back)
  delete
      Permanently delete a board and all its tasks. Requires board owner or admin access and --yes.
  create-board
      Create a board. Flags: --title <t> --team <id> [--sections a,b,c]. Or a JSON manifest via --manifest <file>/--stdin (team_id, title, sections[], optional labels[], tasks[]).
  github
      List the GitHub repositories connected to a board, or replace them with: project github <board> set --repository-ids <csv>. The current settings version is read first, so one command is enough. Board admins only.

Example:
  hypertask project list --limit <n>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

```text
  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask project create-board`

```text
Create a board. Flags: --title <t> --team <id> [--sections a,b,c]. Or a JSON manifest via --manifest <file>/--stdin (team_id, title, sections[], optional labels[], tasks[]).

Usage: hypertask project create-board [options]

Options:
  --title <title>
      Board title (flag mode)
  --team <id>
      Team/workspace id the board belongs to (flag mode)
  --sections <list>
      Comma-separated column names (default: To Do,In Progress,Done)
  --description <text>
      Board description (flag mode)
  --labels <list>
      Comma-separated label names (flag mode)
  --manifest <path>
      Path to JSON manifest file
  --stdin
      Read JSON from stdin (pipe a file: cat manifest.json | hypertask project create-board --stdin)

Example:
  hypertask project create-board --title <title>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask section done`

```text
Mark a column as finished: reports count its tickets as completed, Inbox Zero clears them, agents stop treating them as blocking

Usage: hypertask section done [options]

Options:
  --project <id> (required)
      Project ID
  --section <id|name> (required)
      Section ID or name
  --off
      Mark the column as NOT finished
  --clear
      Remove the setting and fall back to guessing from the column name

Example:
  hypertask section done --project <id> --section <id|name>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

```text

      Show help
```

## `hypertask task`

```text
Manage tasks

Usage: hypertask task <command>

a ticket's comments are read with: hypertask comment list <ticket>

Commands:
  list
      List tasks with filters. Piped output is plain, tab-separated, complete, and machine-readable (no truncation, no color codes) - safe to parse directly without --json.
  next
      List the highest-priority unleased tasks in a project
  get
      Get task details. Piped output is plain, tab-separated, complete, and machine-readable (no truncation, no color codes) - safe to parse directly without --json.
  agent-log
      Read a ticket's agent activity log, newest first (read-only)
  description-history
      List a task's saved description versions
  description-restore
      Restore a task description from a saved version
  context
      Get a read-only task context pack for agent sessions
  tree
      Show full parent/subtask hierarchy for a task
  link
      Link two tasks by numeric ID or ticket number
  unlink
      Remove the relation between two tasks by numeric ID or ticket number
  relations
      List relations for a task
  related
      Find semantically related tasks
  create
      Create a new task
  update
      Update a task
  assign
      Assign a user or agent to a task (idempotent: repeat assign is a no-op)
  waiting-on
      Set the waiting person, or clear both person and comment blocker
  blocker-comment
      Mark or clear the blocking comment without changing the waiting person
  move-to-inbox
      Route a task into a project member's inbox (like the palette action)
  unassign
      Remove a user or agent from task assignees (use --all with --project to clear one assignee across the board)
  move
      Move task: ticket + section (or --section) for the same board, or numeric task id + --to for another project
  move-board
      Move task to a different project/board (first arg = numeric task id)
  search
      Search tasks. Piped output is plain, tab-separated, complete, and machine-readable (no truncation, no color codes) - safe to parse directly without --json.

Example:
  hypertask task list --project <id>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask task agent-log`

```text
Read a ticket's agent activity log, newest first (read-only)

Usage: hypertask task agent-log <ticket-or-task-id> [options]

Options:
  --project <id>
      Project ID; treats a numeric task reference as its board index
  --limit <n>
      Number of entries (1-100, default 20)
  --agent <uuid>
      Filter by agent UUID

Example:
  hypertask task agent-log <ticket-or-task-id> --project <id>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask task assign`

```text
Assign a user or agent to a task (idempotent: repeat assign is a no-op)

Usage: hypertask task assign <ticket> [options]

Options:
  --assignee <id>
      Numeric user ID, or agent UUID from `projects members <id>`
  --agent <name|id>
      Agent display name from `projects members <id>`, an agent UUID, or `me` for the calling agent
  --self
      Assign the calling agent to the task (agent token only, no --assignee needed)
  --project <id>
      Project ID; treats a numeric task reference as its board index

Example:
  hypertask task assign <ticket> --assignee <id>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask task blocker-comment`

```text
Mark or clear the blocking comment without changing the waiting person

Usage: hypertask task blocker-comment <ticket> [options]

Options:
  --comment-id <id|none> (required)
      Positive comment ID on this ticket, or none to clear its red border
  --reason <text>
      Why the blocker is cleared; the server requires it from an agent. Use with --comment-id none
  --project <id>
      Project ID for a bare ticket number; ambiguous task IDs are refused

Example:
  hypertask task blocker-comment <ticket> --comment-id <id|none>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask task context`

```text
Get a read-only task context pack for agent sessions

Usage: hypertask task context <ticket-or-id> [options]

Options:
  --project <id>
      Expected project ID (guards against mismatches)
  --summary
      Return a shorter recent-comment subset

Example:
  hypertask task context <ticket-or-id> --project <id>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask task create`

```text
Create a new task

Usage: hypertask task create [options]

Options:
  --project <id> (required)
      Project ID
  --title <text> (required)
      Task title
  --description <text>
      Comments and descriptions are HTML. Wrap content in block tags. Never embed images; attach files with --attach. Bare text is wrapped in paragraphs.
  --description-file <path>
      Read task description from a local file instead of --description (takes precedence if both given)
  --markdown
      Send the description unchanged for server-side Markdown conversion
  --priority <p>
      Priority: urgent, high, medium, low, none
  --estimate <n>
      Size index: 0 = none, 2-6 = XS,S,M,L,XL
  --labels <list>
      Comma-separated label names or IDs (repeatable; e.g. "CLI,BUG")
  --due <date>
      Due date (ISO 8601)
  --parent-task <ref>
      Parent task: internal id or ticket ref (e.g. HTPR-4578)
  --section <id|name>
      Section ID or name (e.g. 4005 or "Doing")
  --assignee <list>
      Comma-separated user IDs (e.g. "123" or "123,456,789")
  --attach <path-or-url>
      Attach local file or http(s) URL after task is created (repeatable)

Example:
  hypertask task create --project <id> --title <text>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask task list`

```text
List tasks with filters. Piped output is plain, tab-separated, complete, and machine-readable (no truncation, no color codes) - safe to parse directly without --json.

Usage: hypertask task list [options]

Options:
  --project <id>
      Project ID
  --search <query>
      Search tasks by keyword instead of listing. When set, only --project scoping is applied; other list filters are ignored.
  --section <id|name>
      Section column ID or name (name requires --project)
  --assigned-to <value>
      Assignee (me, unassigned, or user ID)
  --assignee <value>
      Assignee (me, unassigned, or user ID). Same as --assigned-to
  --created-by <id>
      Creator user ID (numeric; server-side filter)
  --priority <list>
      Comma-separated priorities: urgent,high,medium,low
  --labels <list>
      Comma-separated label names or IDs (names need --project)
  --label <list>
      Comma-separated label names or IDs (names need --project)
  --sort-by <field>
      Sort tasks by: createdAt, updatedAt, dueDate, priority, title
  --sort-order <asc|desc>
      Set the sort order of results by asc or desc
  --limit <n>
      Results per page
  --offset <n>
      Pagination offset
  --status <field>
      Filter tasks by status (Normal, Archive, Deleted)
  --has-due-date
      Only tasks that have a due date set
  --query <text>
      Free-text search
  --filter <key=value>
      Structured filter (repeatable). Keys: section, label, assignee, status, updated_since, has_pr
  --sort <field>
      Sort as field or field:asc|desc
  --fields <names>
      Comma-separated projection, for example title,url
  --cursor <token>
      Opaque cursor from the previous page

Example:
  hypertask task list --project <id>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask task move`

```text
Move task: ticket + section (or --section) for the same board, or numeric task id + --to for another project

Usage: hypertask task move <ticket-or-task-id> [section] [options]

Options:
  --project <id>
      Project ID; treats a numeric task reference as its board index
  --section <name>
      Destination section name within same board (e.g. "Doing", "Done"); the value may also be the second argument
  --to <id>
      Target project ID — cross-board move (first arg must be numeric task id)
  --to-section <id>
      Target section ID in destination project (use with --to)

Example:
  hypertask task move <ticket-or-task-id> --project <id>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask task unassign`

```text
Remove a user or agent from task assignees (use --all with --project to clear one assignee across the board)

Usage: hypertask task unassign [ticket] [options]

Options:
  --assignee <id>
      Numeric user ID (removes every row shown under that user in `tasks get`, including agent-linked rows) or agent UUID from `projects members <id>`
  --agent <name|id>
      Agent display name from `projects members <id>`, an agent UUID, or `me` for the calling agent
  --self
      Unassign the calling agent
  --project <id>
      Project ID (required with --all; with a numeric ticket, prefers board index then falls back to list id)
  --all
      Unassign the chosen person from every Normal, Archive, and Deleted task on --project

Example:
  hypertask task unassign --assignee <id>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask task update`

```text
Update a task

Usage: hypertask task update <ticket-or-task-id> [options]

Options:
  --title <text>
      New title
  --description <text>
      Comments and descriptions are HTML. Wrap content in block tags. Never embed images; attach files with --attach. Bare text is wrapped in paragraphs.
  --description-file <path>
      Read new description from a local file instead of --description (takes precedence if both given)
  --markdown
      Send the description unchanged for server-side Markdown conversion
  --pull-request <url>
      Link a GitHub pull request to the task
  --priority <p>
      New priority
  --estimate <n>
      Size index: 0 = none, 2-6 = XS,S,M,L,XL
  --due <date>
      New due date
  --clear-due
      Remove the task's due date
  --status <s>
      New status: Normal, Archive, Deleted
  --section <id|name>
      Section ID or name (e.g. 4005 or "Doing")
  --project <id>
      Project ID; treats a numeric task reference as its board index
  --assignee <list>
      Comma-separated user IDs (e.g. "123" or "123,456,789"). An empty value clears every assignee.
  --clear-assignees
      Remove every assignee from the task
  --labels <list>
      Replace the ticket's entire label set. Repeatable/comma-separated for this call only. Does not append. An empty value clears every label. Use --add-label to keep existing labels.
  --clear-labels
      Remove every label from the task; cannot combine with --labels values, --add-label(s), or --remove-label(s)
  --add-labels <list>
      Comma-separated label names or IDs to add, keeping existing labels (repeatable; e.g. "QA")
  --add-label <list>
      Alias of --add-labels. Add labels without dropping the ones already on the ticket (repeatable).
  --remove-labels <list>
      Comma-separated label names or IDs to remove, keeping other labels (repeatable)
  --remove-label <list>
      Alias of --remove-labels. Remove labels without dropping the ones you did not name (repeatable).
  --parent-task <ref>
      Parent task: internal id or ticket ref (e.g. HTPR-4578)
  --clear-parent
      Detach this task from its parent
  --attach <path>
      Attach local file to task after update (repeatable)

Example:
  hypertask task update <ticket-or-task-id> --title <text>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

```text
  --project <id>

  -h, --help
```

## `hypertask time`

```text
Track time

Usage: hypertask time <command>

Commands:
  start
      Start tracking time for a task
  stop
      Stop tracking time for a task
  pause
      Pause the running timer for a task
  resume
      Resume the paused timer for a task
  status
      Show time-tracking status for a task
  log
      Log time with optional note/date, or subtract from your latest completed entry with negative minutes (no metadata)
  update
      Update a completed time entry; provide at least one of --minutes, --date or --note
  delete
      Delete a time entry
  running
      List running timers
  report
      Show a time report

Example:
  hypertask time start <task>

  -h, --help
      Show help
```

## `hypertask time resume`

```text
Resume the paused timer for a task
```
