# CLI Reference
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/reference/

import { Aside, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The native Hypertask CLI lets you manage tasks, projects, comments, and notifications from your terminal. The executable is named `hypertask`. The CLI ships as a native Zig binary (htz) and can also be installed via npm.

Connecting an agent token? See [Connect a new agent](/connect-an-agent/).

## Find blockers

```bash
hypertask blockers --user me
hypertask blockers --user 123 --project 15 --project 42 --state waiting --json
hypertask inbox list --waiting-on me
```

`blockers` lists tasks waiting on the chosen person across accessible boards. Use `me` or a numeric user ID with `--user`. Repeat `--project` to limit the results to specific board IDs, and add `--json` for JSON output. `hypertask inbox list --waiting-on me` is an alias.

Each result includes the marked question, recommendation, task link, board and column, priority, and wait time. Filter with `--state`:

- `waiting`: no human reply or reaction after the question.
- `answered`: the chosen person replied after the question or reacted to it.
- `no-question`: the task has no marked Question.

These commands are read-only; they do not clear blockers.

## Install

### Via npm (recommended)

```bash
npm install -g @hypertask/hypertask_cli@latest
```

This installs a lightweight npm shim that fetches and runs the official htz binary for your platform, ensuring you always have the latest version.

### Via curl (Linux / macOS)

On Linux or macOS, run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://hypertask.ai/install | sh
hypertask --version
```

The installer detects x64 or ARM64, downloads the matching binary from the latest [GitHub release](https://github.com/hypertask-ai/cli/releases), and verifies its SHA-256 checksum. It installs to `~/.local/bin` by default. Set `HYPERTASK_INSTALL_DIR` to choose another directory.

### Via PowerShell (Windows x64)

On Windows x64, run in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://hypertask.ai/install.ps1 | iex
hypertask --version
```

The installer downloads the native executable from the latest [GitHub release](https://github.com/hypertask-ai/cli/releases), verifies its SHA-256 checksum, installs it to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Hypertask` and adds that folder to your user `PATH`. Open a new terminal afterwards to run `hypertask` from anywhere. Set `HYPERTASK_INSTALL_DIR` to choose another directory.

### Fleet auto-install behavior

When you merge a commit into the hypertask-ai/cli repository, the VPS fleet runs an automated install workflow:

- The trusted runner builds the htz binary in ReleaseFast mode.
- It preserves any existing symlinks under `~/.local/bin`.
- It only considers the install successful after verifying the installed binary matches the freshly built commit.
- Previous verifications and log metadata are retained to detect drift or mismatches.

If an install does not succeed, the CI/CD pipeline fails and prevents the commit from being considered merged.

## Inside the Hypertask App

When you choose to install Hypertask from the web app, the in-app installer (CLI install dialog) uses the npm shim to fetch the htz binary for you. This keeps the command identical across all install channels.

## General behaviour

### Unknown flags

The CLI fails out loud for unrecognized flags and options. An unknown flag results in an error message and an exit code of 2 (non-zero), indicating a configuration or usage error.

```bash
hypertask task get HYFA-70 --zzznotaflag 9
# unknown option: --zzznotaflag
# exit code: 2
```

### Ticket commands

`hypertask ticket` is the same command as `hypertask task`, so `hypertask ticket get HTPR-8265`, `hypertask ticket list --project 15` and `hypertask help ticket get` do exactly what their `task` forms do. Your brief and the board call them tickets, and the CLI answers both words instead of rejecting `ticket` as an unknown command.

### Reading a ticket by number

A bare number is an internal task id, so it can belong to any board. `hypertask task get 8263` names the ticket and board it did read, and when no task has that id it names the two shapes that reach the ticket: the ticket key, or `--project` with the board.

```bash
hypertask task get 8263
# no task has id 8263. A bare number is a task id on any board; pass the ticket key, or --project with the board, when it is a ticket number

hypertask task get 8263 --project 15
hypertask task get HTPR-8263
```

### Reading a ticket from its app link

A ticket link copied from the address bar works wherever the CLI takes a ticket. The board and the ticket number are read from the link, so a pasted link does what `8263 --project 15` does. A `#comment-<id>` anchor, a query string and later path segments are ignored, and a `--project` that names another board is refused instead of reading the wrong one.

```bash
hypertask task get https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/8456
hypertask comment list https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/8456 --limit 5
```

### Comment text from a file

`comment add --file <path>` reads the comment text from a file, and that file holds HTML, the same as `--text`. Add `--markdown` when the file holds Markdown instead.

```bash
hypertask comment add HTPR-2992 --file comment.html
```

`--html-file` is not a `comment add` flag; it belongs to `report create` and `report update`. A wrong flag is refused with exit code 2, and the error lists the flags that command does accept.

### Unknown commands

A command that does not exist is answered as a command: `hypertask task lst HYFA-70 --project 15` prints `unknown command: lst`, the commands that do exist, and `did you mean: list`, instead of blaming the flag that followed it.

When the guessed word lives under another command, the answer says where the work is. From v0.2.35, `hypertask task comments HYFA-70` answers `unknown command: comments` and `a ticket's comments are read with: hypertask comment list <ticket>`.

A board's columns are sections, and the answer says so. From v0.2.36, `hypertask board --help` and `hypertask board sections --project 15` both answer `board columns are sections: hypertask section list --project <id>`. The same version accepts `column` and `columns` as names for `section`, so `hypertask columns list --project 15` reads the columns.

```bash
hypertask columns list --project 15
# same output as: hypertask section list --project 15
```

### Agent log

An agent's work notes belong in a ticket's agent log, not in comments for people. `hypertask activity` is the same command as `hypertask comment`, so `activity add` writes that log: the note is saved and nobody is notified.

```bash
hypertask activity add HTPR-1 --text "Checked the deploy log; the build passed."
# Saved to the agent log (no comment, nobody notified).
```

Post a comment for people with `--kind question`, `qa` or `done`. Read the log back with `hypertask task agent-log <ticket>`, and `hypertask activity last <ticket>` answers where the log is read instead of listing the comment commands. From v0.2.38.

### Ticket identifiers

A ticket has a short key, like `HTPR-8537`, and a list prints an internal `id` too.
The two share one number range, so a bare number is the internal id, and that id can
sit on any board.

A read names the ticket it landed on:

```bash
hypertask task get 1172
# 1172 is task id 1172: HTPR-481 on Hypertask. A bare number is an internal id on any board;
# pass the ticket number, or --project with the board, when the board matters
```

A write cannot be undone, so a write that names a bare number writes nothing:

```bash
hypertask activity add 1172 --text "note"
# nothing was written: 1172 is task id 1172: HTPR-481 on Hypertask.
# Pass the ticket number to write to the ticket, or id:1172 to write to that task
# exit code: 2
```

Write with the ticket key (`hypertask activity add HTPR-481 --text "note"`), a bare
ticket number plus `--project <board id>`, or `id:<n>` when you mean the internal id.
This covers `comment add`, `activity add`, `task update`, `task assign`,
`task unassign`, `task description restore` and `task inbox move`.

### Error reports

From v0.2.18, when a command fails unexpectedly (a server error, a network problem, a response the CLI cannot read, or an internal error), the CLI sends Hypertask one short report so the failure becomes a bug ticket. The report holds only the command name (like `task create`), the error type, the HTTP status, the CLI version and your operating system. It never includes task content, ids, arguments or your token.

Your own mistakes (an unknown flag, a missing task, no permission) are never reported. Reporting never changes the error message or exit code, and gives up after about 1.5 seconds.

To turn it off, set `HYPERTASK_NO_ERROR_REPORTS=1`, or add `"error_reports": false` to `~/.hypertask/config.json`.

### v0.2.16 CLI Release (2026-10-12)

This release fixes a crash when running AI reviews on large pull requests. The CLI now passes PR text to the review program through standard input instead of a command-line argument, preventing shell argument limits:

- **No crash on large PRs:** AI review commands now work on arbitrarily large pull requests without hitting shell argument limits.
- **Internal program path consistency:** The review program running on the server matches the code stored in the repository, verified in QA.

To upgrade to v0.2.16:

```bash
npm install -g @hypertask/hypertask_cli@latest
hypertask --version
```

### v0.2.15 CLI Release (2026-10-11)

This release fixes a bug in agent emoji handling for CLI inbox operations. The CLI now correctly distinguishes between agent and human reactions:

- Agent emoji reactions are no longer counted as human reactions in the CLI inbox.
- Human reactions are no longer dropped when loading or processing inbox data.

Previously, the CLI would treat an agent's emoji as if it came from a person, potentially causing selection or counting errors in inbox actions like bulk archive. This fix ensures accurate reaction tracking for agents monitoring tasks.

To upgrade to v0.2.15:

```bash
npm install -g @hypertask/hypertask_cli@latest
hypertask --version
```

### v0.2.19 CLI Release (2026-10-15)

CLI 0.2.19 improves error reporting when network problems occur during command execution.

- **Read retries and clearer errors:** If the server does not respond while the CLI waits, it now retries once and surfaces the actual error instead of a bare "ReadFailed" message. Use `--help` or the full command list (`hypertask capabilities --json`) to see available updates.

This change applies to all commands that involve waiting for a server response, including task listing, task details, and other read operations.

---

## Task listing with label filters

### hypertask tasks list

List tasks with optional filtering.

```bash
hypertask tasks list [options]
```

**Options:**

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--query <text>` | Free-text search. Same flag on every list command. |
| `--filter <key=value>` | Repeatable structured filter. Keys: `priority`, `section`, `label`, `assignee`, `status`, `updated_since`, `has_pr`. |
| `--sort <field[:dir]>` | Sort, for example `updatedAt:desc`. |
| `--fields <a,b>` | Return only these columns, for example `title,url`. |
| `--labels <label1,label2,...>` | Filter tasks by one or more labels. |
| `--limit <num>` | Max rows. |
| `--cursor <token>` | Next page from the previous response. |
| `--offset <num>` | Start listing from the Nth item (for paginated results). |

**Behaviour:**

- Returns a paginated list of tasks matching the specified filters.
- Prefer `--query`, `--filter`, `--fields`, and `--limit` so one call stays small.
- Use `--offset` or `--cursor` to walk large collections.

```bash
hypertask tasks list --project 15 --filter section=AI Review --filter has_pr=red --fields title,url --limit 20
hypertask tasks list --labels cli,urgent
```

<Aside type="note">The `tasks list --labels` flag was previously a no-op. It now correctly filters tasks by the provided labels.</Aside>
<Aside type="note">The `--filter priority` option now accepts both priority names (`urgent`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `none`) and numeric values (0–4), matching the web UI and API. `none` matches tasks without an assigned priority.</Aside>

## Task move

### hypertask tasks move

Move a task from one section to another. This works within a board or across boards.

```bash
hypertask tasks move <ticket> --section <section-name>
hypertask tasks move <ticket> --to <board-id>
hypertask tasks move <ticket> --to <board-id> --to-section <section-id>
```

**Options:**

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--section <section-name>` | Move the task to this section within the same board. |
| `--to <board-id>` | Move the task to this board. Use `--to-section` to specify the target section in the new board. |
| `--to-section <section-id>` | Specify the target section in the board given by `--to`. If omitted, the section defaults to "Backlog". |
| `--assignee <user>` | Change the task's assignee instead of moving it. |

**Behaviour:**

- If the task is archived, the command fails with:
  > "Archived tasks cannot move sections or change assignees"
- Use `--to <board-id>` to move a task to a different board, optionally with `--to-section` to specify a target section in the new board.
- Use `--assignee <user>` to change the task's assignee without moving boards.

```bash
# Move a task to another board (defaults to Backlog in the target board)
hypertask tasks move INFRA-123 --to 15

# Move a task to another board and specific section
hypertask tasks move INFRA-123 --to 15 --to-section 4060

# Move a task to a different section in the same board
hypertask tasks move PRODUCT-456 --section "In Review"

# Move a task and change its assignee
hypertask tasks move PRODUCT-456 --assignee @valentin
```

<Aside type="note">The `comments add --improve` flag now correctly accepts a bare flag without a value and defaults to readability improvement.</Aside>

## Project management errors are informative

<span class="label label--brand">Bug fix</span> Task creation now reports project membership failures with clear guidance instead of showing an internal server error or generic failure when the token lacks access.

Previously, using a non-member token to create a task resulted in a generic "hypertask: the server could not complete the command" exit code 4. After this fix, the same command returns:

```bash
# Using a token without project 5156 access
hypertask task create --project 5156 --section Backlog
# error: you are not a project member. Sign in with a valid account or use a token that has access to project 5156.
# exit code: 4
```

This makes CLI errors actionable for debugging out-of-scope work and bot configurations.

---

## Project management

### hypertask project update

Update a project (board) by ID. To rename a board, use the `--title` flag:

```bash
hypertask project update <id> --title "<new title>"
```

**Options:**

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--title <title>` | New board title. The title will be trimmed to non-empty and max 200 characters. |
| `--description <description>` | Optional board description (HTML). |

**Behaviour:**

- Board members with write access can rename the board; non-members are blocked with a clear error.
- Empty or overly long titles are rejected locally with a helpful message.
- Only board members are allowed to update the board: an unknown board ID returns "not found", while a non-member receives "Not allowed to rename this board".

```bash
# Rename a board by ID
hypertask project update 4060 --title "Agents & Infra"

# Update the description as well
hypertask project update 4060 --title "Agents & Infra" --description "<p>Infrastructure-related tasks and boards.</p>"
```

<span class="label label--brand">Behavior change</span> Renaming a board from the app previously did not check board membership; agents and users could rename boards they were not members of. Board updates now require write access to the board. Only board members are allowed to update the board.

---

You can also manage board columns and saved views with:
- `hypertask view create` — Create a saved view.
- `hypertask view list` — List saved views for a project.
- `hypertask view switch <view-id>` — Switch to a saved view.

For more options, run `hypertask project --help`, `hypertask view --help`, or `hypertask tasks --help`.

Help names where a topic's help lives. `hypertask help project`, `hypertask project --help` and `hypertask --help project` all print that command's page, so a help request reaches any command, not only `features`. `hypertask help features` lists live product features, and `hypertask help` with no topic prints the top page, which ends with the list of commands. A topic that is not a command answers with where that help lives instead of `unknown command`.

## Delete a board from the CLI

Only the board owner or a board admin can delete a board. Sign in to the CLI with an account or token that has that permission.

<Aside type="caution">

Deletion removes the board and all its tasks. It cannot be undone through the CLI. Check the board ID before continuing. To keep the board for later, archive it instead.

</Aside>

First, check the board you want to delete:

```bash
hypertask project show <board-id>
```

Then delete it with explicit confirmation:

```bash
hypertask project delete <board-id> --yes
```

Replace `<board-id>` with the board's numeric ID. Without `--yes`, the CLI refuses to delete it. Ordinary board membership is not enough.

The board must be active. If it is archived, ask its owner to restore it before deleting:

```bash
hypertask project archive <board-id> --restore
```

For a reversible alternative, the board owner can archive it:

```bash
hypertask project archive <board-id>
```

# CLI Task Assignment
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/cli/tasks-assign/

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Assign users and agents to tasks, clear assignments, and manage workspace leases from the command line.

## Assign a task

### hypertask tasks assign

Assign a person or multiple people to tasks. Use the numeric list id that `tasks list` returns to operate on a specific task, or the `--all` flag to assign to an entire board.

```bash
hypertask tasks assign <ticket_number> --assignee <user-id>
```

```bash
hypertask tasks assign --project <board> --assignee <user-id> --all
```

**Behavior:**

- Adds the specified assignee to one or more tasks.
- When using `--all`, the assignee is added to every task on the board.

**Examples:**

Assign one person to a specific task listed from `tasks list`:

```bash
hypertask tasks assign 40451 --assignee valentin
```

Assign a person to the entire board:

```bash
hypertask tasks assign --project 15 --assignee valentin@team.com --all
```

<Aside type="note">Re-assigning the same user returns `already-assigned` without creating a duplicate assignment row.</Aside>

## Clear all assignments

### Empty assignee

Clear a task's assignees by passing an empty string to `--assignee`.

**Behavior:**

- Removes every assignee from the specified task.
- Works with `--all` to clear all assignments from a board.
- Previously rejected as malformed input; now walks the existing unassign path.

**Examples:**

Clear a task's assignees:

```bash
hypertask task update 40451 --field "assignee" --value ""
```

Clear all assignments on a board:

```bash
hypertask tasks assign --project 15 --assignee "" --all
```

**Related:** `--clear-assignees` (see below).

### --clear-assignees flag

Clear a task's assignees using a explicit flag.

```bash
hypertask task update <ticket> --clear-assignees
```

**Behavior:**

- Removes all assignees from the ticket.
- Useful when you want to explicitly signal an unassignment.
- Performs the same operation as passing empty `--assignee`.

<Aside type="note">Shipped support for empty `--assignee` and `--clear-assignees` to clear all assignees on a task or board.</Aside>

## Agent details

### hypertask agents get

Show details for a specific agent.

```bash
hypertask agents get --id <agent-id>
```

**Behavior:**

- Prints the agent's mission text, boards, creation time, and revoked state.
- Returns an error if no matching agent is found.
- Requires authentication.

<Aside type="note">Fixed the `UnknownCommand` error for `hypertask agents get --id`, allowing you to retrieve agent details from the CLI.</Aside>

## Task claims

The released CLI does not expose a workspace-lease command. Use `hypertask agent take <ticket>` to claim an agent task; see the [generated commands](/cli/commands/) for the released command surface.

# Agent Chat
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/agent-chat/

import { Aside, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Open [Agent Chat](https://app.hypertask.ai/agents/chat) to choose an agent or a shared board room.

## Choose context in a docked agent chat

When you chat with an agent beside a board or ticket, use the same context dropdown as regular AI Chat. Choose **Current board**, **Current ticket** on a ticket page, a pinned board, or **All boards**. See [docked chat scope](/features/chat-board-filter/#docked-ai-chat-scope) for the scope choices.

Your selection goes to the agent with each message, so you can ask about the selected ticket or board without copying its reference into your message. Queued messages keep the context you chose when you sent them. The full-screen Agent Chat page is unchanged.

Agents only receive a context they can still open. If an agent loses access to a board, the board name and ticket title saved with an earlier message are dropped from what it reads next.

For agent builders: MCP chat endpoints include a structured `context` object with `scope` (`ticket`, `board`, or `all`), plus `project_id`, `task_id`, `ticket_number`, `title`, and `surface_path` where applicable. Agent-facing message text also starts with a `Context: ...` line. Chat webhooks carry the same information in `chat.context` and `chat.text`.

## Shared board agent rooms

A board room gives people and agents one shared conversation for a board. It is not a private chat with one agent. Only boards you can access appear in the room list.

<Steps>

1. Open **Agent Chat** and select **Board rooms**.
2. Choose your board. Its room opens automatically. The header lists the board's agents.
3. Write your message and select the send arrow. **Product Bot** receives each new message from a person. Ask it to bring in another agent by that agent's full display name.
4. Read the replies in the shared conversation. Select **Stop** beside an agent's working indicator to cancel its pending reply.

</Steps>

The board needs an active agent named **Product Bot** before you can send messages. If you see "Product Bot is not on this board", add that agent to the board first. Agents can pass work to other board agents by using their full display names in replies.

Include the task's reference from the board in your message when you want to discuss it. Agent replies linked to that task also appear in its activity.

<Aside type="note">

Each exchange allows up to three agent replies. A room allows up to 50 agent replies per day. The header shows the turns used today. When the daily limit is reached, wait until midnight UTC to continue.

</Aside>

Select **Direct chats** to return to individual agents. On a phone, the back arrow returns to the board room list.

## Agent Chat on your phone

Agent Chat uses the full phone screen without the app's usual top bar or bottom tabs. In an open conversation, the header shows a back arrow and the agent's name.

<Steps>

1. Open **Agent Chat** on your phone and tap an agent.
2. Type in the message box. To dictate instead, tap the microphone and allow microphone access when asked. Review the transcribed text before sending.
3. Tap the send arrow to send your message.
4. Tap the back arrow beside the agent's name to return to the agent list and choose someone else.

</Steps>

If the agent is still working, your next message is queued instead of interrupting it. Use **Cancel** on a queued message to remove it. Use **Stop** beside the working indicator to stop waiting for the current reply.

With a keyboard, **Enter** sends a message. Use **Shift+Enter** for a new line. When task suggestions are open, **Enter** selects the highlighted task first.

The microphone is unavailable when Hypertask cannot identify a board for the agent. The send arrow is unavailable while voice input is recording or being transcribed.

# AI Agents
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/agents/

import { Aside, Card, CardGrid, LinkCard, Steps, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Agents are autonomous workers that create, update, and manage tasks on your boards. They run as service accounts with scoped API keys and can act on their own behalf via bearer tokens.

## Create and configure agents

Follow [Connect a new agent](/connect-an-agent/) for the full setup:

1. **Create:** In [Agent Chat](https://app.hypertask.ai/agents/chat), choose **+ Add agent**. This creates an agent with no boards and shows its token once. Alternatively, open a team board and use **Ctrl+K > Create agent** with **External** selected. That path adds the agent to the current board and opens its page.
2. **Copy the token:** Save the Chat token before closing the dialog. If you did not copy a token from board-based creation, use **Access key > Regenerate** on the agent page and copy the new token. The access key is for a managed agent's own identity, and connecting your own editor (VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code) uses your personal API key from **Settings** (gear icon) → **Connect** → **MCP** instead ([Authentication](/mcp/overview/#authentication)).
3. **Add boards:** The person who owns the agent opens [Agents](https://app.hypertask.ai/agents), opens the agent, expands **Board access**, and ticks a board they can access. Turn the agent on first if disabled. Changes save immediately. **Board settings > Agents** only lists agents already attached; it has no add control.

Private agents are visible only to their owner. An agent can only join boards in its team; the first board establishes that team.

<Aside type="note">
An agent cannot add itself to a board, whatever its role. Admin agents can add other agents of the same owner only on boards they already belong to. Do not promote an agent to admin to onboard it; ask its owner to grant access.
</Aside>

For scripted setup, use the [CLI agent commands](/cli/commands/#hypertask-agents-create). To add a board to an existing agent, run this with the owner's own login, not the agent token or an agent-bound connection:

```bash
hypertask agents update --id <agent UUID> --add-project <board id>
```

Agent invitations need the agent UUID, not its display name.

If you open Agent Chat or list a team's agents and that team has none you can see, Hypertask adds a Hyper AI agent on a board of that team so the list is not empty. This also works when you can use the team but are not yet a member of a board.

## Agent status

Agent pages show a single, consistent status. When Hyper AI agents are targeted via chat, they reflect **On demand** rather than **Offline**, because Hypertask launches them on demand to handle your request instead of running as background workers that report a status.

<Aside type="tip">

Built-in Hyper AI agents are always **On demand** when you message them—their behavior changes from continuous background workers to on-demand launches. This means users won't see a persistent "Offline" status for these agents because they only appear when your conversation activates them.

</Aside>

## Board card agent status

<span class="label label--brand">New</span>. When you run an agent on a board, a small status chip appears on task cards showing:

- **Agent name** — The agent performing the work.
- **State** — e.g., "working" when the agent is actively updating tasks.
- **Age** — How long since the agent last did something, displayed as "just now," "1m ago," "5m ago," etc.

The status updates live with the card data and never triggers an extra request per card. Performance measurements show the chip does not make the board measurably slower.

<Aside type="tip">

Watch the status chip on board cards to see how your agents are progressing through tasks in real time.

</Aside>

## Agent reactions

<span class="label label--brand">New</span>. Agents can receive emoji reactions on their comments. A thumb-up on an agent's comment reaches that agent immediately as a signal of acknowledgment or approval.

When you respond with a reaction on an agent's comment (for example, ⬆️ or 👍), Hypertask sends that reaction to the targeted agent within seconds. The reaction appears on the task detail page and in the comment feed, and the agent receives the signal even if you're not both online.

Agent reactions work across all platforms: desktop, mobile, and through APIs. The reaction is persistent and visible when you return to the task later.

<Aside type="tip">

For security, reactions on agent comments stop counting toward flag-based triggers after the comment is edited.

</Aside>

## Agent notifications

<span class="label label--brand">Improved</span>. Agent notifications include mentions directed at agents (e.g., "Reply to @dev-bot"). These are handled with special guard-rules to prevent them from being incorrectly archived during snooze or reminder lookups. The system skips reminder validation when the notification is addressed to an agent, ensuring agent rows stay visible until you explicitly take action on them.

### Guest Hyper AI seeded notifications

Fresh guest inboxes now receive 4 seeded notifications from a Hyper AI agent. When available, the Important split is enabled, helping new users immediately experience AI-driven prioritization.

### Agent Connected and First Task email messages

<span class="label label--brand">Improved</span>. Agent notifications now use a shared onboarding email design for:

- **Your agent is connected** — Confirmation email when you sign up and connect an agent
- **Your first task** — Email when a task is assigned to your newly connected agent

These emails mirror your selected theme colors, typography, and layout tokens, so they match the look and feel of other in-boxed notifications. Subscribe to Agent notifications in your account settings or skip them entirely if you prefer list-only delivery.

## Clear refusals for invalid actions

<span class="label label--brand">Improved</span>. Agents that try to perform invalid or unauthorized actions now receive clear, early refusals instead of server errors.

For example, if an agent attempts to archive a Done task that cannot be archived, it receives a specific “not allowed” message rather than a generic [HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error](<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7231#section-6.6.1>) response. This makes debugging agent workflows easier and prevents unexpected crashes during bulk operations.

<Aside type="tip">

Check error messages from your agents when they're stuck—clear refusals point to permission issues, board and column permissions, or task storage states that limit what actions are available.

</Aside>

## Agent chat polling behavior

<span class="label label--brand">Improved</span>. Agent Chat now uses a simpler, direct method to check agent status instead of flag-driven polling. The previous feature flag for polling has been removed, and the system uses shorter, more consistent checks. Users experience reliable agent status updates without the hidden switch.

## Writing check

Agent comments and new tickets are refused when they use a dashed code name, quote Valentin in plain quote marks, ask a Question in the wrong shape, or leave out Problem, Fix, Done when, Risk, or Decision. People can still write those. Put a code name in the agent log. Put his words in a quote block. A Question starts with What this is, then at most three plain points, then Question, My recommendation, Why, Yes, and No, each on its own line.

## Agent governance

All agent activities are logged in the board's activity history. You can view who performed each action, when, and the tasks that were modified. This transparency helps teams audit agent workflows and resolve issues quickly.

# Agents Dashboard
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/agents-dashboard/

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

# Agents Dashboard

The **Agents Dashboard** gives you a central view of your agents, including summary statistics, per-agent details, and board-scoped dashboards.

## Access the Agents Dashboard

- **URL**: `https://app.hypertask.ai/agents`
- From any page, use `Cmd+K` (Mac), `Ctrl+K` (Windows/Linux) and search for **"Go to Agents"**.

## Agent list by status

The overview page (`/agents`) groups your agents into three top-level sections:

- **Running** — agents currently active and executing tasks.
- **Quiet** — agents not currently running, but ready to start.
- **Off** — agents paused or stopped.

Each group displays agent cards showing key information.

## Agent cards

Each agent card shows:

- **Agent name** — the agent identifier.
- **Status** — Running, Quiet, or Off.
- **On/Off toggle** — pause or resume the agent.
- **Heartbeat line** for the merge/unblock timer.
- **Avatar** — a generated robot icon for each agent.

### Heartbeat line

The heartbeat line visualizes the agent's 10-minute merge/unblock check:

- **Green dot, short bar** — timer ran within the last 15 minutes.
- **Amber dot, medium bar** — timer ran between 15–30 minutes ago.
- **Red dot, no bar** — timer missed its 10-minute window or no data available.

### Card outlines

A red outline signals a **blocked** agent — no one is actively working on it. This helps you spot bottlenecks at a glance.

### Blocked-summary widget

A blocked-summary widget shows the number of agents currently blocked, helping you prioritize follow-up work.

## Board-scoped agent pages

Each board has its own dedicated agent page showing the agents configured for that board:

- **URL format**: `https://app.hypertask.ai/agents/<board-number>`
- Example: Board 5500 is available at `https://app.hypertask.ai/agents/5500`.

The board page includes:

- Board-specific agent list.
- Toolkit bug totals, including AGTE tickets tagged as bug.
- Configuration source: board, repository, branch, and agent list read from a shared setup.
- Main merge counts or reference links for the board.

Use board pages to inspect board-level agent health and bug tracking per board.

## Per-agent availability

All agents show generated robot avatars from their detail pages and the dashboard. This provides visual recognition without relying on initials or external icons.

### Agent examples

| Agent | Status |
|---|---|
| Preview Bot | Running |
| QA Agent | Quiet |
| Scheduler | Off |

## Performance and reliability

Use the agents page to:

- Spot which agents are actively working.
- Pause or resume agents consuming resources.
- Monitor agent distribution across workflows.
- Identify blocked agents via red outlines and the blocked-summary widget.

## MCP client evaluation frame

When the MCP client eval is enabled, the agents page displays a table of 20 real Hypertask tasks run through the MCP server and CLI. Each row shows pass/fail, token in/out, wall time, and tool call count. This helps you compare MCP to the CLI and catch regressions.

## Working with pages and task detail pages

Agents can reference task detail pages (e.g., `/detail/project-15/<ticket>`) via the production verifier, enabling them to verify lifecycles and create links as part of workflows.

## Troubleshooting

<Aside type="note">

If you don't see an agent in the dashboard, check that:

1. The agent is connected to an active board.
2. The agent schedule has necessary permissions.
3. The agent is associated with your team or scope.

See [AI Agents](/features/agents/) and [Scheduling Agents](/mcp/scheduling/) for setup details.

</Aside>

---

# What AI chat can do
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/ai-chat-capabilities/

Ask a product question for a documentation-backed answer.
For example: “How do I connect an agent?”
The answer should include its source article.

## Choose your surface

| Surface | Available tools | What it can change | Boundaries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Board sidebar | Board, ticket, comment, inbox, page, skill, agent, and time tools | Accessible tickets, comments, labels, assignments, pages, and supported board settings | The selected scope limits board context. Opening chat grants no extra permissions. |
| Full-screen chat | The same built-in tools as the sidebar | The same supported changes as the sidebar | A chat's scope still matters. Switching screens grants no extra access. |
| Floating chat | The same built-in tools as the sidebar | The same supported changes as the sidebar | Floating changes presentation, not permissions or tools. |
| Phone chat | Built-in chat tools | The same supported board changes | Small screens can use different controls. Tools still enforce account permissions. |
| Connected MCP client | Tools returned by that connection's tool list | Actions allowed by its token and role | Read-only agents cannot write. Clients choose how they use tool guidance. |
| CLI | Commands listed by `hypertask --help` | Supported commands allowed by its login | The CLI runs commands, not an assistant. Its calling agent chooses what to run. |

Built-in chat supports skills and task relationships.
Its tools are not an identical MCP catalogue.
For connection details, see [MCP Integration](/mcp/overview/).
The [MCP Tools Reference](/api/tools-reference/) lists external tools.
The [CLI Reference](/cli/commands/) lists available commands.

## Ask about the product

Product questions use the help search tool first.
This includes plans, prices, limits, shortcuts, and setup.
Answers should be short, with relevant article links.
They should not reproduce entire articles.

An undocumented feature is “not documented”, not promised.
You can ask to file a clarification ticket.
A failed lookup does not prove feature absence.

Questions about your work use board tools instead.
Examples include “Find my overdue tickets” or “Summarize comments”.
Help search does not search your private tickets.

## Clickable ticket answers

Ask chat to find your tickets or list recent work.
Answers can include ticket rows beneath a short explanation.
Rows show the title, status, assignees, and priority.
Select a row to open its ticket.
Each group starts with up to five rows.
Select **+N more** to expand that group.
Reopening a conversation refreshes ticket details and permissions.
Tickets you can no longer access disappear.

## Limits

- Chat cannot access boards your login cannot access.
- Tool availability can vary by role and connection.
- A missing tool cannot perform the requested action.
- Chat should explain that limitation, without claiming success.
- Bulk changes can require your explicit confirmation.
- A link does not prove navigation or saving.
- Attachments depend on model and supported file handling.
- Uploading an image does not guarantee image understanding.
- Chat cannot see your screen beyond supplied context.
- Documentation can lag behind newly released changes.

For everyday examples, see [AI Features](/features/ai-features/).

# AI Features
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/ai-features/

For tools and limits, see [What AI chat can do](/features/ai-chat-capabilities/).

import { Aside, Card, CardGrid, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

AI is woven through every part of Hypertask — create tasks, filter your board, smart-label workloads, and manage daily operations without leaving the workflow you already use.

<Steps>

1. **AI-assisted task creation**
    - Click `AI` in the top-right corner of any board, open the `Ask Hypertask AI` panel, and describe a task in plain English.
    - AI parses the description and creates a task pre-assigned to you with a title, description, and relevant tags (task types, priorities, area).
    - Review the generated task before saving; edit fields or refine the prompt and generate again.

2. **Prompt-based filtering**
    - In the `Board Filter`, type natural-language constraints like:
        - `show me top-priority bugs`
        - `tasks assigned to Valentin and due this week`
    - Use combinations such as `high priority and not blocked`, and press `Enter` to apply.

3. **Smart labels**
    - Open a label (or the Manage Tags screen) and create a new label marked as a **smart label**.
    - In the "Smart label — AI keeps this label on matching tasks" field, define which tasks should carry it, for example:
        - `backend issue, involves DB, high impact`
    - Save; AI immediately classifies the board up to 500 existing tasks and adds the label to matches. Smart labels show a sparkle icon in label lists.
    - New tasks are classified when created; edited tasks are re-classified when title or description change; updating the prompt re-runs classification for the entire board.

4. **AI usage without a signed-in user**
    - AI usage can now be recorded and stored as usage tracks even when calls don't originate from a signed-in user.
    - This allows external agents or systems invoking the AI APIs to function without requiring active authentication, while still producing usage records available to admins.

5. **Batch-powered background workloads**
    - Background smart labels and other AI classification runs that involve many tasks are routed to Anthropic's Batch API at half price, allowing cost-efficient processing at scale.
    - Matching tasks receive their labels automatically; activity is logged in the task activity feed.
    - AI writes a compact representation of your content and sends it to the embed service, which can reject very long or empty text or refuse very long or empty text. On these failures, the upsert silently rotates the text and upserts without final vectors instead of failing, so comments and pages remain searchable with the relevant tags even when vectors aren't generated.
    - You don't see extra UI for this—it happens invisibly in the background with consistent results.

6. **AI Chat suggestions for tickets**
    - Open AI Chat in a ticket panel to get context-aware suggestions tailored to that ticket's specific information.
    - Previously, suggestions could be generic or fail entirely when the server returned "No output generated"; Haiku 5.5 now returns proper suggestions that match the ticket context.

7. **Faster agent task lists**
    - AI agents are now much quicker to load their task lists, especially after server warm-up.
    - Previously slow database reads that fetched task lists have been optimized: the slowest 5% of calls improved from ~129 ms down to ~40 ms. The improvement consistently benefits agents on both warm and cold servers, making AI-driven workflows feel far more responsive.

8. **AI Chat histories**
    - A spinner marks chats that are replying. The sidebar header and conversation list show it. Each chat keeps its own indicator. It disappears when replying finishes, fails, or stops.
    - Open AI Chat from the right rail or press `Ctrl/Cmd + I` to see a list of conversations.
    - In the full-screen chat view (desktop), the history list pages as the window resizes, and you scroll to load more older chats. Pick or filter from that list to open a chat.
    - On mobile, the list is limited; tap an entry to open its history.
    - The docked chat always shows your most recent chats inline; use the full-screen view for history navigation.
    - Your agents are listed in an **Agents** section at the top of the chat title list. Pick one to switch the chat to that agent's conversation in place. Its name shows in the chat title, and choosing it never sends a message.
    - You can also type `@` in the chat box. Agents are listed first, then boards and other items. Press `Enter` or click to add the agent as a chip and continue writing; nothing is sent until you press Send.
    - Drag the desktop chat edge to resize. Your account remembers this width in this browser.
    - Closing, reloading, and changing boards keep your choice. A narrow window temporarily reduces the displayed width. Widening restores your choice.

9. **Comment summaries preserve open questions**
    - When AI summarizes your comments, it now accurately reflects whether questions have been answered or remain unresolved.
    - Comment summaries display `Open: ...` for unanswered questions instead of inventing an answer, and retain "still unresolved" language when appropriate.

10. **Bulk archiving avoids server errors**
    - Agents that attempt to archive many tasks see a clear refusal message instead of a server crash.
    - An earlier incident had agents trying to archive 31 Done tickets per day, triggering a 500 error. The fix now returns a direct `not allowed` response, keeping workflows smooth and errors visible for observers.

</Steps>

## Run chats together

Start a reply, then open another chat. Each chat replies independently.
There is no two-chat limit. Existing usage limits still apply.

Follow-ups wait only for their own chat. They send in order, even while
you read another chat. Select **Stop** in a chat to stop that reply;
other chats keep running.

### Keep a conversation across tickets

Pin AI chat open in its menu, then open another ticket. Your selected conversation and earlier messages stay in the sidebar. New messages use the ticket you are viewing as context.

Select **New chat** to start a separate conversation. Creating a ticket with the task writer puts that ticket's own introduction in the conversation you have open; it never opens the chat for you.

## Image generation removed

Hypertask no longer generates new images.
Existing images and uploads remain unchanged.

Image generation is absent from team settings.
Check **Settings → Team → Default models** and **AI features**.
The **Ctrl+K** image generation shortcut was removed.
Image model mentions were also removed.

## Where AI appears

| Area | What AI does |
|------|--------------|
| **Task creation** | Parses your description into a task with title, description, priority, and tags. |
| **Board filtering** | Understands natural-language constraints and builds dynamic filters. |
| **Smart Labels** | Keeps labels on tasks that match your AI prompt; changes to tasks or the prompt trigger reclassification. |
| **AI Chat** | Global assistant for questions, summarization, and quick actions, with full-screen history paging. |
| **Ticket AI suggestions** | Provides context-specific suggestions in ticket panels that mirror the ticket's subject and related data. |
| **Bulk AI workloads** | Heavy classification runs use the Batch API to handle large boards efficiently; background jobs go through Anthropic's half-price Batch endpoint. Usage is recorded as usage tracks regardless of whether a signed-in user is present. |
| **Agent task lists** | Optimized reads for quick agent workloads; significant speedup for the slowest dataset slices. |
| **Task summaries** | Summarize the current task says what the task is first, then where it stands, then up to three open points. It does not open with a next action. |
| **Comment summaries** | Summarize comments and preserve whether questions remain open for human follow-up. |
| **Duplicate hint** | The Task Writer compares your note with up to eight similar tickets. When a similar ticket is clearly the same work, the draft opens with Looks like HTPR-123 may cover the same work. Otherwise the draft is unchanged, and teams on their own AI account are skipped. |

## When the chat opens and closes

The AI chat stays where you put it.

- It opens when you open it, and closes when you close it. Moving between tickets, boards, My Tasks and the inbox leaves it as it was.
- It keeps the same conversation while you move around a team. A new ticket no longer starts a new thread behind your back.
- Creating a task leaves it as it was too. A closed chat stays closed; an open one stays open.
- Reloading a tab keeps the state you left: open stays open, closed stays closed.

## Task creation with AI writer

<Steps>

1. **Open the New Task box** — Use <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd> on desktop or <kbd>Cmd+J</kbd> to open the New Task creator from boards, the inbox, or any view. On the Tasks page, click **New Task** in the toolbar.

   To change the destination, press <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+B</kbd> (or <kbd>Cmd+Shift+B</kbd> on Mac). The board picker lists recently visited boards first, then sorts ties alphabetically. It remembers board visits in this browser. Search for a board and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>, or click its name.

2. **Describe your task** — Enter a brief description of the work you need done. You can type directly or let AI expand your ideas. The model chip under the note shows the model that will write the task: click it to pick another model or effort level, or use **Reset to default** to go back to the board's default.

3. **Let AI write the task** — Reviews your inputs and generates a complete, structured task with a title, description, priority, and relevant tags. AI respects your board's templates and style when available.

4. **Review and refine** — Edit any field in the generated task. You can press <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> (desktop) or <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd> (Mac) in the description area to refine the AI's work, regenerate, or add more detail.

5. **Save the task** — When you're satisfied, click **Create** (or <kbd>Enter</kbd>) to save the task and add it to the board. The task appears immediately in the appropriate column or section.

6. **Answer the follow-up questions** — The new task opens with the AI chat sidebar next to it. Under **Questions and ideas for this ticket**, it shows up to three one-tap chips based on your original note and your board's rules, such as a next action to take, a job to split out, or an open decision to settle. Click one to send it in the same chat. When nothing fits, no chips appear.

</Steps>

### Creating tickets through AI Chat

Ask AI Chat to create a ticket. Its saved link appears before writing finishes.
Open it while its description is being written. The finished title, description,
priority and size follow. Saved title or description edits stop automatic replacement.
If writing fails, the saved ticket remains. Chat tells you its description is
unfinished. Finish that ticket instead of creating another.

### AI writer failure reasons

<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> When the AI writer fails to generate a task, the **Ctrl+J New Task** box and the AI Task Writer now show you the real reason for the failure instead of hiding it. Your note is still saved as a task, so you don't lose your work:

- **Error messages displayed** — Common errors like quota limits, missing context, or prompt format issues show explainable messages.
- **Task created anyway** — Your original description or note is preserved as a task, so you can retry AI later or edit it manually.
- **Applies everywhere** — This fix covers task creation from boards, the inbox, and when editing task descriptions.

If AI generation is not available (for example, your team has not configured an AI key), the text you entered appears without modification, keeping your workflow uninterrupted.

### AI Task Writer

The AI Task Writer is a prompt-based task creation flow that generates complete, shippable tickets from paste inputs.

### How it works today

The Task Writer uses the board's saved [custom instructions](/getting-started/settings-profile/#ai-settings) whenever you write a ticket with **Ctrl+J** compose, ask AI chat to **create a ticket**, or use the CLI/MCP task writer.

- **Board format** — Keeps the section layout shared by past tickets, such as Problem, Hypothesis, Control, Variation, and a scoring section, while keeping each section short.
- **Custom fields** — Fills the board's [Number, Select, Text, Date, and Checkbox fields](/features/custom-fields/) when the instructions or past tickets show what to use. For example, a score field can match the score in the title. Values that do not fit the field are skipped.

It also uses search to find related tickets instead of inventing them.

### Using the Task Writer

- From a board: **Ctrl+J** / <kbd>Cmd+J</kbd> and select **Create with AI** — **Task Writer**.
- From the command palette: **Ctrl+K** — search for "Task Write" and select it.
- From a task: Click the AI icon in the task header and select **Task Writer**.

After the Task Writer generates a draft, you can refine it just like any other AI-generated comment or description.

When Ctrl+J or AI chat writes a task description or comment that references an uploaded image or image link, the image appears inline in the text by default. Ask for "attachment only" or "link only" to keep it as an attachment or link instead.

## Included AI allowance

Free gets a small starter AI allowance on fast budget models. Pro includes more AI on managed models with no keys needed. BYOK uses your own model keys. Owners and board admins see percent used in **Settings > AI Usage**.

Background AI, including smart labels and summaries, counts toward the same allowance as interactive AI when it uses Hypertask's key.

Calls using [your own provider key](/features/byok/) do not use the included allowance.

<Aside type="note">
When the included allowance is reached, further calls on Hypertask's key are refused. Your own-key calls can continue.
</Aside>

Demo chat requires an active demo guest session. If prompted, start the demo again to keep chatting.

## When AI is not available

<span class="label label--brand">Behavior change</span> AI features now show clear guidance when a team does not have an AI key configured. Previously, teams without an AI key would see server errors when trying to use AI in agents or the CLI. Now, users receive a concise message directing them to add an AI key through the **Appearance & AI Models** settings page:

> "AI features require an AI key. Configure your AI key in Appearance & AI Models."

This applies to AI-powered task creation, filters, smart labels, and agent workflows that invoke AI.

## Settings

- Choose your preferred AI model in the **Appearance & AI Models** settings page. Different models may produce different responses.
- If a provider rejects your own AI key during chat, the message names that key and tells you to update it in **Settings**, then **AI**, then **Bring your own key**.
- Adjust leniency of AI-assisted task creation in the same settings area if you prefer more precise or broader suggestions.
- Smart label accuracy can be tuned by sharpening or relaxing your prompt; see the "How it stays current" details in the Smart Labels reference.

<Aside type="note">

Smart labels and prompts are a best-effort AI signal. They do not substitute for human review. Ensure your prompt manages edge cases or exceptions directly, for example: "NOT: schema changes on branches not yet merged."

</Aside>

<Aside type="tip">

Use smart labels together with filters and saved views to create reusable patterns for recurring workloads (e.g., `on-call issues`, `quick fillers`, `enterprise integrations`).

</Aside>

# AI Feedback from a Bot Account
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/ai-feedback-from-bot/

import { Card, CardGrid } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

In Hypertask, events such as failed-login activity can be surfaced through an AI Feedback bot account. This account does not represent your personal identity; instead, it serves as a neutral feedback channel that system notifications can write to.

<Aside type="note">
System-level alerts are no longer written directly to your account. Instead, they use the dedicated bot so clear separation exists between user workflow and event logging.
</Aside>

### What is the AI Feedback bot account?

- **Account:** [ai-feedback@crolab.org](mailto:ai-feedback@crolab.org)
- **Purpose:** File reports like failed-login activity for visibility in the team workspace.
- **Identity:** The account is labeled "AI Feedback". Nothing associated with failed-login events is written as your personal account name.

### Use cases

- **Incident logging:** Failed-login attempts can be recorded as structured reports without exposing user identity.
- **Observability:** Team leads and administrators can monitor security-related events through the bot channel without sifting through individual inboxes.

### How it works

When the server logs failed-login activity, the event is written through the AI Feedback bot. For clarity, users who experience a failed login are not notified about how the report appears; only that the report exists in the workspace. This design keeps user workflows uninterrupted while preserving the event log.

    Explore other AI-powered features like task creation, smart labels, and AI agents.
  </Card>

# Appearance & AI Models
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/appearance/

import { Aside, Card, CardGrid, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Appearance Settings

### Light and dark themes

Hypertask supports both light and dark themes, controlled from your profile or the Command Center.

- **Dark theme** â\x80\x94 reduces eye strain when working in low-light environments and is ideal for long coding sessions.
- **Light theme** â\x80\x94 provides high contrast for collaborative reviews and when sharing your screen.

You can toggle themes instantly from the settings menu. Preferences are saved per-user.

In AMOLED, floating AI chat has a thin outline and compact corners so it stays distinct from the black page, on desktop and phone. Other themes keep their existing appearance.

### Graphite 2

Choose **Graphite 2** in **Settings → Appearance**. Or open **Ctrl+K**, search **Graphite 2**, and press **Enter**.

Graphite 2 uses a quiet dark-grey palette, IBM Plex Sans, and Iconoir sidebar icons. Task titles use a lighter weight, while tags stay unfilled. Your choice survives a reload. **Dark · Graphite** and the other themes keep their existing appearance.

## Keyboard shortcuts

From the Command Center, use **Ctrl+K** to open the global command palette. While focusing on a task detail, you can also use:

- **Ctrl+O** â\x80\x94 Open links from the latest reply in a new tab (Agent Chat and board comments).
- **Alt+Left/Right** â\x80\x94 Navigate through tasks or agents in increasing or decreasing order.

These shortcuts are available across boards, chat panels, and the Agents overview.

<Aside type="tip">

Some shortcuts are also active in the main command palette when a compatible view is loaded.

</Aside>

## Text editor preferences

### Comments and descriptions

When composing comments or editing task descriptions, you can:

- Dictate **Ctrl+K**, **Ctrl+Space** (on supported browsers): Start voice dictation from the text field.
- Save **Ctrl+Enter**: Send the comment; the task may stay or advance depending on context.
- Open links **Ctrl+O**: When a reply includes a clickable link, open it in a new tab.

The comment composer is pinned to the bottom of task detail panels, keeping it accessible while you read and compose.

## AI models

### Model selection

Hypertask supports multiple AI providers and models. During configuration, agents operate with provider-specific model names. Agent Chat respects the engine configured on an agent:

- **Claude-based agents** use Claude models (for example, claude-sonnet-5).
- **Codex-based agents** use Codex models (for example, gpt-5.6-luna).

The chat lane configuration must align with the agent's engine.

<Aside type="note">

You do not need OpenRouter-specific keys in Hypertask; the runtime handles exchange of credentials and model mapping. If you plan to use OpenRouter lanes beyond the default provider, include OPENROUTER_GLM_API_KEY for squad-based workflows.

</Aside>

**Claude Haiku 5.5** is now Hypertask's default AI model for everyone, replacing Haiku 4.5. The new default is available across all plans, offering consistent model behavior for all users. When Haiku 5.5 is selected, it behaves equivalently to GPT 6 Luna in all supported surfaces including AI Task Writer, Agent Chat, and code-generation workflows.

Model quality now reflects real-world usage: Claude Haiku 5.5 cost per request is approximately 1.7× higher than GPT 6 Luna due to longer answer lengths, though the per-token price is identical. The model is fully operational on all supported environments, including Free and paid subscriptions.

<Aside type="tip">

Once the model is selected in your profile, the choice applies globally to any AI feature you use, keeping agent behavior and output style consistent across tasks, boards, and workspace contexts.

</Aside>

### Quiet mode

Quiet mode controls how agent activity appears in run activities and thread comments. It applies to agents in active runs:

- **Run activity** â\x80\x94 by default, agents write detailed progress chatter to the run activity tab. Quiet mode suppresses most run activity logs.
- **Thread comments** â\x80\x94 quiet mode disables comment generation. Comments are only posted for specific actions:
  - Question
  - Decision
  - Handoff
  - Done

When running in quiet mode, agents remain fully engaged, but their directional footprint in the task history is streamlined. To enable quiet mode, use the `quiet-run-activity` token or configure it via board-level agent settings.

<Aside type="tip">

Quiet mode is useful for workflow histories where you want to review agent behavior via structured run logs, but keep thread conversations focused on human decisions and actions.

</Aside>

## Icons, fonts, and visual tokens

### Sidebar icons

Icon visual standards are managed in the Typography & Sidebar Visuals page. Controlled strokes and consistent spacing ensure icons are legible across light and dark modes.

### Font scale

Typography uses a defined type scale for headlines, descriptions, and UI labels. Choose consistent weights and sizes from the standard set to maintain visual hierarchy.

### Component reuse checklist

When adding UI controls to the app, define the existing component being reused or provide a specific reason. This checklist applies to all UI pull requests and is enforced via the canonical guide and required gate. Each new control must be mapped to an underlying component or documented with a no-reuse justification.

<Aside type="note">

Requests that reference or implement reusable components should include a mapping for each control added. Reviewers use the checklist to verify reusability claims and avoid unnecessary component proliferation.

</Aside>
