# Billing & Seat Management
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/billing/

import { Card, CardGrid, TabItem, Tabs } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Hypertask billing controls license capacity, seat limits, and access tiers. Manage seats, track costs, and safely test billing changes in production without risking database side effects.

## Your billing label in Stripe

Stripe uses your team name as the display name on invoices and in the billing portal. Hypertask never shows internal IDs or the word "undefined". For customers without a team name in the app, the owner's email appears instead. Previously blank or malformatted names are now filled from the team name or owner email; customers that have neither team name nor matching owner remain blank.

> Verify customer names in your Stripe billing portal. If a name appears blank, check that its owning team has a name and that a matching owner email exists.

## Seats

Seats represent active users with individual access to Hypertask. Each seat corresponds to a user with login credentials and full access to the platform features.

**Seat limits by plan:**
- Free plan: Unlimited members and unlimited open tickets. You can own up to 3 boards. Archived boards are not counted. A paid or comped plan has no board limit.
- Paid and team plans: Active seat limits per plan
- Enterprise: Custom seat limits

When you create or add accounts, new seats are allocated automatically. Upgrading your paid plan increases your seat capacity; unrestricted reassignments are tracked for billing reconciliation.

## Cost forecasting

The cost forecast shows estimated consumption for GitHub repositories connected to Hypertask. This view helps you anticipate file storage and integration costs before they hit your budget.

**View your forecast:**
1. Go to the **Cost Forecast** page
2. See per-repository estimates broken down by usage type
3. Compare projections against your current subscriptions

## Testing billing changes safely

Stripe test-mode harness lets you safely test billing flows in production without risking database writes or production incidents.

The test harness:
- Runs **guarded seat billing logic** in a controlled environment
- Uses **in-memory application state** so tests don't affect live data
- Implements **bounded cleanup** to discard test states after execution
- **Never writes to the Hypertask database** during test runs

This means you can safely iterate on seat-loss logic, billing entitlement checks, and upgrade/downgrade flows in production-like conditions without creating cross-tenant leakage or corrupting live seats.

## Seat loss and automatic repair

Automatic repair of lost seats is available in production for affected teams. This feature prevents silent seat loss when users pool in from other teams, and helps maintain billing accuracy.

**How automatic repair works:**
- Detects when active teams have fewer seats than their current plan supports
- Verifies that the team has a valid Stripe payment method on file
- Requires billing-owner input if the active subscription cannot identify a single safe replacement Stripe item, to avoid modifying the wrong subscription item
- Blocks automatic repair and prompts for billing-owner review if:
  - A Stripe item is stored but no longer valid
  - The active subscription does not contain exactly one safe replacement at the stored price
  - Automatic selection could modify the wrong subscription item

Only teams with a payment method on file are eligible for automatic repair, and repair operations are guarded against unsafe mutations to subscriptions.

## License management

Seat allocation follows consistent rules across surfaces:

- New user creation adds a seat to your allocation
- Adding teammates in the app, via CLI, or through API all respect the same capacity checks
- Free plan members are unlimited
- Upgrading your plan increases your tracked capacity and adds seats automatically within the new tier bounds

## Team ownership verification

All billing-affected endpoints now verify team ownership server-side before performing mutations:

| Endpoint | Change |
|----------|--------|
| Checkout session creation | Verifies the authenticated user has billing access to the team before creating a checkout URL |
| Task mutations | Reads billing authority from the authenticated user and enforces access checks before state changes |
| Comment operations | Validates the requesting user's access to the target board and task before posting |

This prevents client-controlled parameter mismatches from bypassing authorization and ensures operations are scoped only to the intended team's resources.

## Stripe customer operations

Stripe customer creation for new accounts now surfaces all errors rather than silently swallowing them. Previously, certain paths returned null on failure without indicating the underlying issue, making debugging difficult. All customer creation paths now properly report errors to help you identify and resolve account or payment configuration problems.

# Board Settings
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/board-settings/

import { Aside, Card, CardGrid, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Use board settings to plan one board and control its automatic behavior. Set its target and milestones, post health updates, mute notifications, or configure archival, staleness, time tracking, and assignment rules.

## What this affects
Board settings apply to individual boards on a project. They govern default behaviors that are applied consistently across tasks when rules are triggered:
- **Archive actions** — Automatically archive old tasks or mark them for archival to keep your board clean.
- **Project planning** — Set a target date, track milestones, and post the board's current health.
- **Board notifications** — Mute ordinary inbox, email, and push notifications from this board only.
- **Staleness rules** — Automatically detect tasks that have been idle for a set period and take action.
- **Auto-assign rules** — Set per-column rules so new or unassigned tasks get attention where they belong.
- **Time totals** — Optionally show accumulated tracked time on task cards and in table view.
- **Synchronized IndexedDB defaults** — For authenticated Board and Table routes, the synchronized IndexedDB read model is now enabled by default to keep data in sync across opened tabs without manual refresh. You can still opt into the local model by using `<code>?local_db=0</code>` in the URL.

<Aside type="note">
Board settings are stored at the board level, so you can tailor behaviors per workflow. Changes here apply immediately; monitor the effect on your active tasks.
</Aside>

## Reach
You can open board settings from:
- **Ctrl+K command palette** — Search for **"Board settings"** and select your board. The board and team you opened from are now preselected.
- **Board menu** — Open a board's menu and choose **Settings**.

```markdown
<CardGrid>
<Card title="Auto-archive" icon="folder">
Clear expired backlog and automate housekeeping.
</Card>
<Card title="Staleness detection" icon="timer">
Identify tasks that haven't moved recently.
</Card>
<Card title="Auto-assign rules" icon="user">
Propagate responsibilities to unassigned cards.
</Card>
<Card title="Synchronized IndexedDB defaults" icon="database">
Keep data in sync across browsers by default for authenticated board and table routes.
</Card>
</CardGrid>
```

## Ticket prefix
Each board has a deterministic ticket prefix (e.g., HTPR, YPER4, HYFA). Owners can rename the prefix from board settings without changing existing ticket numbers. Prefixes are 2–5 letters or digits, unique within the team, and appear as live previews.

### How to change a prefix
From the app:
1. Open a board.
2. Click **Settings** > **Board** > **General**.
3. Find **Ticket prefix**.
4. Enter a new prefix (2–5 characters, letters or digits) and press Enter.
5. Old ticket IDs continue to resolve, so links, comments, and PRs that reference them stay accurate.

From the CLI:
```bash
hypertask project update --prefix NEWXY --project 15
```

The prefix is editable on the **Create board** screen (defaulted to the automatic suggestion) and available to agents via the same `project update --prefix` flag.

### Discovering ticket prefix settings
From the command palette, type **"ticket prefix"** to jump to this setting. The search returns **"Settings: Ticket prefix (board)"** for the current board. Use this to quickly locate the prefix configuration when you need to update it.

### Rationale
- **Instant updates:** The displayed ID is built from the board's current prefix and the ticket's number, so changing the prefix is a quick update instead of rewriting every ticket.
- **Backwards compatibility:** Old ticket IDs keep resolving via aliases, just like old numbers already do.
- **Avoid clashes:** Moved tickets take the next free number, so prefixes and numbers never conflict, even after deleting tickets or changing prefixes.

<Aside type="tip">
Prefixes are currently limited to these known values: HTPR, YPER4, and HYFA, which are used by existing agents. Changing those prefixes will require updating agent checks accordingly.
</Aside>

## Board notifications
Open **Settings → Board → General**, then turn **Board notifications** off to mute one board. The change applies immediately and persists across refreshes.

Muting a board stops its ordinary:
- Inbox notifications, including snoozed items returning later.
- Push notifications.
- Immediate and digest emails.
- Assignment, reaction, task-move, and due-date alerts.

Your global notification channel settings stay unchanged, and other boards continue notifying you. Direct replies from managed agents still appear in your inbox so an explicit agent request can return its answer.

Turn **Board notifications** on again whenever you want to resume delivery.

## Project planning
Open **Settings → Board → Planning** to keep the board's outcome and current health in one place.

- Set the board's **target date**.
- Add dated **milestones**, then mark them complete as the project advances.
- Post a short health update as **On track**, **At risk**, or **Off track**.
- Review the 20 most recent updates with their author and timestamp.

Any board member can read planning and post a health update. Only the board owner or an admin can change the target date or milestones.

Target and milestone changes save immediately. Press **Ctrl+Enter** or **Cmd+Enter** to post a health update from the message field.

## Auto-archive
Configure automatic archival of tasks that no longer require attention. Archive is different from deletion—it keeps history while removing items from the active view so you don't have to manually clean up stale columns.

### Available options
Rules you can set per board:
- **Enable auto-archive** — Turn the rule on/off.
- **Archive after** — Choose how many days tasks remain before archival.
  - Common presets: 90, 120, 180, 365.
- **Archive unused** — Automatically archive tasks that have not been touched recently (see Staleness).

### How it behaves
When a task crosses your configured threshold:
- The board removes the task from column counts.
- Tasks are moved to the board's Archive section.
- History (comments, attachments, subtasks) remains intact.

Tasks in any column are eligible: backlog, in-progress, review, and so on.

<Aside type="tip">
Use the **Archive after** setting on columns you keep as a long-running backlog. Combine with staleness for a two-layer cleanup rule.
</Aside>

## Set a column work limit

Use a work limit to spot crowded columns without blocking task moves.

1. Open the board and click a column title.
2. In **Manage board columns**, open that column's settings.
3. Enter a positive whole number in **Work limit**.
4. Leave the field to save the limit.

The column count shows active tasks / limit and turns red above the limit.
The count includes active tasks hidden by filters. Archived and deleted tasks do not count.
You can still create and move tasks when the column is over its limit.
Clear **Work limit** to remove the limit. The limit belongs to the column, so saved views share it.

## Staleness detection
Staleness rules keep track of active tasks that have not been moved, updated, or interacted with in a defined window. This helps surface forgotten items that might need re-evaluation or removal.

Configuration:
- **Stale after** — Number of days since the last change/due date.
  - Suggested ranges: 30, 60, 90.
- **Auto-assign stale tasks** (Optional) — Toggle the rule that moves or re-assigns stale tasks to a specific column or assignee.
- **Stale reminders** (Optional) — Get notified when tasks reach the staleness threshold so you can prioritize review or cleanup.

When staleness is enabled, Kanban cards show the task's age on the board before its age in the current column. Fresh cards show muted ages. Cards become amber at the warning threshold and red at the hot threshold. Use Ctrl+K to toggle staleness for the board or the current view.

### Filtering stale vs healthy
Every staleness filter is named so that typing **stale** in the filter menu finds all of them:
- **Stale in column** — days since the task last changed column, falling back to its creation date if it has never moved.
- **Stale without comment** — days since the last comment, falling back to creation if nobody has ever commented.
- **Stale on board** — days since the task was created, regardless of activity (not affected by column moves or comments).
- **Not stale** — the inverse: both the column age and the comment age are under the warn threshold. This deliberately ignores board age: a long-lived task that is still being moved and discussed is not stale.

All four filters apply the per-board staleness threshold automatically, so a filtered board always agrees with the ages shown on the cards.

<Aside type="caution">
Staleness only accounts for updates to the task record. Activities like commenting or toggling status updates the last-touch date automatically.
</Aside>

## Auto-assign rules
Define rules that automatically assign or re-assign tasks to specific members. This is useful for ensuring that new pull requests, backlog items, or triage items land with the right people without manual overhead.

### Per-column auto-assign on column move
In addition to setting a default for the entire board when a task is created or is unassigned, you can configure a per-column auto-assign rule: whenever a task is moved into this column, it will be assigned to the specified person or group. Ctrl+K "Auto-assign for this column" opens the per-column configuration.

To configure per-column auto-assign:
1. From the board or section header, open the context menu (or use Ctrl+K "Auto-assign for this column") and select the section where you want the rule.
2. Pick an assignee (group or individual) to apply as tasks are moved into that column. The assignment is additive and idempotent—moving a task back into another column and then into this column again respects the rule.
3. When the rule applies, all tenants receive a notification and the assignee is messaged in the source channel if notifications are set up for the board.

Auto-assign runs within the effective membership and session context enforced for board write access. Use board-visibility gating to control which users gain or retain write access to the board; ID-based attempts outside that context are scoped to the session owner's permissions.

### Calling auto-assign via CLI/MCP
When auto-assign is triggered by CLI or MCP tools, the assignee lookup is evaluated in the context of the authenticated user or tool's session. Actions cannot be authorized by leases or background jobs outside that session; approvals are enforced through the board's membership and write-access model.

### How to configure (defaults)
- **Target columns** — Specify which columns should apply auto-assign triggers:
  - Any column that can receive tasks (e.g., In Progress, Review).
- **Assign to** — Select a project member or a role-based assignment:
  - Individual users.
  - Groups (e.g., "Testers," "Backend team").
- **Optional priority filter** — Apply only to tasks with certain priority levels (e.g., Urgent, High).

### Scenarios
- **Backlog channel** — Assign new backlog items to reviewers or maintainers.
- **Review overload** — Auto-assign completed items to QA reviewers when they become "In Review".
- **Slack alerts** — Combine with board notifications to alert assignees when auto-assign runs.

<Aside type="tip">
Pair auto-assign rules with open notifications (e.g., open issue in Slack team) to ensure assignees know their attention is needed without just silently moving cards.
</Aside>

## Autosave drafts
Changes to board settings are saved automatically. If you navigate away or refresh the page, your settings persist:
- **No manual save needed** — All toggles, number inputs, and column mappings are applied instantly.
- **Revert behavior** — If you make a mistake, the board defaults (detected from project/staleness rules) can be used as a backup; update the offending rule and save again.

## Logging and history
Hypertask tracks rule executions at the board level for review:
- **Rule runs** — Historically, Hypertask logged rule runs to a log table (Admin role visible).
- **Rule hygiene** — To keep logs manageable, Hypertask retains only recent rule executions (e.g., last 14–30 days) on the log table, while preserving a full backup in a more extensive repository for administrative use.

<Aside type="note">
Hygiene protects performance and schema stability over time. Project owners should rely on boards and historiques for governance rather than logs after a few days.
</Aside>

## Synced IndexedDB defaults
You can choose between two read models for Boards and Tables:
- **Synchronized IndexedDB (default)** — Active when no `<code>?local_db=0</code>` in the URL. Keeps data in sync across opened tabs and browsers smoothly, at the cost of higher CPU and a small memory overhead. Use this if you regularly open the same board in multiple tabs or devices.
- **Local IndexedDB (optional)** — Activated by appending `<code>?local_db=0</code>` to the URL. Reads and writes stay in the local browser state, giving high performance with less CPU and a smaller footprint. Data may not reflect changes from other tabs or browsers until you reload.

This defaults to the synchronized model for authenticated Board and Table routes. The system preserves the opt-out via URL flags, so local flow can still be opted into for testing or performance-sensitive workflows.

## Auto-error routing targeting Bugs
When auto-error tickets are routed to sections, Hypertask now targets the exact Bugs section by default instead of the board's default column. This applies globally for boards with a specific Bugs section. Boards without a clearly defined Bugs section fall back to the current default section behavior. Changes take effect after board settings are saved.

<Aside type="tip">
If you see Bugs incorrectly routed to another section, double-check that the Bugs section exists with a unique name and that you're using the latest board settings cache after this release.
</Aside>

# Board & Subtask Visibility
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/board-visibility/

import { Aside, Tabs, TabItem, Steps, Card, CardGrid, Table, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Every board has a **Visibility** setting that controls which task and subtask encodings are exposed. This setting is applied consistently across all surfaces where a board is viewed or acted upon and can be overridden in the **Board hierarchy**.

## Board visibility modes

A board's top-level setting is configured from the board's header, using **Ctrl+K** → "Edit board visibility" (or via the context menu). The available modes are:

| Mode               | Description                                                | Conflicts with inherited |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| **Visible**        | All task and subtask fields are shown.                     | No                       |
| **Basic**          | Only the `title` and `description` of tasks are shown.     | Partial (core fields may still be inherited) |
| **Dimmed**         | Visibility applies to the owning team only (BYOK & free teams are effectively Hidden). | No (inherits from parent if permitted) |
| **Hidden**         | Layout shows only the owning team; other teams see an empty placeholder. | Only the owning team |

## Saved-view access control

<span class="label label--brand">Security fix</span> Saved-view endpoints now respect board membership data. Before requests are processed, Hypertask validates whether a user has access to the board that owns the saved view:

- **Block access** – requests from users not on the board (including through chat API and MCP) are met with a `404 Not Found` result.
- **Reject unauthorized reuse** – callers cannot rename, delete, or switch to saved views on boards they cannot access.
- **Preserve their own data** – your own board still lists its saved views, exactly as before.

This change ensures saved-view endpoints are scoped strictly, preventing cross-board data leakage through saved-view references or AI‑assisted view actions.

## Profile details in board detail answers

<span class="label label--brand">Security fix</span> Board detail answers now safely expose profile information. Before this fix, a board detail answer would show every profile field of the board owner and task assignees, including private details. After this fix:

- **Private profile visibility** – Board members no longer see private profile details of the board owner or assignees.
- **Limited exposure** – The old board detail answer now shows each person with only their `id`, `name`, and `photo`.
- **Consistent behavior** – This applies to API responses that include profile details for tasks and owners, so public references (links, summaries, and views) respect the same privacy boundaries.

### Why this matters

- Boards with strict visibility settings can share detail previews without leaking sensitive profile data.
- Agents and MCP tools that query board details show profile data consistent with visible vs. hidden modes.
- Saved-view and AI-chat integrations that render profiles stay within the same privacy model as other board filtering.

## Board access for reads

<span class="label label--brand">Security fix</span> Hypertask now properly restricts board-visible resources (tasks, pages, tables, and column names/settings) to users who have access to the board. Standard tasks, tables, and pages show only work that belongs to boards you are a member of. Before this fix:

- **Page access leak** – a page would keep its old-board access even after its task moved to another board, so users without access to the new board could still open and search the page.
- **Column visibility leak** – any logged-in user could read another board’s column names and settings, including through search filters and tables.
- **Cross-board exhaust** – a board member could search across all boards and open test pages, exposing additional columns and configuration.

After the fix:

- **Moving a task moves its pages** – when you move a task to another board, its pages are now restricted to users with access to that board. Users who cannot see the new board cannot open or search the page.
- **Columns are board-scoped** – columns and their associated layout/filter settings from boards you're not on are hidden. Only your boards contribute to search results and table columns.
- **Search is scoped properly** – global search, filtered tables, and the search screen only return content you have board access to; cross-board data is filtered out at the backend.

### Why board-aware access matters

- **Prevents unauthorized access** across unrelated workspaces at a single login.
- **Aligns searches and tables** with your effective board memberships.
- **Keeps pages in context** – pages follow their task and stay visible only to the people who can see the new board.

## Board access for writes

All write paths consistently enforce membership-based access before mutating targets. Members cannot bypass access checks by switching identities or relying on CLI/MCP identities different from the session owner. This applies across CLI task and comment mutations (e.g., `task create`, `task update`, `comment add`), MCP task/comment tools (`board_update_task`, `board_add_comment`, `legacy_comment`), and the REST API (`board_update_task`, `board_add_comment`, and the legacy comment endpoint `/api/board/comment`). Write actions are now strictly tied to the authenticated user's session and the board's membership settings; no identity swap creates a separate write context.

### Why write gating matters

- Matching access semantics between reads and writes prevents accidental cross-board updates.
- Boards with constrained visibility (Basic, Dimmed) can rely on a stable access model even when multiple identities are involved.
- CLI, MCP, and REST workflows stay aligned: no identity switch or hidden flag can bypass board membership checks.
- Auto-assign and auto-archive operations are restricted to the effective membership context; claims or leases cannot authorize actions outside the session owner's permissions.

You can read more about access control for downloads in the [Images and Attachments](/features/images/) documentation, which documents that files are only reachable for people who see the parent ticket.

## Rail and sidebar behavior

When you disable the **Rail** (sidebar) in Appearance settings, the following applies:

- **Rendering**: On client-side hydration, the rail is immediately hidden. Before hydration completes, an early SSR pass may briefly render it alongside the main view.
- **User-visible fix**: Rail-off users no longer see this flash during page load. After the initial SSR render is removed under strict hydration guards, the UI stabilizes without the rail ever being visible.
- **Consistency**: The rail-off state is enforced across all pages and views, ensuring a clean workspace for users who prefer a focused, rail-free app surface.

---

## Why use visibility modes?

- **Free and BYOK users** set a board to **Dimmed** so only the owning team sees its tasks. People on other teams see placeholders. Invitees join as an Admin or a Member.
- **Boards that are shared externally** may set visibility to **Basic** to limit detailed data that isn't relevant to external collaborators.
- **Bot agents and scheduled MCP pipelines** may use **Disabled** subtask visibility in saved views to reduce payload size and operational noise.
- **Kanban vs table layout compatibility**—low-detail modes ensure consistent views regardless of whether you are looking at cards or a table, without changing board-level visibility.

---

## Keyboard shortcuts

From a board's header:

- **Ctrl+K** → **Edit board visibility** (opens a context menu with the four board modes)
- **Ctrl+K** → **Save view** (creates or updates a saved view with any displaySubtasks mode)

From any board or task list:

- **Ctrl+S** (on a view) → **Save as view** (opens a dialog; includes a **Display subtasks** toggle)
