# Boards & Sections
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/boards/

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

<aside>
The shipping gate for this page was on 2026-10-03 (Owner+QA preview only). Bottom board/Calendar/Inbox/AI/Search dock is initially hidden on ticket pages on mobile under flags like <strong>htpr-6860-mobile-page-hide-dock</strong>. Other screens keep the dock; leave a ticket page via <strong>Back to task</strong>.
</aside>

## Board access, invites, and permissions

### Board invites and access
<span class="label label--brand">Security fix</span> Sharing access to a board now respects team boundaries. A board invite:

- Only adds the signed-in person to the board that generated the invite.
- Is refused when no login is provided.
- Is refused if the invite target board differs from the invite source board.
- Can only be resended by the board's owner and current members.

**Behavior before this fix:** An invite could be successfully resent and used to create tickets on a different board, potentially exposing cross-team data.**\\n\\n**After this fix:** Each board's access is gated strictly. Invites can only be resent and used within their intended context. Users outside the board's membership cannot leverage invites to access or create tickets on other boards.

This change ensures invites are a scoped, safe method to grant board-level access without exposing cross-team boundaries.

### Adding columns and sections
<span class="label label--brand">Security fix</span> Adding columns to a board is now restricted to board members only. A signed-in person who is not a member of the board's membership will be refused when attempting to add a column.

**Behavior before this fix:** An unauthorized user could add columns to a board they were not part of, potentially affecting multiple team areas.**\\n\\n**After this fix:** Only board members (including board owners, members, and invited participants with valid access) can add columns. This restriction aligns with the board-wide access model and ensures that board structure changes are controlled within the intended team context.

### "Board unavailable" error screen handling
<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> The "Return to previous board" button now safely handles the "This board or ticket is unavailable" error screen.

**Before this fix:** Clicking the "Return to previous board" button while encountering an unavailable board would trigger an immediate server request that caused the browser to crash.**\\n\\n**After this fix:** The button gracefully handles the unavailable state without crashing. Users can safely return to their previous board or navigate to another area of Hypertask without encountering errors.

## Creating a board

## Quick add with N

Use quick add when you only need a task title. It works in both board and table views.

1. Open your board and point at the column where you want to add work. Focus a column or select a task in it if you prefer.
2. Press **N**. A small title box opens in the column under your pointer. Move the pointer off the board and it uses the focused column, then the selected task's column, then the first column. In table view, it uses the selected row's section or the first section.
3. Type a title and press **Enter** to create the task.
4. Press **Escape** to close the box without creating another task.

You can also open quick add with a column's **+** button. Press **C** to open the full task editor instead. **Shift+C** no longer opens quick add.

The shortcuts do not run while you are typing in a field or while a dialog or command palette is open.
## Select cards on your phone

On a phone, hold a card for about a second and let go without moving your finger. The card gets a tick and the selection bar opens at the bottom, with archive, assign, labels, move and more actions.

- While cards are selected, tap another card to add it, or tap a ticked card to remove it.
- Hold a card and drag it to move it, as before. Dragging never selects a card.
- When no card is selected, a tap opens the card as usual.

## Archive every ticket in one column

1. Open your board, then open Commands (**Ctrl+K**).
2. Choose **Archive all tickets in a column**.
3. Pick a column. Check its exact ticket count.
4. Choose **Archive tickets**, or **Cancel**.

The count includes tickets hidden by view filters.
Other columns stay unchanged. Nothing is permanently deleted.
Tickets moved since confirmation stay unchanged, too.
Individual refusals do not stop the other tickets.
Use the result's **Undo** to restore successful archives.

## Find tickets waiting on you

Every board includes **Blocked by me**. Open the view from the board's view
tabs on desktop, or the view picker on your phone.

The view shows tickets where you are marked as the blocker. Tickets blocked
by someone else, tickets without a blocker, and task dependencies alone stay
out. Clearing or changing the blocker updates the view. Each person sees
their own tickets, so there is no filter to create or save.

## Mark the comment that explains a block

A ticket can name the person who blocks it, and one comment can carry the
reason. That comment is the blocker comment.

1. Hover the comment, then click the **More** button (three dots) that appears at its right end. The command menu opens for that comment.
2. Choose **Mark as blocker**.
3. The comment gets a red frame. Choose **Unmark as blocker** to take it away.

Only a real comment can carry the frame; activity rows cannot. One ticket has
at most one blocker comment. Marking a second comment moves the frame.

Agents use the same marker from the command line. The blocker comment and the
blocking person are separate, so one can be set without the other:

```bash
hypertask task blocker-comment HTPR-123 --comment-id 456
hypertask task waiting-on HTPR-123 --user 6
```

An agent that clears a blocker records why it did, so the ticket keeps a note
of who cleared it.

## Find tickets created by an agent

1. Open your board's filters with **Shift+F**.
2. Choose **Created by**, then an agent.
3. Save the view to keep this filter.

Only tickets created by that agent appear.
Choosing a person excludes their agents' tickets.
Combine filters using **Match ANY** or **Match ALL**.
This also works in the board's table layout.
Calendar and My Tasks keep existing creator choices.

# Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/byok/

import { Aside, Card, CardGrid } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

BYOK lets you bring your own API keys and providers directly into Hypertask. Add keys from providers like Vercel, add custom endpoints, and manage provider keys across your workspace.

## Add a Provider Key

Add a key from any supported provider directly in your workspace:

1. Open the **Board** menu (···K or click the board icon)
2. Select **Board settings** or go to **Settings > Keys & providers**
3. Click **Add provider** and choose from the available options, or paste a provider URL for custom endpoints

## Supported Providers

Hypertask supports the following provider types:

- **Vercel** — Gateway keys for deployments and integrations
- **GitHub** — Token-based authentication for repository access
- **Custom endpoints** — Self-hosted or third-party services via HTTPS

<Aside type="note">
Provider access is tied to your project-level permissions. Only owners and admins can add or remove keys for a project.
</Aside>

## Provider interchangeability

Agents can use interchangeable provider implementations for AI operations. The current overriding provider must be defined per-run by specifying an absolute provider URL. This may be a built-in (e.g., https://claude.com or https://codex.com) or a custom endpoint. Valid URLs are validated on input and persisted where applicable.

After providing a URL and verifying it, the provider becomes active for that run. Agent workflows using MCP tools or external schedulers can reference this provider URL to guarantee consistent model selection and access control across runs—no manual command-line environment variable overwrite is required when a provider URL is configured.

## GDPR-safe mode

Enable GDPR-safe mode to remove all China-hosted providers from your configuration across the platform. This toggle removes providers from settings and selectors and rejects BYOK keys that list China-hosted endpoints. The setting applies globally to your team workspace and persists across devices.

### How GDPR-safe mode works

When you enable GDPR-safe mode:

- **China-hosted providers are rejected:** Keys and custom endpoints pointing to providers hosted in China (e.g., Alibaba Cloud regions, Tencent Cloud regions) are removed from your saved configuration and cannot be used.
- **Settings and selectors are cleaned:** China-hosted entries are removed from settings, preference selectors, and validation flows.
- **BYOK validation:** By adding a new key with a China-hosted endpoint, the validation endpoint rejects it and surfaces a clear error.
- **System-wide impact:** Features like Gateway fallback and backend latency optimization climb back to non-China endpoints when available.

### Enabling GDPR-safe mode

To enable, go to **Settings > Privacy** and toggle **GDPR-safe mode** on. The change takes effect immediately and persists for your team.

<Aside type="tip">
GDPR-safe mode does not affect regions outside of China. It specifically targets providers and endpoints hosted within mainland China.
</Aside>

## Managing Your Keys

After adding a key, each provider row displays:

| Control | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Test button** | Verify the key works with the provider before saving |
| **Edit** | Update key details or change provider configuration |
| **Remove** | Delete the key (requires confirmation) |

### Test Provider Keys

Use the **Test button** next to any provider key to verify connectivity and authentication:

1. Click **Test** on the provider row
2. The system sends a quick validation request to confirm access
3. View the result—**success** confirms the key works, **error** shows configuration issues

Re-test after changing keys, switching domains, or updating provider credentials.

## Vercel Gateway Keys

Add Vercel gateway keys for deployments, edge functions, and related services:

1. Select **Vercel** from the provider list in Settings
2. Paste your Vercel **Personal Access Token** or specific project token
3. Click **Test** to verify the key's scopes
4. Save to add the key to your provider configuration

Vercel keys function similar to other provider keys—they're used for API access and integration with Vercel-powered features.

## Custom Endpoints

Bring key-based providers or self-hosted services into Hypertask by adding a custom endpoint:

1. Choose **Custom endpoint** as the provider type
2. Enter the endpoint URL (HTTPS only)
3. Provide any required headers, API keys, or bearer tokens
4. Click **Test** to confirm the endpoint is accessible
5. Save the configuration for reuse across your projects

Custom endpoints are stored securely and tied to your account and project access levels.

## Ephemeral per-turn provider home

During agent agent runs that connect to a provider home, each turn creates an ephemeral directory for that turn. The provider home is scoped to the current turn and doesn't persist across turns. Before each turn starts:

- Every path in the provider home is scanned
- Paths matching the resumable allowlist are preserved (these are expected, safe files such as state resumed from a previous turn)
- All other paths are deleted immediately (including any provider-created cache files that may have been written to the home)

By wiping the provider home outside the allowlist at run start, Hypertask ensures that stale cache files and provider-specific junk do not accumulate. Provider favorites that need to be preserved for resume already belong to the resumable allowlist; other files are cleared out to keep the environment clean.

This behavior aligns with how you'd set up a provider home manually on your system: prepare the directory for a specific run and clean up loose files afterwards, without keeping things around across unrelated work.

<Aside type="tip">
If you see unexpected cache files being cleaned up, check the resumable allowlist—anything else in the provider home that is not explicitly expected for resume will be removed at each run start.
</Aside>

## Key Security and Access

BYOK keys in Hypertask are managed with these principles:

- **Server-side storage** — Keys are stored on Hypertask infrastructure and never exposed to third-party providers beyond what's needed for authentication
- **Per-project scoping** — Providers and keys are tied to specific projects, limiting cross-project key sharing
- **Access controls** — Only owners and admins can view, add, or remove provider keys
- **No cross-board leakage** — Keys from one project/board are not visible or accessible from another

<Aside type="caution">
Never share keys between projects. If a team needs access to a provider key, have an admin add it directly rather than copying the token across accounts.
</Aside>

## Using Provider Keys

Once configured, provider keys are used automatically:

- **AI agents** — Available when making provider-specific API calls
- **Workflows** — Integrated into agent runs that require provider authentication
- **CLI tools** — References provider keys from your account when making authenticated requests

You don't need to manually invoke provider keys. They're selected automatically based on your current context and permissions.

<p>Stakeholders — please review and reply with corrections or missing context.</p>

# Calendar
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/calendar/

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The calendar at `/calendar` shows every task with a due date across your boards. Filter which boards and people are included from the boards panel, and save any combination as a reusable view.

<Aside type="tip">

You can enshrine your preferred weekday start and weekend visibility by saving a preset, or rely on the default behavior for a fresh calendar.

</Aside>

## Default behavior

When you open a calendar without a saved preference:

- **Week starts on Monday** (Day and Week views show Monday through Friday; weekends are not shown). If you prefer Sunday as the starting day or want to show weekend rows, change your preference in Settings.
- **Weekend days are hidden in Week view** (you still see Monday through Friday). If you prefer to see the full week including Saturday and Sunday, adjust your preference in Settings.

To change your default weekday start or weekend visibility, go to Settings and set your preferred options. Controls are surfaced via <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> commands (if configured).

## Managing calendar views

Default views include Day, Week, Month, My Tasks, Overdue, Blocked, and Agents. All default views are ordinary orderable views: you can drag them anywhere in the view cluster, including up to an earlier row. You can also show each default view in Manage views (drag + hide) and reorder it alongside saved custom views.

From **Manage calendar views**, you can rename any calendar view that you own. Owned views show a settings affordance that lets you edit the name. Teammate-owned views are locked and cannot be renamed. The modal includes a clear close/back control for safe, deliberate switching between saved and owned views.

## Views

Switch views from the dropdown at the top left (or press <kbd>W</kbd> for week, <kbd>M</kbd> for month):

- **Day**: full-width table layout with tasks as rows. Use <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>D</kbd> to switch to day view. On desktop, Day view now includes a weekday-selector strip above the calendar. To jump to a specific weekday, click any weekday label in the strip. Keyboards actions <kbd>U</kbd> and <kbd>I</kbd> move to previous/next day; <kbd>T</kbd> jumps to today; <kbd>Tab</kbd> and <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> move focus; <kbd>Shift</kbd>+arrows reschedule the focused task.
- **Week**: five columns with hidden weekends (by default), or seven columns if you show weekends.
- **Month**: the classic grid.

## Shareable links

The calendar URL always encodes what you are looking at:

```
https://app.hypertask.ai/calendar?view=day&date=2026-07-31
```

- `view` is `day`, `week`, or `month`.
- `date` is the anchor day in `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Copy a link at any time to share exactly the same view and date. Open a shared link to land on that day's specific view, regardless of the recipient's own last-used calendar state. Links with invalid dates fall back to the recipient's own calendar.

For agents: construct these URLs directly when pointing a person at a specific day or week, e.g. `https://app.hypertask.ai/calendar?view=week&date=2026-08-03`.

## Week strip month expander

In the Week view, a month expander lets you quickly jump to any month. When you change days or weeks using arrows or navigation controls, the picker now stays in sync with your current view instead of remembering the month it opened with.

## Rendering reliability

The calendar renders reliably in production even when a persisted user state is null. Server-side identity-dependent calendar filters use the validated account ID passed from the server boundary, preventing SSR crashes on boards with missing user configurations.

## Legacy image support

If your board has historical images stored with an old S3 host configuration, the calendar no longer crashes when loading those images. Hypertask now accepts legacy bucket hosts in `next.config` remotePatterns, so old images load without bringing down the entire page. Requesting an official image migration, which will rewrite stored URLs to `files.hypertask.app`, remains a separate data cleanup effort. The calendar now works smoothly even when some images are still on an old host.

## Blocked tasks

Blocked tasks now stand out in Calendar. Month, week, and day views show the same red left edge as the board, making it easy to spot bottlenecks at a glance without switching to your board view.

On mobile agenda cards, blocked tasks now show the person blocking them with a red chip. This chip appears on both blocked and unblocked calendar agenda rows, so you can always see who's holding up work at a glance.

---

# AI Chat Board Filter
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/chat-board-filter/

import { Aside, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Use the board filter in AI Chat to quickly focus on chats from one board, or view all chats across your boards. Set a default to start side by side.

## Docked AI chat scope

Use the scope menu in the docked AI chat to choose what the conversation is about:

- **Current board** — the default scope; focuses on the board you are viewing.
- **Current ticket** — available on a ticket page; focuses on that ticket's title, description, and comments. The scope stays on **Current board** until you choose **Current ticket**, and switches back to **Current board** when you leave the ticket.
- **Pinned boards** — choose a pinned board as the scope.
- **All boards** — includes all your accessible boards.

**Current ticket** is only available in the docked chat on a ticket page. The full-screen chat page is unchanged.

## When AI chat opens

The docked AI chat no longer opens by itself. It opens when you open it, and it stays where you left it as you move between tickets, boards, My Tasks and the inbox, on desktop and on your phone.

A closed chat stays closed when you create a task; an open one stays open. If you close it, a reload keeps it closed, and a tab where you left it open keeps it open.

**Settings > General > Task Page** no longer offers the three auto-open switches, because nothing opens on its own. The older **Keep AI chat closed always** and **Open AI chat by default** choices are gone with them.

## Board filter behavior

- **All boards** — shows every chat across all your accessible boards.
- **One board** — shows only chats from that board.
- Default is **All boards**, so all your chats appear by default when you open the chat.

<Aside type="tip">
Run /chat or switch to the Chat view to start a conversation. Then use the board filter above the chat list to switch between "All boards" and a specific board.
</Aside>

## Agent Chat sidebar status

When you open an agent chat with an agent that supports status visibility, the chat sidebar displays real-time per-agent status instead of a static green dot.

### Available status indicators

- **Active** — the agent is currently processing a task or message.
- **Idle** — the agent is idle but available, with an optional duration indicating how long it has been idle.
- **Idle with duration** — same as Idle, but explicitly shows the elapsed time (in minutes) since the last activity.
- **Out of tokens** — the agent has exhausted its token budget and cannot process further requests until refreshed.
- **Inactive** — the agent has been turned off or has no recent activity; it is not responding.

### How status changes are shown

- The status is computed server-side at request time and shown as text immediately next to the agent name.
- Changing from one status to another updates in real time without needing to refresh the page.
- If an agent is explicitly turned off, it always shows Inactive until you restore the agent or the chat session closes.

## Agent Chat auto-scroll behavior

Agent Chat automatically scrolls to the most recent messages as new content arrives, including queued and typing indicators, so you never miss updates during active conversations.

### Scrolling behavior

- When you are already at the bottom of the chat list and new messages arrive or queued statuses appear, the window follows them.
- If you scroll up to view earlier messages and new messages arrive, the scroll position stays where you left it until you scroll back down.
- When a new message appears while at the bottom, Chat immediately follows to keep the latest message in view.

<Aside type="tip">
This behavior applies across all supported channels and helps you stay aligned with agent progress without manually paging through the thread.
</Aside>

# Collaboration
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/collaboration/

import { Aside, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Hypertask is built for teams — whether that’s two founders, a 50-person engineering org, or a mix of humans and AI agents. Every feature is designed around the idea that project management is inherently collaborative.

## Team workspaces
Workspaces are the top-level container in Hypertask. Each workspace groups related projects together and manages team membership.

A workspace might represent your company, a department, or a client engagement. You can belong to multiple workspaces.

## Project members
### Inviting people
Invite team members to a project by generating an **invite link**. Invite links support several controls:

| Setting | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Expiration** | Set when the link stops working (e.g. 7 days, 30 days, never) |
| **Usage limit** | Cap how many people can join via this link |
| **Domain restriction** | Limit invites to specific email domains (e.g. `@yourcompany.com`) |

<aside type="tip">
Domain restrictions are useful when you want to share an invite link broadly (in Slack, for example) but limit access to people within your organization.
</aside>

### Roles and access

A board has an owner. The owner can set each other person to **Admin** or **Member**. Those are the only two roles you can assign, and the owner’s own role cannot be changed.

There is no Viewer role and no read-only role. Someone who only needs to look at a board still joins as an Admin or a Member.

Manage the people on a board in **Settings > Board > Members**. That list is for the board you have open.

To let a client see a single board, invite them to that board only. People see a board when they own it or are a member of it, so a client invited to one board does not see your other boards.

Billing is under **Settings > Team > Billing**. The team owner can view billing and update the payment method. The team owner, the board owner, or a board Admin can view billing details and change the billing email.

### BYOK and API keys
API key management is available to **BYOK (Bring Your Own Key)** teams. BYOK teams see and manage API keys directly in the **Settings → Team** navigation. For non-BYOK teams, the API Keys entry is hidden from this section.

## AI Agents
AI agents can be added to boards just like human team members. When you add an agent to a board, it gains access to that board’s tasks and can be assigned work, @mentioned in comments, and participate in the project workflow.

### Adding agents to boards
<Steps>
1. Open the board’s settings or invite panel.
2. Look for the **invite modal** — it shows both team members and any agents you’ve created.
3. Select the agent you want to add to the board.
4. The agent appears in the board’s member list and can be assigned tasks.
</Steps>

Agents added to a board are treated as members of that board. This means:
- Agents appear in the assignee dropdown for tasks on that board
- Agents can be @mentioned in comments and will receive notifications
- Agents can read and update tasks on that board via MCP

<aside type="note">
Agents do not count as team seats toward your subscription limit. You can add as many agents as you need without affecting your seat count.
</aside>

### Agent access scope
When you create an agent, it inherits access to all boards in projects where you’re a member. Use the board-level invite modal to **restrict which boards an agent can access** — boards not on the list treat the agent as if it doesn’t exist.

This is useful when:
- You work across multiple clients or teams and don’t want a given agent active everywhere
- You want to limit an agent to only the boards where it has relevant context
- You have specialized agents for different workflows and need to keep them scoped

## Feedback
Give feedback directly from the app with a prominent call-to-action. The feedback button is always available at the bottom of the app shell rail and opens a fully-featured real feedback modal with:
- Fast-track submission fields for quick suggestions
- Rich text support so you can include screenshots, drafts, or detailed feature requests
- Clear category selection to route your feedback to the right teams
- Direct posting to the Feedback board with auto-assignment

<aside type="tip">
Use the feedback button to share ideas, report bugs, or suggest improvements. Your input shapes future releases and directly affects the UX improvements we ship.
</aside>

## @mentions
Type `@` in any comment to mention a team member. Mentions do two things:
1. **Send a notification** — the mentioned person receives an inbox notification immediately.
2. **Add as follower** — the mentioned person is automatically added as a follower on the task, so they receive future updates.

Mentions work in comments and task descriptions, and support native and external agents:

<aside type="tip">
If you receive a mention that looks suspicious, report it to your workspace owner.
</aside>

### Agent @mentions
<aside type="note">
Agent owners are not notified of their own agent’s comments.
</aside>
@mentioning an agent (native or external) triggers a **Mentioned notification** in that agent’s inbox. External agents with scoped tokens receive notifications via their `agent_notifications` array and can poll it with `hypertask_inbox` (`action: "list"`) to pick up mentions.

This means you can @mention external agents in comments and task descriptions to trigger automation; the agent’s inbox receives a Mentioned notification, and it can respond via MCP comments with proper HTML markup.

If an external agent isn’t receiving @mentions, verify that it has board-level access.

## Emoji reactions
React to tasks and comments with emoji. Reactions serve as lightweight feedback — a quick thumbs-up to acknowledge work, a flag to signal concern, or a celebration when something ships.

### Fast like button
For the most common reaction — a simple thumbs-up — Hypertask provides a **fast like button** that appears directly on task cards and comment rows. No need to open the full emoji picker:

- **Mouse users:** hover over a task card or comment row to reveal the like button, which shows a tooltip with a "[L]" hint; click it to toggle your reaction on or off.
- **Mobile users:** tap the like button that appears inline alongside the comment or task actions.

The like button is a shortcut for the thumbs-up reaction. It appears in the full reactions list alongside any other emoji your teammates have added, and it triggers the same notification to the author as any other reaction.

### Mobile emoji picker
On mobile devices, emoji reactions are organized into a docked picker that mimics popular messaging apps:
- Picker appears docked at the bottom of the screen, aligned with the keyboard input area
- A search bar on the Emoji tab lets you quickly find emojis by name
- Selecting an emoji immediately applies it as a reaction, with the picker closing automatically

### Comment display
Comments can be starred (saved) or pinned, and the visual indicators update based on comment state:
1. **Pinned + saved** — only the orange pinned dot displays (saved state is suppressed)
2. **Pinned only** — only the orange pinned dot displays
3. **Saved only** — only the yellow saved/starred dot displays

### All reactions icon
Click the activity icon next to a comment to see all reactions. This icon appears when someone has reacted in any way, whether it’s a like or another emoji expression.

## Agent decision requests
Agents can ask you for decisive feedback on tickets. When an agent encounters a decision that impacts work (e.g., "Archive this task," "Move to inactive," etc.), it opens a **decision request** on the ticket with one-tap approve/answer buttons.

### Triggering decision requests
Decision requests appear as inline panels on the ticket:
- **Approve** — Applies the agent’s suggested action with one tap
- **Reject / More options** — Opens a menu with detailed choices or alternative actions

Agents only create decision requests when the suggested action clearly affects board state and benefits from human sign-off. Routine summaries, AI editor outputs, and informational messages do not trigger requests.

### Agent aftermath
Once you respond:
- **Approved decisions** — The agent applies the action to the ticket immediately (e.g., archives the task and adds a reason comment)
- **Rejected or alternative** — The agent stops iterating on that item and moves on, leaving the ticket in its current state

You can review all pending decision requests anytime in the ticket feed — the panel stays visible until resolved.

## Real-time sync
Hypertask keeps every connected client live — no manual refreshes needed. Changes made anywhere in the app (or via the CLI and MCP) appear instantly for everyone who has the same board open.

**What updates in real time:**
- Tasks appearing, disappearing, or moving between sections when created, archived, or moved
- Task title, status, priority, and assignee changes
- New comments and reactions
- Board and section changes

Creating a task from the CLI and watching it appear on an open board with no page reload is a first-class workflow — useful for monitoring agents running in your terminal or CI pipeline.

### Real-time collaborative text editing
Multiple people can edit the same rich-text field at the same time, with changes merged automatically.

This applies to:
- Task descriptions
- Comments (while drafting)
- Any rich text field in the app

There are no save buttons — changes persist as you type.

<aside>
Real-time sync means AI agents editing task descriptions via MCP won’t overwrite human edits. Changes are merged automatically.
</aside>

## Managing comments
You can manage comments on any task — including comments left by other team members or agents. This is useful when:
- Cleaning up outdated or irrelevant comments
- Removing agent-generated comments that are no longer needed
- Tidying up task threads for better readability

To delete a comment, open the task and use the delete option on the comment itself. Comment management is available to all project members — trust within the team is assumed for collaborative housekeeping.

### Comment hover panel
The comment hover panel in table views and card lists is streamlined for faster access to actions:
- **Reply** — standard reply action
- **React** — add or remove a reaction (thumbs-up, favorite, flag, etc.)
- **Three-dot menu** — click the three-dot to reveal remaining options

Press and hold <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> (or the three-dot itself) to access the full menu with all comment commands pinned at the top:
- **Edit** — modify the comment
- **Summarize** — generate an AI summary of the comment thread
- **Fast like** — quickly add a thumbs-up reaction

For the most common reaction, just hover and click the like button directly on the comment row. No need to open the full emoji picker.

### Mobile long press to actions
On a phone, press and hold a comment to open the Command Center with that comment's actions at the top. **Edit comment** is first when you wrote the comment. Swiping a comment is off so it does not fight the task swipe that already moves you to the next or previous ticket.

### Mobile comment actions menu
When you open a comment's Command Center on mobile, the first actions are the comment ones:
- **Edit**: open the comment composer (shown first when you wrote the comment)
- **Delete**: remove the comment from the thread
- **Star or turn off star**: save or unsave the comment
- **Pin or turn off pin**: pin the comment to the top of the feed

### URL auto-linkification
Bare URLs in comments are automatically converted into clickable links at render time, regardless of how the comment was created. This applies to comments posted via the web UI, CLI, MCP, or any API client — so a deploy URL pasted by a CLI script or an agent's status update with a link will always be clickable for your teammates.

Links open in a new tab. URLs that are already formatted as hyperlinks or embedded inside images are left unchanged.

### Quoted replies
When you reply to a comment, Hypertask inserts a placeholder for the quoted message.

### GIFs and emoji in comments
The comment composer includes a built-in **Emoji & GIFs picker** with two tabs, giving you Slack-style expressiveness in task discussions.

#### Slash commands
Type a slash command at the start of your comment to open the picker instantly:

| Command | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `/emoji` | Opens the picker on the **Emoji** tab |
| `/giphy` | Opens the picker on the **GIFs** tab |

#### Emoji tab
Browse and search a full emoji library. Click any emoji to insert it into your comment at the cursor position.

#### GIFs tab
The GIFs tab is powered by **Giphy** and offers two modes:
- **Trending** — shows popular GIFs by default when you open the tab.
- **Search** — type any query to find a GIF that fits the moment.

Click a GIF to insert it into your comment. Inserted GIFs render as **resizable media** — drag the corner handles to adjust the size, and the chosen dimensions are preserved when the comment is posted.

<aside type="note">
GIF search requires a Giphy API key configured on the Hypertask deployment. If GIFs are not loading, contact your workspace admin.
</aside>

## Comment edit mode
Edit a comment to refine your thoughts or fix mistakes. The editor includes keyboard shortcuts to help you work efficiently:

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| **ESC** | Leave edit mode without sending (clears unsaved edits) |
| **Ctrl+Enter** | Send the edited comment |

### Exiting edit mode
When you’re in edit mode and want to abandon your changes:
- **Mouse:** click the trash can icon in the edit-mode footer
- **Keyboard:** press **ESC**

Both options exit edit mode without posting the comment and without polluting the conversation with draft text.

## Activity logs
Every change in Hypertask is recorded in the activity log — a full audit trail of who did what, and when.

Tracked actions include:
- Task creation, updates, and deletion
- Section moves
- Assignment and priority changes
- Comments and reactions
- Member joins and leaves
- Board and section modifications

Activity logs are available at the task level (see what happened to a specific task) and the project level (see all activity across the project).

### Comments-only view (default)
The task feed defaults to **comments only** — history events such as field changes, assignments, and status moves are hidden to reduce noise. This keeps the conversation readable at a glance, especially on busy tickets.

To reveal history events:
- Click the **Show history** pill at the top of the feed, or
- Press **`Ctrl+Shift+H`**

Both controls toggle history events on and off. You can also access **Show/Hide history** and **Expand/Collapse all comments** from the command palette (`Ctrl+K`).

<aside type="tip">
If you need a full audit trail of every change on a task, use **Show history** (`Ctrl+Shift+H`) to surface all activity events inline with the comment thread.
</aside>

# Custom Fields
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/custom-fields/

import { Aside, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Overview

Custom fields let you attach structured data to every task on a board, beyond the built-in properties like priority, size, and due date. Each board defines its own set of fields, and every task on that board gets a value slot for each one.

Five field types are supported:

| Type | Use for |
|------|---------|
| **Number** | Ratings, scores, estimates — anything you sort numerically |
| **Text** | Free-form notes that need their own column |
| **Select** | A fixed list of options |
| **Date** | A date separate from due date |
| **Checkbox** | A yes/no flag |

The flagship use case is an **ICE rating** (a Number field for Impact/Confidence/Ease scoring) used to rank a backlog. The [ICE ranking recipe](#ice-ranking-recipe) below walks through setting one up end to end.

## Creating a field

<Steps>

1. Press `<kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>` and search for "Create custom field".
2. Enter a name for the field.
3. Pick a type: Number, Text, Select, Date, or Checkbox.
4. Press `<kbd>Enter</kbd>` to create it.

</Steps>

The field is created on the current board and is visible by default — no separate step to turn it on.

## Setting values

Open a task and the field appears as a property row in the right rail, alongside priority, size, and due date. Click it, type or pick a value, and press `<kbd>Enter</kbd>` to save.

When you create a ticket with the [AI Task Writer](/features/ai-features/#how-it-works-today), it can fill Number, Select, Text, Date, and Checkbox fields from the board's saved instructions or past tickets. For example, a score field can match a score in the title. Values that do not fit the field are skipped. This applies to Ctrl+J compose, AI chat ticket creation, and the CLI/MCP task writer.

## Table view: columns and sorting

Every custom field on a board shows up as a column in [table view](/features/table-view/):

- **Sorting:** click a custom field's column header to sort by it. Number and Date fields sort numerically/chronologically; empty values always sort to the bottom regardless of sort direction.
- **Columns picker:** open "Configure table columns" to toggle any custom field's visibility or drag it to reorder, the same as built-in columns. "Reset to default" restores the original set.

## Views

A [saved view](/features/favorites/) captures the table's current sort, so a view sorted by a custom field stays sorted every time it's opened. This is what makes an ICE ranking view sharable: save it once, and everyone who opens the view sees the backlog in ICE order.

## ICE ranking recipe

<Steps>

1. Create a Number field named `ICE` on the board (see [Creating a field](#creating-a-field) above).
2. Open each task and set its ICE score in the right rail.
3. Switch to table view, add the ICE column if it's hidden, and click the header to sort descending.
4. Save the sorted table as a view named "ICE ranking".

</Steps>

Anyone who opens the "ICE ranking" view sees the board pre-sorted by score, no re-sorting required.

## For agents & API

Custom fields are managed through the same `Bearer htk_...` REST API used elsewhere in Hypertask ([authentication](/api/rest-api/#authentication)). Task detail responses include a `customFieldValues` array for every task on a board with custom fields defined.

### Create a field

**Endpoint:** `POST /api/mcp/custom-fields`

Creating a field is idempotent on `name` — calling create again with a name that already exists on the board returns the existing field instead of erroring.

```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_id": 123, "name": "ICE", "type": "number"}' \
  "https://app.hypertask.ai/api/mcp/custom-fields"
```

**Response example:**

```json
{
  "fieldId": 789,
  "name": "ICE",
  "type": "number"
}
```

### Set a value

**Endpoint:** `POST /api/mcp/custom-fields/value`

Accepts either `field_id` or `field_name`. The recommended surface is to first create the field via `POST /api/mcp/custom-fields`, obtaining `field_id`, then assign values. Values are strictly validated against the field's type — for example, a non-numeric value sent to a Number field is rejected with a `400` response.

**Set value by field_id**

```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"task_id": 789, "field_id": 789, "value": 42}' \
  "https://app.hypertask.ai/api/mcp/custom-fields/value"
```

**Switch to field_name (auto-creates the field first)**

```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"task_id": 789, "field_name": "ICE", "value": 42}' \
  "https://app.hypertask.ai/api/mcp/custom-fields/value"
```

**Tips:**

- Use `field_id` in named endpoints after retrieval for clarity.
- Typed values must match the field's declared type.
- Empty or unset values are represented as `null` unless overridden.

### Delete a field

**Endpoint:** `DELETE /api/mcp/custom-fields/{fieldId}`

```bash
curl -s -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HT_API_KEY" \
  "https://app.hypertask.ai/api/mcp/custom-fields/456"
```

Deleting a field removes every task's value for it. This can't be undone.

<Aside type="caution">
A board can have up to **50 custom fields**, and field names are capped at **64 characters**. Requests past either limit are rejected.
</Aside>

# Favorites
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/favorites/

import { Card, Tabs, TabItem, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

# Favorites

Keep your most important boards within arm's reach by pinning them to the favorites bar. Quickly jump between core workspaces without hunting through lists or filters.

## Pin Boards

1. Open any board's menu (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> or click the board icon next to its title).
2. Toggle **Pin to favorites**. The board will appear in the favorites bar at the left rail.

## Drag to Reorder

- Grab a favorite by its drag handle (⋮⋮).
- Drag it to a new position and release.
- The sidebar reflects the new order immediately.

The favorites bar uses dependable viewport breakpoints for desktop spacing, matching other layout surfaces for consistency and clarity.

## Remove Favorites

- In the favorites bar, **Remove** a pinned board via the context menu (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> or click the three dots).
- The board disappears from your favorites but remains accessible in the board list.

## System Behavior

<p>The favorites bar persists across sessions. When you reconfigure your sidebar layout, your pinned favorites stay visible under the rail. Access management and sharing settings are not affected by pinning.</p>

# Images and Attachments
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/images/

import { Aside, Tabs, TabItem, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

We treat HEIC and HEIF images like any other file: they render consistently across thumbnails, inline previews, galleries, and lightbox views. If a preview isn't suitable, exclude the format from previews or use a low-res fallback.

## Supported formats

| Format | Default behavior |
|--------|------------------|
| HEIC/HEIF | Keep the original for download; the system generates a JPEG copy for previews |
| JPEG/PNG/WebP | Render at full quality |

## Viewing HEIC/HEIF

1. Attach a photo from an iPhone or Mac.
2. The platform creates a browser-compatible JPEG copy for previews, while the original HEIC/HEIF is preserved for download.
3. See it in the same places as regular images:
   - **Attachment thumbnails** below comments and email bubbles
   - **Inline embed** inside a comment or task description
   - **Board gallery** or gallery views that show attachments
   - **Task detail lightbox** with a thumbnail strip at the bottom

## Downloading HEIC/HEIF

HEIC and HEIF photos uploaded to tasks and comments retain their original file format in the download. When you click **Download** on an attachment:

- The original HEIC/HEIF file is downloaded, preserving the full image quality
- Previews across the platform use the generated JPEG copy for faster rendering and broader compatibility

This ensures you can access the highest-quality version of your photos while maintaining fast, consistent previews everywhere else.

## Who can download attachments

<span class="label label--brand">New</span> Only people who can see the parent ticket can download its attachments. Access follows board membership: people who are not the owner, an Admin, or a Member of that board cannot reach downloads.

### How it works

- When opening a task or viewing the task detail lightbox, the system checks that you own the board or are an Admin or Member before exposing download URLs.
- If you are not on the board, downloads come back as not found.
- The board owner, Admins, and Members who can see the ticket can download files. Agents on that board can download too.
- This change prevents unauthorized downloads for attachments that originated on private or board-limited tasks.

### What this protects

- Attachments stored on private tickets are not reachable by users who should not see that context.
- AI-generated task previews now respect the same access gate, ensuring draft images on private tickets are not exposed outside the intended scope.
- Regular downloads continue to work as before for anyone with proper ticket visibility.

### When it applies

- The board owner, Admins, Members, and AI agents on the board can download its attachments.
- People who are not the board owner, an Admin, or a Member cannot reach downloads. A public share link can show the board, and it does not let them download.

## Excluding previews

To prevent HEIC/HEIF from generating previews (e.g., if the file is too large for preview generation):

1. Open the attachment's context menu (three dots).
2. Select **Excluded from previews** to disable automatic preview generation.
3. Uploaders still receive the file; observers only see the original format and a download link.

## Lightbox image strip

In the task detail lightbox, the thumbnail strip shows all attachments in that task. Supported formats and non-preview status appear consistently across all attachments.

## Handling malformed previews in the lightbox strip

If the lightbox shows a broken image icon for a non-decodable file:

- A file icon now appears instead of a broken icon, making it clear the image content could not be decoded.

## Warnings for unexpected content

If a file exhibits preview or display issues (broken icons, no thumbnail, or an unexpected format shown), check:

- The file is flagged as excluded from previews (if the goal was to prevent preview).
- The file is a HEIC/HEIF image under preview logic (historically, some browsers rendered these as named files before conversion completed).

## Upload tips

- **Keep resolution manageable:** Very large HEIC images can lead to longer preview conversion times.
- **Review lightbox strip:** If a thumbnail seems wrong after a HEIC upload, the browser might still be loading a placeholder until conversion finishes.

## Paste support

You can paste photos directly into comments and task descriptions. The system handles both HEIC/HEIF files and regular image formats in the same paste handler:

- HEIC/HEIF: Preserves the original and generates a JPEG preview
- JPEG/PNG/WebP: Downloads as-is

This gives you a single paste workflow whether you're uploading from Photos via copy-paste or dragging and dropping files.

[Learn more about keyboard shortcuts for superhuman-style snippets in the Superhuman-Style Snippets documentation.](/features/superhuman-snippets/)

## Handling blocked image hosts

<span class="label label--brand">New</span> If your network or a firewall blocks the image server domain, attachments now retry through the app domain and display instead of staying broken.

### How it works

- Images usually load directly from `files.hypertask.app`.
- When a request to `files.hypertask.app` fails (for example, due to network restrictions or a firewall), the app retries once through `app.hypertask.ai`.
- On successful retry, the image displays in comments, task descriptions, attachments, and the task detail lightbox.
- This happens automatically; no configuration is required on your side.
- Normal networks that can reach `files.hypertask.app` continue to load images straight from the image server, so performance is unchanged.

### When this helps

This change helps users on restrictive networks (including some corporate Wi-Fi and VPNs) where:

- The image host is blocked, resulting in broken images or connection errors.
- You cannot easily unblock the domain.
- You don't have control over network policy.

Example scenario: A comment includes an image attachment, but your network blocks `files.hypertask.app`. Previously the image would appear broken. Now the app retries through `app.hypertask.ai`, and the image loads as expected.

### Reloading for browsers that blocked images before

If you saw broken images on a previous visit and still use a network that blocks the image server:

- <strong>Refresh the ticket page</strong> and the attachments with retry behavior will load properly.
- After the initial load, the images are cached by your browser, so you should not need to re-enter restrictive network conditions to see them.

[Learn more about keyboard shortcuts in the Keyboard Shortcuts documentation.](/features/keyboard-shortcuts/)

## Resizing images on pages and ticket descriptions

You can manually adjust image size on pages and in ticket descriptions.

### Auto-fit vs manual resize

- <strong>Auto-fit:</strong> Images without a saved size automatically adjust to fit the context (mobile, desktop layout, and container width).
- <strong>Manual resize:</strong> Drag the handle on any image to set a custom width. When you type text nearby and the edit is saved, the new size is persisted.

### Persisted size

- After you drag an image's resize handle and see "Saved," the image's width is saved to that page or ticket description.
- Reloading the page or ticket keeps the image at the custom size instead of reverting to auto-fit.
- Using multiple sizes on the same page works as expected: each one stays where you set it.

### Mobile experience

- On mobile, resized images still respect screen width and remain readable.
- Auto-fit images respond to pinch-to-zoom; resized images follow the set width.

### Common use cases

- <strong>Bulleted lists with images:</strong> Size images consistently (e.g., 50% width) so they look uniform in lists.
- <strong>Diagrams on pages:</strong> Grow or shrink diagrams on a page to finer steps.
- <strong>Ticket descriptions:</strong> Include screenshots at a consistent scale along with typed text.

[Learn more about creating pages in the Pages documentation.](/features/pages/)

<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> When uploading a file and immediately saving before the preview appears (for example with keyboard shortcuts or Save & new), the attachment now persists on the task instead of dropping.

# Inbox & Notifications
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/inbox/

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The **Inbox** gathers all notifications (mentions, assignments, and more) into a single feed, letting you process them efficiently. Use keyboard shortcuts for quick actions and keep important work at the top of your queue.

## Viewing the inbox

Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> to open the command palette and search for **"Inbox"**, or go to the Inbox page from the sidebar. The inbox shows:
- **Unread notifications** from mentions, assignments, reactions, and follow updates
- **Actionable items** like tasks, notifications with dismiss options (undo, dismiss all, undo all), and confirmed operations (invites, feedback)
- **Important tasks**: rows marked with the **Important** label appear first, in priority order and timeline-sorted (newest first)

### Replying to notification emails

Reply directly to a task notification email to add your response as a comment on the task. Send the reply from the same email address as your Hypertask account so Hypertask can verify it and post it under your name.

The inbox can be grouped into multiple views:

<Aside type="tip">Use <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>F</kbd> from the Inbox to search across all notifications. This is scoped across boards for board-agnostic filtering.</Aside>

### Bulk archive

Select multiple notifications with mouse clicks or keyboard navigation. When you select rows, the selection count appears next to the archive and remind icons, and the archive action archives all selected notifications in one step:

| Action | Shortcut | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| **Select all** | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | Select all visible rows in the current view, mirroring page behavior |
| **Archive selected** | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>E</kbd> | Archive all selected notifications |
| **Archive all** | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>E</kbd> | Archive all notifications (opens confirmation if many) |

<Aside type="note"><kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> selects all visible rows rather than every row in the inbox due to index limits - select specific subsets when the list is long.</Aside>

### Triage with AI chat

Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> (<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> on Mac). Choose **Triage inbox**. This starts a new AI chat.

Ask AI chat to read your inbox. It reads up to 500 messages per page and can continue through the remaining pages without asking for confirmation.

Before archiving a batch, chat previews every affected ticket, including other messages it would clear on those tickets. Confirm once for that batch. If the batch changes, chat shows a fresh preview and asks again. Its reply names the tickets it cleared.

### Inbox views

| View | Shortcut | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| **Inbox** | Default | All notifications |
| **Search** | Search icon | Text-based search across all boards |
| **Notifications** | Notification icon | List of all notification types |

### Inbox filtering scope

New users in a board see notifications for private tasks, while users removed from a board no longer receive those notifications in their Inbox. To prevent a stale notification from reappearing, you can reply to it (or tap Undo) to remove it from your queue. Cleaning up unsubscribed notifications helps keep the Inbox focused and relevant.

## Agent chatter in the inbox

<span class="label label--brand">Improvement</span> Agent messages from the AI now stay out of the personal inbox. Agent-only comments (FYI messages) and agent chatter no longer appear as notifications for human users. Instead:
- **Agent chatter ignored** – Pure agent commentary without a human @mention does not reach its owner's inbox.
- **FYI mentions visible** – An agent FYI comment with a human @mention does appear in the inbox, making it clear the human is being included in the loop, but it stays out of the Important section.
- **Only open questions land in Important** – When an agent poses a question that requires a human response, the message lands in the Important section so you can act on it first.

This applies to all agents using Hypertask's AI integration and keeps your inbox focused on questions and actions directly tied to your own work.

## Numbered pins in the mobile inbox

On mobile, each inbox row shows a numbered indicator next to the sender name. This creates a visual order that matches the date you received the notification, making it easier to scan recent items:
- **Numbered pins** appear on desktop and mobile inbox rows
- The numbers correspond to timeline order (newest first)
- This keeps your attention on the most recent important items without relying solely on the top position

<Aside type="tip">The numbered pins complement the timeline-sorted order for returning visits, giving you a quick visual guide to your recent notifications.</Aside>

## Invite link validation across pages

<span class="label label--brand">Improved</span> Pages that generate or use invite links now validate board context. **My Tasks** and **Inbox** no longer send invite-link requests without a board, which previously caused console errors. Requesting an invite link without a board now shows a clear message instead of a server error, keeping the console clean and providing explicit feedback when a board is required.

This change applies across most pages that send invite links, ensuring any invalid requests surface a user-friendly message rather than an unhandled error.

## Shortcuts tip visibility

<span class="label label--brand">Improved</span> When using the archive keyboard shortcuts (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>E</kbd> or <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>E</kbd>), the tip that shows which shortcut to press (for example, "press E to archive") now appears and stays visible. The tip is tied to the bottom shortcut bar ("Ctrl+K for Command center, J to go down...").

Before this fix, repeatedly archiving would close the bottom shortcut bar or clear the inbox, causing the tip to disappear and making it hard to see which key shortcut to use. The tip is automatically disabled when the shortcut bar is hidden for the session, so navigating to the Inbox or re-opening the shortcut bar restores visibility.

## Board chip in the new task box

When you use <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd> to create a new task from the inbox, the new task box shows a board chip indicating the intended destination:
- **Always visible**: The chip appears as soon as the box opens, so you always see the target board.
- **Same everywhere**: On a board or a ticket detail page, it shows that page's board.
- **Editable**: Click the chip to choose a different board before saving the task.

<Aside type="note">Ctrl+J uses the same board selection logic as the AI chat box: the focused ticket's board if there is one, otherwise the open board split, and finally the last used board for All or Important views.</Aside>

# Integrations
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/integrations/

Hypertask works with Cursor and Codex. Both connect through MCP, the same way as any other MCP client.

## Works today

These are in **Settings**, then **Connect**:

- **[MCP](/mcp/overview/).** Works with any MCP client, such as Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.
- **[CLI](/cli/reference/).** The `hypertask` command.
- **[REST API](/api/rest-api/).**
- **[Webhooks](/mcp/agent-webhooks/).** Signed requests to a URL you control.

**Figma** is under **Settings**, then **Profile**, then **Accounts**. Connect a Figma account there. Hypertask uses that connection when a task includes a Figma link.

**ChatGPT** uses an OpenAPI action. The steps are on [MCP Integration](/mcp/overview/#client-configuration), under the ChatGPT tab.

## Not available yet

- **Slack app.** Not available yet.
- **GitHub per board.** Connecting GitHub to a board is not available yet.
- **Google Calendar sync.** Not available yet. Due dates still appear on the Hypertask [calendar](/features/calendar/).
- **Other importers.** There is no Jira, Trello, or Asana sync, and no other native importer.

# Keyboard Shortcuts
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/keyboard-shortcuts/

import { Aside, CardGrid, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

This page lists every keyboard shortcut registered in Hypertask for Windows/Linux and Mac.

<Aside type="note" title="App-shell rail">
The **App shell surfaces** shortcuts <kbd>1</kbd> through <kbd>6</kbd> apply only when the app-shell rail is enabled.
</Aside>

<Aside type="note" title="Mac board switching">
On Mac, switch boards with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>0-9</kbd>, not <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>0-9</kbd>. Mac browsers reserve <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>1-9</kbd> for tab switching.
</Aside>

<Aside type="note" title="Mac command palette">
On Mac, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> opens the command palette in addition to <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>.
</Aside>

## App shell surfaces

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Inbox | <kbd>1</kbd> | <kbd>1</kbd> |
| Board | <kbd>2</kbd> | <kbd>2</kbd> |
| Table | <kbd>3</kbd> | <kbd>3</kbd> |
| Calendar | <kbd>4</kbd> | <kbd>4</kbd> |
| Toggle AI chat | <kbd>5</kbd> or <kbd>]</kbd> | <kbd>5</kbd> or <kbd>]</kbd> |
| Search | <kbd>6</kbd> | <kbd>6</kbd> |

<Aside type="note" title="Undo behavior">
Outside a text editor, undo restores the latest pending task, inbox, star, or pin action while its undo notification is visible. Inside a description, comment, or other editor, the same shortcut keeps its normal text-undo behavior.
</Aside>

## Board

Press <kbd>N</kbd> to open quick add in the column under your pointer. With the pointer off the board it uses the focused column, then the selected task's column, then the first visible column. <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> no longer opens quick add. The shortcut does not run while you are typing or a modal is open. <kbd>C</kbd> still opens the full task creator.

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Add task in the full creator | <kbd>C</kbd> | <kbd>C</kbd> |
| Fast entry at top, when enabled | <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> | <kbd>Option</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> |
| Fast entry at bottom, when enabled | <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> | <kbd>Option</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> |
| Add sub-task | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>+</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>+</kbd> |
| Add task at top | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> |
| Open quick add | <kbd>N</kbd> | <kbd>N</kbd> |
| Open task | <kbd>Enter</kbd> | <kbd>Enter</kbd> |
| Next view (old header design) | <kbd>]</kbd> | <kbd>]</kbd> |
| Previous view | <kbd>[</kbd> | <kbd>[</kbd> |
| Move focus to top | <kbd>gg</kbd> | <kbd>gg</kbd> |
| Move focus to bottom | <kbd>GG</kbd> | <kbd>GG</kbd> |
| Move task down | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>J</kbd> +  | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>J</kbd> +  |
| Move task up | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> +  | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> +  |
| Move task right | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>L</kbd> +  | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>L</kbd> +  |
| Move task left | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>H</kbd> +  | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>H</kbd> +  |
| Cross-row movement and row-targeted throws | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>J/K</kbd> reorder within the current column; <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>L/H</kbd> throw to an adjacent column by default (original card preserved, then restored), and supporting vertical reorder via <kbd>Shift</kbd> + the arrow keys while holding the column throw key | |
| Move task to the left | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>L</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> +  | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>L</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> +  |
| Sort Kanban board | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>S</kbd> | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>S</kbd> |
| Toggle table layout | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>T</kbd> | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>T</kbd> |
| Show task options | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>+</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>+</kbd> |
| Move task to the right | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>H</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> +  | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>H</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> +  |
| Assign a user | <kbd>A</kbd> | <kbd>A</kbd> |
| Start / stop timer | <kbd>W</kbd> | <kbd>W</kbd> |

## Board batch selection
These controls apply on a desktop board. Use the **Open actions** button in the bottom selection bar to open the same batch actions from the mouse.

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Select every card on the board | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> |
| Select every card in the focused column, or the column under the pointer when nothing has focus | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>A</kbd> |
| Select or deselect the active card | <kbd>X</kbd> | <kbd>X</kbd> |
| Select a range in one column | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + click | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + click |
| Archive selected cards | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>E</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>E</kbd> |
| Assign selected cards | <kbd>A</kbd> | <kbd>A</kbd> |
| Set tags on selected cards | <kbd>T</kbd> | <kbd>T</kbd> |
| Move selected cards | <kbd>M</kbd> | <kbd>M</kbd> |
| Clear selection | <kbd>Esc</kbd> | <kbd>Esc</kbd> |

<Aside type="tip" title="The Share Task window names each shortcut on hover">
Open it with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>S</kbd> (<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>S</kbd> on a Mac) and hover any of its four options. A tooltip shows that option's own keys: private title and link, private link only, public title and link, and public link only.
</Aside>

<Aside type="tip" title="Ctrl+O lists every link and attachment">
View all links (Ctrl+O on the links and sub-tasks row) now lists every link and attachment on a ticket, including those in descriptions, comments, and attachment files. Previously, some links and files were missed.
</Aside>

## Mobile comment composer gesture actions
On mobile devices, the comment composer keeps dictation as the primary input method with simplified controls:

- Dictate first, then refine with the *Improve with AI* option (opens a focused bottom sheet on mobile)
- Send remains the secondary, accessible action
- The Improve with AI trigger provides inline text enhancement without replacing dictation as the primary entry point

<Aside type="tip">
On mobile, start with dictation and tap *Improve with AI* to refine your comments without leaving the input flow.
</Aside>

## Mobile in-app gestures

- On mobile, press and hold a comment to open the Command Center with comment actions at the top. Edit comment is first when you wrote the comment.

## Image & Media
Keyboard controls for media insertions and pickers in comments and task descriptions.

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Open GIF picker | <kbd>/</kbd> in a comment or description (search for "giphy") | <kbd>/</kbd>, then "giphy" |
| Navigate GIF picker | Arrow keys highlight; Tab switches tabs | Arrow keys highlight; Tab switches tabs |
| Insert GIF into comment | <kbd>Enter</kbd> | <kbd>Enter</kbd> |

<Aside type="tip">
The GIF picker is a picker component you navigate with keyboard. Type <kbd>/</kbd> in the comment or description compose box, search for "giphy", then use arrow keys to move the highlight, Tab to switch 10x10 tabs, and Enter to insert the selected GIF.
</Aside>

<Aside type="tip">
Focus chat input via <kbd>Ctrl+Q</kbd> now works on /chat and on boards when a docked chat instance is present, focusing the input.
</Aside>

| Code | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> |

<Aside type="tip">
The Command Palette lists board and section actions, including "Hide column", "Show columns", "Archive board", "Delete board", and more. Use <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> and type keywords like "hide", "show", "archive", "delete" to quickly access relevant actions.

### Board settings from Ctrl+K
When you search for **"Board settings"** in the Command Palette using <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd>, the board picker now preselects the board you came from. This works whether you're on a ticket page, board page, or another view - even if you previously had a different team open in settings. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to cancel and restore your previous state.

<Aside type="tip">
Try it: open any ticket, press <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>, type "board", pick **"Board settings"**. The board picker shows that ticket's board and preselects the right team.
</Aside>

## Hiding and Showing Columns
To hide a column using the Command Palette:

1. Open the Command Palette: <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>
2. Type "hide" to find the "Hide column" action
3. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to hide the active (hovered/last-clicked) column directly
4. The Command Palette closes automatically after execution

To show previously hidden columns:

1. Open the Command Palette: <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>
2. Type "show" to find the "Show columns" action
3. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to reveal all hidden sections

<Aside type="note">
"Hide column" now targets the last clicked or currently hovered section rather than cycling through sections, making it easier to hide the specific column you're working with. The "Empty columns" command also reads the current state and filters both the Kanban view groups and the table view groups, showing "Show empty columns" when they're hidden and "Hide empty columns" when they're visible.
</Aside>

An empty view keeps its visible columns on screen, even when empty columns are hidden. Your saved setting does not change. Add a ticket and the other empty columns hide again. Columns you hid individually stay hidden.

## Board palette
Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd> (Windows/Linux) or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd> (Mac) to show the board palette overlay. On the left rail, the board palette displays your user account row with:
- **Email or handle** - Click to open the account switcher dialog
- **Avatar** - Click to open Account & Profile settings

This provides quick access to switching workspaces or reviewing your account configuration without leaving the current board.

<Aside type="tip">
The board palette joins <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> as a non-intrusive way to access workspace settings while staying in context.
</Aside>

## Open Latest Updates
Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> (Windows/Linux) or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> (Mac) then search for **"Latest Updates"** in the board palette or command palette to open the Latest Updates panel from any route in the app. This provides quick access to see recent activity across your boards without leaving your current view.

## Global Alt+Number board shortcuts
**Before:** On the table view or any board view, <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>1-7</kbd> shortcuts did nothing even when the app-shell rail was supposed to be active, causing them to behave as no-ops.

**After:** When the rail is enabled, <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>2-7</kbd> now correctly switch to their corresponding surfaces (Board = 2, Table = 3, Calendar = 4, AI Chat dock = 5, and Search = 6) from any view. On Mac, the global board switcher uses <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>2-7</kbd> instead of <kbd>Cmd</kbd> to avoid interfering with tab switching.

<Aside type="note">
The app-shell rail and global Alt+Number shortcuts were designed to provide tactile, one-hand navigation across main surfaces. Enabling the rail (via account menu or command palette) unlocks these skips so they work reliably everywhere, not only on the rail itself.
</Aside>

## Time reports quick-log
Quick-log time directly from the board or a task card using <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>:

- **On a board or task card** - Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> to open the quick-log dialog preconfigured for the selected card.
- **On an open ticket** - Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> to instantly jump to the per-ticket time log modal, skipping the intermediate step of selecting the ticket from the board list.

The quick-log interface supports Hours and Minutes fields, board and user filters per entry, and works across time zones with per-entry local-noon timestamps for accurate log association with the logged day.

**Keyboard shortcuts**:

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Quick-log time on a selected board card | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> |

## Timer shortcuts
Time tracking shortcuts are available when time tracking is enabled for your board or task:
- **App shell rail** - Press <kbd>7</kbd> on the rail to open the running-timers view
- **Task detail** - Press <kbd>Option</kbd> + <kbd>T</kbd> or <kbd>Alt+T</kbd> to start or stop the open task timer

The timer indicator appears in the task card and task detail, showing whether a timer is running for that task.

See the <a href="/features/time-tracking/">Time Tracking</a> page for full details.

## System-theme prediction
When you open the Command Palette with <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> (or <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd> on Mac), theme-related options now display context-appropriate labels to make system-theme mode predictable. Retired numeric theme modes (1-5) redirect safely to the Appearance settings with your in-session command state preserved.

<Aside type="tip">
Theme options in the command palette now adapt to your system theme and gracefully redirect legacy theme choices to Appearance settings.
</Aside>

## Copy current page URL
When you open the Command Palette with <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd>, the action **"Copy current page URL"** copies the complete browser address, including the board, view, task, filters, and section. The action is available everywhere <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> opens, including task detail, calendar, and inbox views.

<Aside type="note">
The action is available to everyone.
</Aside>

## Use everywhere, including Settings
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> (Windows/Linux) or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> (Mac) now opens the Command Palette on every signed-in page. This includes:
- Boards, tickets, inbox, and search (existing behavior)
- My Tasks view
- All settings pages, such as Settings & General, Board general, and Appearance

On Mac, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> also works in addition to <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>.

Public/sign-in pages, including the sign-in page, still ignore this shortcut.

Escape behavior in Settings:
- First <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the command menu and keeps you in Settings
- A second <kbd>Esc</kbd> exits Settings as usual

This makes the command palette consistently available for board actions, views, and shortcuts throughout the app.

## Mobile in-app gestures
- On mobile, press and hold a comment to open the Command Center with comment actions at the top. Edit comment is first when you wrote the comment.
- Dictation remains the primary input method on mobile; Tap *Improve with AI* to refine your comments without leaving the input flow

## Mobile page exit gesture
On mobile, pressing **<kbd>Esc</kbd>** in the full-screen Pages view now exits via the back action - just like other views in the app. With text typed but unsaved, <kbd>Esc</kbd> clears the unsaved draft. Without text, a single <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the page and stays on the task.

## Ctrl+J board chip
When you press <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd>, the new task box shows which board the task will land on, using the same board chip UI as the AI chat box. The chip appears as soon as the box opens, on every page: a board, a ticket, the inbox and views that mix boards. On a board or ticket page it shows that page's board.

**Board selection logic:**

- **Focused ticket's board:** If a ticket is visible and focused in the inbox, <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd> places the new task on that ticket's board.
- **Open board split:** If there's no focused ticket, the task goes on the open board split.
- **All or Important:** If no board is in context, <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd> uses All or Important as a default board.

Click the chip before saving to change the board.

<Aside type="tip">From the inbox, <kbd>Ctrl+J</kbd> is the fastest way to start a new task on a specific board without exiting the feed.</Aside>

## Sending from the Ctrl+J new task box
The new task box sends with the same shortcut as comments and descriptions, so Enter is free for paragraphs.

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Send the new task | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Enter</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Enter</kbd> |
| Start a new paragraph | <kbd>Enter</kbd> | <kbd>Enter</kbd> |

The hint under the box names the shortcut. One press creates one task with everything you typed, and your note stays in the box if the task fails.
### New Task board shortcut hint

Hover over the board chip in **New Task** to see its keyboard shortcut:
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd> on Windows and Linux,
or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>B</kbd> on Mac.
The same shortcut appears below the task box. Click the chip or use that
shortcut to choose a board. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to cancel without losing
your draft.

# Pages
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/pages/

import { Aside, Card, CardGrid, LinkCard, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Pages keep research and notes on your boards. A page can stand alone or link tickets. Open **Pages** below **Table** in the sidebar. You can also use **Commands → Go to Pages**.

## What is a Page?

A page belongs to a board. Linking a ticket does not grant access. Pages follow their board’s existing permissions. Pages are:

- **Board-owned:** Stand alone or link multiple tickets.
- **Markdown-first:** Write in markdown; the editor renders rich HTML with TipTap.
- **Agent-friendly:** Created, appended, updated, and archived programmatically via CLI, MCP, REST, and AI Chat.
- **RAG-indexed:** Every write is indexed so the AI can search, summarize, and reason over page content.
- **Versioned:** Every change is captured with history and restore capabilities.
- **Conflict-safe:** Optimistic-lock guards return a 409 conflict if multiple agents try to write at once.

## Create and find pages

1. Open **Pages** from the sidebar or Commands.
2. Choose **This board** or **All boards**.
3. Search by page title or content.
4. Choose **New page** to start a document.
5. Choose its board when prompted.

Your title and content save automatically.
**Archived pages** lists documents removed from active lists.

## Search finds a page from different words

<span class="label label--brand">Improvement</span> Pages were already sent to the search index, but page search only matched the exact words you typed. Page search now reads that index, the same way ticket search does, so a page written as "view tab count includes cards in hidden columns" is found by "tab counter includes cards that the view hides".

What changed for you:

- **The Pages screen** returns the right page for a question written in your own words, up to 50 results per search.
- **Agents** get the same behaviour through the page search tool in REST, MCP and AI Chat.
- **Exact words still work**, and exact matches stay first in the list.
