- **Board access is unchanged.** A page is only returned when the current page still passes the same board, project, archive and link checks, so better ranking never shows a page you could not open.
- **No search, no change.** The unfiltered page list behaves exactly as before.

The release switch is `htpr-9017-smart-page-search`. With it off, page search falls back to matching the exact words you typed.

## Link tickets and pages

On a page, choose **+ Link ticket**.
Pick an existing ticket from the search window.
**Linked tickets** shows the page’s visible ticket links.
Choose **Unlink** to remove a link.
Unlinking keeps the page and ticket.

On a ticket, open **Commands → Link page**.
Pick an existing page from the list.
The page appears in that ticket’s **Pages**.
Existing page lists also offer **+ Link page**.
Commands also includes **Link page** and **Link ticket**.

Pages without visible tickets show **Back to Pages**.

---

## Agent permissions for page operations

<span class="label label--brand">Security fix</span> Hypertask now properly restricts page actions based on an agent's access mode. Depending on the agent's live configuration, it may be:

- **Normal (read/write):** Can create, change, archive, and restore task pages.
- **Read-only:** Can only read pages. Creating, changing, archiving, or restoring is refused.

**Behavior before this fix:** A read-only agent was able to perform all four page actions (create, change, archive, restore) on task pages, bypassing its access mode and effectively gaining write-like permissions despite being restricted to reading.

**After this fix:** The server checks an agent's access mode before each page action. A read-only agent now receives a secure refusal for all four write operations, and the page remains unchanged.

This change, verified live on the QA team's own board, ensures that agent permissions match the documented behavior.

## Comments indexed for search

<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> Comments that are very long or empty now generate searchable search copies. Previously the AI service that creates these copies would reject such comments, leaving them invisible in results. Now they are compressed and indexed, keeping full search coverage for comment threads. This change is part of the broader Turbopuffer upsert optimization, which also affects page content indexing.

## Publishing a long report from a file

<span class="label label--brand">New</span> The CLI can read page content from a file, so a long report does not have to fit in one command-line string. Linux caps a single argument near 128KB, which used to force agents to paste a report in pieces.

```bash
hypertask pages create --task HTPR-123 --title "QA report" --html-file report.html
hypertask pages update 456 --content-file report.html --canvas
hypertask pages append 456 --content-file notes.md
```

- `--content-file <path>` reads the content from a file and keeps the page's current type on update and append.
- `--html-file <path>` reads the content and marks the page type `html`.
- Add `--canvas` to store the file exactly as written, styles and inline images included. This is the way to publish a self-contained HTML report.

## Mobile pinch zoom

# Reports
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/reports/

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The **Reports hub** (`/report`) lists saved reports and board velocity reports for boards you can access.

## Review board velocity

Open **Reports**, then choose a board under **Velocity**. You can also open the command palette from a board and choose **Board velocity report**.

Choose **Today**, **7 days**, **14 days**, **30 days**, **3 months**, **6 months**, or **12 months**. The default is **30 days**.

The report shows:

- Median time to finish a task and tasks finished per week
- Finished work and comments by board member
- Created versus finished tasks
- Open and stale tasks by column

## Create a saved report

Ask AI chat or an agent to create a report for a board. You can also save HTML with the CLI or MCP. Saved reports appear under **Reports** in the hub, with their board, author, and last update time.

### CLI

Use a short slug, the board's numeric ID, a title, and an HTML file:

```bash
hypertask report create weekly-summary \
  --project 15 \
  --title "Weekly summary" \
  --html-file ./weekly-summary.html
```

Use `--body` instead of `--html-file` to pass HTML directly. Add `--description` for a short summary. The CLI also supports `report list`, `report get`, `report update`, and `report delete`. Every command needs `--project`; every command except `list` also needs a slug. Deleting a report requires `--confirm`.

### MCP

Call `hypertask_reports` with the `create` action:

```json
{
  "action": "create",
  "input": {
    "project_id": 15,
    "slug": "weekly-summary",
    "title": "Weekly summary",
    "body_html": "<h1>Weekly summary</h1><p>Three tasks completed this week.</p>"
  }
}
```

Use `list`, `get`, `update`, or `delete` to manage saved reports. Open the URL returned by the tool to view the report.

<Aside type="note">
A saved report is a snapshot, not a live query. Include all data in its HTML. Inline styles and scripts work, but network requests and external script libraries do not. Update the report when its data changes.
</Aside>

## Status updates

A **status update** is an AI-written summary of what has happened on a board, saved as a report.

**To generate one:** from the board, press <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> and run **Generate status update**. It opens when ready.

The update has four parts:

- **Headline** - one sentence on where the board stands
- **Shipped** - work that reached a done column or was archived
- **In flight** - work moving through the other columns
- **Risks and blockers** - tickets sitting still or otherwise worth attention

It is written from the same board data the velocity report uses - ticket movement over the window, per-column counts, staleness thresholds - so the figures it quotes are computed rather than generated. Ticket titles are passed to the model as data, not instructions, so a task title cannot steer what the summary claims.

Each board keeps **one** status update, at a fixed address:

```
/report/project-<board-id>/status-update
```

Regenerating rewrites that page rather than creating a new one, so a link to it always shows the current state. The default window is the last 7 days.

<Aside type="caution">
The slug `status-update` is reserved for this feature on every board. A report you create manually with that slug will be overwritten the next time an update is generated.
</Aside>

## Best practices

- Give reports clear titles and short slugs.
- Include the reporting period in the content.
- Update an existing report to keep the same link.
- Use inline SVG or CSS for charts.

# Scheduling
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/scheduling/

# Scheduling

Plan when work starts, set up recurring tasks, or reuse common task structures. Scheduling features help you align work with deadlines, keep deliverables on track, and streamline repetitive project workflows.

## Due dates

Set when a task should be completed:
- **Pick a date**: Click the due date field on a task or in the New task form, then choose from the calendar.
- **Predictive phrases**: Enter phrases like "tomorrow," "next week," or "in 3 days" to set relative dates.
- **Remove a due date**: Click today's date or select "No due date" to clear it.

### Snoozed tasks in My Tasks

To temporarily hide a task from your My Tasks list, set a snooze until a specific date:
- Open the task and use the snooze option in the edit panel, or
- Use the command palette (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd>) and search for "Snooze this task"
- The task will no longer appear in My Tasks until that date passes
- The snooze date sets a calendar reminder so you can resurface the task later

A snooze is per task and independent of other views. Tasks remain otherwise accessible from boards, calendars, and saved views.

### Grouping by due time

My Tasks lists tasks by due time by default:
- **Overdue**: Due dates in the past, always at the top
- **Today**: Due date is today
- **This week**: Due date is within the next 7 days
- **Later**: Due date is any time in the future
- **No due date**: Tasks without a set due date

Use the **Group** toggle or saved view settings to show board groups instead.

## My Tasks planning view

The **My Tasks** view gives you a personal planning dashboard for work assigned to you:
- Groups by due time (Overdue, Today, This week, Later, No due date)
- Full Kanban board filters available across all time groups
- Custom columns you've defined on your boards are preserved in My Tasks
- Real-time live updates: rows refresh automatically when changes happen from other tabs, the CLI, or agents, without reloading the page
- Quick-add at the top: type a task title and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to create a task on the view's default board, assigned to you

### Saved views

Save custom filters, sorting, board selection, and hidden columns to create personalized My Tasks views:
- **Full filtering**: Filter by title, assignee, priority, due date, labels, and more
- **Sorting**: Sort by any of the same fields, with priority as the primary sort key
- **Board selection**: Show tasks from one board or across multiple boards
- **Done columns hidden by default**: Keep focused on active work

<span class="label label--brand">Behavior change</span> Saved views now use the same save, reset, and Ctrl+K picker flows that you use on the Kanban board for deep controls. The Scope button (including Involvement, Detail, and Group scope) and its corresponding command now open the consistent board picker panel you see throughout the app, with search and standard keyboard navigation for "up to scope" actions. This keeps your palette familiar across inbox and board surfaces.

> **Tip**: Create a My Tasks saved view to align on active priorities; at any time you can reorder the view's filters, sorting, or board selection without losing them.

Saved views persist at the account level and can be reused or deleted from the view toolbar.

## Repeating tasks

Configure a task to repeat on a schedule:
- Set a due date and enable repeat
- Choose a frequency (daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly)
- Specify repeat until (date or count)

When a repeat task is marked complete, a new instance appears with the next due date.

## Task templates

Task templates save task structures for reuse:
- Create a template from a completed task's fields, due date, and subtasks
- Apply templates to new tasks to keep formatting consistent
- Manage templates from the Board Settings or task detail "Templates" section

## Start dates

A start date records when work is *meant to begin*, separately from the due date that records when it must *finished*.

**To set one:** open a task, press <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>, run **Set start date**. The field accepts natural language — `today`, `tomorrow`, `next week monday`, `in 3 days` — or pick from the presets. Choose **Reset** to clear it.

The task detail shows a **Start date** row only once the field is set; a task without one looks exactly as it did before.

A start date on its own never makes a task overdue. Only a missed *due date* does that. A task that started last week but has no deadline is current work, not late work, and **My tasks** files it accordingly.

### API

```http
POST /api/tasks/setStartDate
Content-Type: application/json

{ "taskId": 1234, "startDate": "2026-08-10T09:00:00.000Z" }
```

Pass `"startDate": null` to clear it. Returns the updated task. Requires membership of the task's board.

## Repeating tasks

A repeating task recreates itself when you finish it.

**To set a repeat:** open a task, press <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>, run **Repeat task**, and choose a cadence:

| Cadence | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Daily` | Every day |
| `Weekdays` | Every weekday, Monday to Friday |
| `Weekly` | Every 7 days |
| `Biweekly` | Every 14 days |
| `Monthly` | Same day each month, clamped to the last day of shorter months (31 Jan → 28 Feb) |

Choose **Don't repeat** to stop a task repeating. The option only appears when a rule is already set. A repeating task shows a **Repeats** row in the task detail.

### What "finishing" means

The next occurrence is created when you **move the task into a done column**, or **archive it yourself**. It carries over the title, description, priority, size, labels and assignees, with the date advanced by one period.

Two cases deliberately do *not* create a new occurrence:
- **Auto-archive.** A board's auto-archive sweep fires because nobody touched a task, which is abandonment rather than completion. Repeating there would regenerate neglected tasks indefinitely.
- **Moving the task to another board**, including into that board's done column. Relocating work is not completing it.

Finishing a repeating task late never produces an already-overdue copy: the next date is rolled forward until it is genuinely in the future, keeping the original time of day and, for weekly rules, the original weekday.

If a board has no column that counts as "not done", the task does not repeat — the new occurrence would otherwise be created directly into a done column, where it would read as finished work the moment it appeared.

### API

```http
POST /api/tasks/setRecurrence
Content-Type: application/json

{ "taskId": 1234, "recurrence": "Weekly" }
```

Valid values: `Daily`, `Weekdays`, `Weekly`, `Biweekly`, `Monthly`, or `null` to stop repeating. Requires membership of the board.

## Task templates

A template stores the shape of a task so you can create the same kind of work repeatedly without retyping it. Templates are per board, and capture the **title**, **description**, **priority**, **size** and **labels**.

**To save one:** open a task you want to reuse, press <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>, run **Save task as template**. The template is named after the task title.

**To use one:** from the board, press <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>, run **New task from template**, and pick from the list. The new task is created in the board's first non-done column and opens immediately.

Labels that were deleted after the template was saved are skipped rather than failing the creation.

### API

```http
GET    /api/task-templates?projectId=15      # list a board's templates
POST   /api/task-templates                   # { "taskId": 1234, "name": "Weekly review" }
DELETE /api/task-templates                   # { "templateId": 7 }
POST   /api/task-templates/apply             # { "templateId": 7 }
```

`name` is optional on create and defaults to the task's title. All four require membership of the board.

## My tasks

**My tasks** answers "what am I working on today" across every board you belong to. The inbox remains the place to triage what arrived; this is the place to plan.

**To open it:** <kbd>G</kbd> then <kbd>M</kbd>, or <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> and **Go to my tasks**, or visit `/my-tasks`.

It shows every open task assigned to you as a **table**, the same table the board uses. By default the sections are due-time groups: **Overdue**, **Today**, **This week**, **Later**, and **No due date**. Overdue stays first. Use **Group** to switch to one section per board. Saved My Tasks views remember that choice.

**Ordering puts urgent work first.** In time groups, Overdue is the first section. In board groups, boards that contain overdue tasks sort above boards that do not. Inside a group, overdue tasks lead, then the rest by due date, with undated tasks last.

**Cross-board priority sorting.** In any table column, click the column header to sort by that column. Sorts are applied across each board's section, so you can see the highest-priority tasks at the top of the list, ordered by the board's default priority level.

**Priority levels.** Tasks across all boards are sorted using the board's real priority levels: No Priority, Urgent, High, Medium, and Low. The sort uses these levels consistently regardless of the board's visual cues.

**The split pills filter by board.** They still work inside a time group. "All" shows every board; picking a board narrows the table to that board alone. <kbd>Tab</kbd> and <kbd>Shift+Tab</kbd> cycle through them, exactly as on the inbox and board surfaces.

**Sorting keeps the grouping.** Clicking a column header sorts within each time or board section rather than flattening everything into one list.

Navigation matches the inbox and scheduled views: <kbd>J</kbd> and <kbd>K</kbd> (or the arrow keys) to move, <kbd>Enter</kbd> to open, <kbd>Esc</kbd> to go back.

My tasks is a planning surface across every board you belong to. Use the quick-add row at the top to create a task on the view's default board (My Tasks asks once if none is set), or create from a board, the inbox, or <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>.

## Agent scheduling and provider selection

# Search
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/search/

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

# Search

Search across your board to find tasks fast. Type to filter by people, boards, labels, statuses, dates, and more, with autocomplete that suggests operators and values as you type.

## Search filters

Use operators to filter tasks by specific fields:

- **from:** Restrict to tasks created by a specific person.
- **assignee:** Restrict to tasks assigned to a specific person.
- **commenter:** Restrict to tasks commented on by a specific person.
- **in:** Restrict to tasks in a board, section, or column; `board:` also filters by board.
- **label:** Restrict to tasks with a specific label.
  - **Board-scoped label suggestions (Owner + QA preview):**
    - When a board is picked with an `in:` or `board:` chip, `label:` only suggests labels from that board.
    - Each label shows the number of search results on the right (open and done, not archived).
    - Labels with zero results appear at the bottom, greyed out.
    - Without a board selected, all your labels appear (same-name labels merged into one row).
  - <div class="asideInfo"><small>Preview for owners and QA only. Available when board-scoped label suggestions are enabled.</small></div>
- **is:** Narrow by type; for example, `is:card` to show only standard cards.
- **priority:** Filter by task priority: `priority:urgent`, `priority:high`, `priority:medium`, or `priority:low`.
- **type:** Filter by result type: `type:ticket` for tickets or `type:comment` for comments.
- **dates:** Show tasks matching a date condition.
  - `dates:2026-10-03` Tasks with this exact due date.
  - `dates:<2026-10-03` Tasks due before.
  - `dates:>2026-10-03` Tasks due after.
  - `dates:in-range 2026-10-01..2026-10-07` Tasks within a date range.
  - `dates:overdue` Overdue tasks.
  - `dates:today` Tasks due today.
  - `dates:this-week` Tasks due in the current week.
  - `dates:later` Tasks due beyond the current week.
  - `dates:todays` Tasks due today or yesterday.
- **has:** Show tasks that have a value in a field.
  - `has:due-date` Tasks with a due date.
  - `has:attachment` Tasks with at least one attachment.
  - `has:comment` Tasks with at least one comment.
- **"exact phrase":** Match an exact phrase, for example `"bug report"`.
- **-word:** Exclude results containing a word, for example `-blocked`.

These operators work together; combine them, for example `from:alice label:urgent dates:>2026-10-03` to find urgent tasks created by Alice after a specific date.

Quoted phrases and `-word` exclusions stay plain text in the search box, rather than becoming coloured operator chips.

## Autocomplete

As you type, Hypertask suggests:

- **Filter names**: Type `la`, `fr`, or `is` to reveal `label:`, `from:`, and `is:` with ghost text. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> or <kbd>Enter</kbd> to accept.
- **Filter values**: After typing `from:` or `label:`, a dropdown shows people or labels. After typing `is:`, a dropdown shows states like `open`, `done`, and `archived`.
  - `priority:` suggests `urgent`, `high`, `medium`, and `low`.
  - `type:` suggests `ticket` and `comment`.
  - `has:` shows `attachment`, `comment`, and `due-date` options.
  - `dates:` shows presets: `today`, `this-week`, `last 7 days`, plus a date picker.
- **Filter types have unique colours**: `from:`/`@`, `assignee:`, and `commenter:` are purple; `in:`/`#` and `board:` are blue; `label:` is rose; `is:` and `priority:` are green; dates are amber; `has:` and `type:` are cyan. Slack-style operators autocomplete with the same colours as the other operators.

## Person name matching behavior

**Owner and QA preview:**

- **Typed person filters**: When you type a name for `from:`, `assignee:`, and currently `commenter:`, it matches every person you can see whose name or email contains that text, ignoring case and accents. For example, `from:valentin` finds Valentin Yeo and any account named valentinyeo; `assignee:yc` finds Yusuf C. and any name containing "yc" in the email. Using `-from:valentin` excludes all those matches.
- **People from the picker**: A person you select from the autocomplete list is matched exactly, so `from: Valentin Yeo` narrows to just that person.
- **Without the flag**: If fuzzy person matching is off, typed person filters require the exact full name and case-sensitive search.

<div class="asideInfo">
<small>Preview for owners and QA only. General release is scheduled after final QA sign-off on fuzzy matching for all users.</small>
</div>

## Tips panel

When the search bar is empty or focused, a <strong>tips panel</strong> lists every operator with an example and plain meaning. Tips include `priority:high`, `type:ticket`, `"exact phrase"`, and `-word`. Click any tip to insert it. Saved searches and recent searches also appear inside the tips panel.

## Keyboard navigation in search

- **Navigate suggestions**: Use ↓ (or <kbd>j</kbd>) and ↑ (or <kbd>k</kbd>) to move through values and tips without typing.
  - In empty search, <kbd>j</kbd>/<kbd>k</kbd> moves through tips.
  - In a typed query, <kbd>j</kbd>/<kbd>k</kbd> move through results while you type.
- **Accept a suggestion**: <kbd>Tab</kbd> or <kbd>Enter</kbd> inserts the pending value.
- **Escape**: Closes suggestions and drops focus from the search bar.
  - On search results, <kbd>Esc</kbd> returns you to your previous search term and its results, or to recent searches and tips when there is no previous search.
  - Esc never leaves you on a blank results page.
- **Open a result**: Put focus on a result row with arrows, then press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to open the task.

## Results while typing

Results appear while you type via debounced search. No need to press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to see matching tasks.

## Chips

After applying filters, clickable chips appear in the search bar. Click a chip's X to remove it. Clearing text keeps filter chips until you press <kbd>Backspace</kbd> one extra time.

**Board chips** now display the board icon and name (e.g., `board:inne`), with no extra `#` prefix.

When you type a filter operator such as `from:` or `assignee:` and select a person from the dropdown, the operator character is now absorbed into the chip itself. For example, selecting a person after typing `from valentin` results in a `from: Valentin Yeo` chip instead of leaving `from` and the person both visible.

**Board tabs behavior**: When the board-tab flags are enabled and all search results come from the same board, either because you filtered to one board or because results naturally returned from a single board, the row of board tabs is hidden to keep your attention focused on that board. If the search returns tasks from multiple boards, the tabs remain visible so you can switch between them from search results.

## People and board pickers

- **@ people picker**: Start typing `@` to select or create people.
- **# board picker**: Start typing `#` to select or create boards.

Pickers appear when typing a people or board-related operator such as `from:`, `assignee:`, or `in:`.

## New tasks appear immediately in search

<Aside type="tip">

Tasks created through the API now appear in search results right away without needing to update their title.

</Aside>

Previously, when you created tickets via the API without a title update, the search index would not reflect the new entries. Now, Hypertask updates the search index immediately after task creation, so the new tasks show up when you search.

To verify it’s live:

- Create a new task using the API or CLI with just a description.
- Switch to the search screen and use a keyword from the description to see the new task appear in results.
- No additional steps like editing the title are required.

This change applies to all API surfaces, including the MCP tools and REST endpoints, and makes search results consistent across all task creation flows.

<div class="asideInfo">
<small>Also fixed slow AI calls that were stalling due to fresh server startup. Slow calls now finish in half the time or less.</small>
</div>

<div class="asideInfo">
<small>Long pages and comments are now indexed for search. Previously very long or empty pages and comments were rejected by the AI service that generates search copies, and would not appear in results.</small>
</div>

# Search Screen
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/search-screen/

# Search Screen

The search screen provides a focused, keyboard-first way to find tasks across your board. It adopts a Superhuman-inspired design: a single aligned list of recent searches and tips, grey value completions (operator and values), and keyboard-driven workflows while deferring results until selection or Enter.

## Enhanced search preview: Owner+QA only

This enhanced search screen is a strict preview available to the Owner and QA roles. It is not a general release and does not require any minimum activity threshold. If you see the normal search UI, ensure you are on a checked board and the search preview flag is enabled for your account or team.

## Layout and structure

Top-level search shows a consistent list:

- **Recent searches**: A single list of your most recent searches.
- **Tips**: Helpful hints below recent searches (operator shortcuts, example queries).
- **AI panel**: Fixed on the right side, leaving the core search interface on the left.

No floating boxes. The suggestions list is full-width and aligned with the search box on desktop and mobile.

- **Mobile board tabs**: Under the search box, board tabs sit clearly above the bottom navigation, tapable with ample spacing and swipe-friendly when many boards exist.

- **Desktop**: Board tabs follow the same layout, for the same filter behavior across devices.

## Empty and loaded states

- **Empty search**: Recent searches (or none, if you have none) appear once, then tips below them. The AI panel stays fixed on the right side; the left side is free for search only.
- **Loaded search**: After selecting a suggestion or pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd>, aligned results appear under the suggestions list. Results do not start loading until you accept a suggestion or press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.

## Grey inline value completion

As you type, the inline suggestions box shows:

- **Top suggestion**: Completed in grey inside the list. Accept with <kbd>Tab</kbd>.
- **Operators**: Hinted inline (e.g., <code>el:</code> hints <code>label:</code>).
- **Values**: Top value preview in grey (e.g., <code>from:mal</code> shows <code>Malcolm Stern</code>).

This applies to common value types: people (names + emails), labels, boards. Results do not trigger while you type; they load only after you pick a suggestion or press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.

**Example**: Type <code>from:val</code>; the top suggestion <code>Valentin Yeo</code> appears in grey; select it with <kbd>Tab</kbd> to trigger a board fetch and show results.

## Tips panel

Under recent searches, tips explain operators the first time you open search:

- <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd> — open command palette.
- <code>from:</code>, <code>assignee:</code>, <code>in:</code>, <code>label:</code>, <code>is:</code>, <code>dates:</code>, <code>has:</code>, <code>priority:</code> — field modifiers.
- <code>"quoted phrase"</code> — exact phrase match.
- <code>-word</code> — exclude tasks with a word or phrase.
- Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> on an inline value to accept it; choose Ask AI, operators, people, labels, or boards.

## Keyboard shortcuts (search UI)

- <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd> — open command palette.
- <kbd>Enter</kbd> — apply selected suggestion and load results.
- <kbd>Tab</kbd> — accept and grey the top inline suggestion and load results.
- <kbd>Shift+Tab</kbd> — previous suggestion.
- <kbd>Esc</kbd> — clear or dismiss panels.

## Sample workflows

1. Click the search box or press <kbd>/</kbd>. Empty state: recent searches and tips appear.
2. Type a partial term or operator (e.g., <code>from:mal</code>). Inline completion shows the top value in grey. Results do not load yet.
3. Select a suggestion with <kbd>Tab</kbd> (or hover & click). Results load under the suggestions list.
4. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to clear and return to the recents/tips layout; results are removed.

## Status notes

- This new search screen replaces the live results from the previous iconic live-results approach and works behind the existing search flags.
- Verified live for Owner and QA; full release plan to widen the flag is out of scope for this documentation.

# Skills
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/skills/

import { Aside, Card, CardGrid, Tabs, TabItem, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Skills let you cluster related tasks, projects, and workflows around shared expertise. A skill can be anything: a domain, a technology, or a role. You can assign skills to people, filter any task list by skill, or use skills as metadata in saved views.

<Aside type="tip">
Use skills to surface specialized work: "React", "Schema Design", "Customer Research", or "Onboarding". Assign a skill to a person, and watch it surface in searches, assignments, and saved views.
</Aside>

## Save a workflow from AI chat

Ask chat to create a skill:

> Turn this session into a skill.

Or describe a workflow you want saved.
Review its name, slug, trigger, instructions and scope.
Choose personal scope or the current board.
Confirm the draft to save it.
Or request edits or reject the draft.
Edits need another preview before saving.
Nothing saves until you confirm the draft.
If the slug exists, approve an update instead.

Use `/slug` in chat, comments, or Task Writer.
Ctrl+J also supports saved skills.

## Create & assign skills

Skills are scoped to: personal (for you), project (for a board), or team (for all members of that team). When you assign a skill to a person, the assignment is also scoped to the skill’s scope, so a team-level skill appears in each project’s skill list.

<Steps>

1. **Open Skill management**
   - Use the **Ctrl+K** command palette and search for **"Skills"**, or go to the **Settings > Skills** page.

2. **Create a skill**
   - Click **New Skill**.
   - Give it a name (e.g., "Python" or "Design System").
   - Optionally add a description.
   - Choose the scope:
     - **Personal** — skill available only to you.
     - **Project** — skill available on a specific board/project.
     - **Team** — skill available to all members of your team, regardless of project.

3. **Assign a person**
   - On the skill card, click **Assign People**.
   - Search for a team member and add them.
   - Assignments are scoped: a personal skill assignment is only visible to you; a project assignment is only visible on that project’s board.

4. **Backlog/assign tasks by skill**
   - Filter a task list by skill using the skill picker.
   - Or assign a skill to a task to tag it for later filtering or reporting.
   - Saved views can also explicitly filter by skill.

</Steps>

## Run a skill from a ticket comment

Start writing a comment on any ticket. Type `/`, then choose an available skill. Use Enter or click to choose the skill.

The AI chat sidebar opens with its answer. The skill reads the ticket and your draft. Your comment stays editable and unposted.

### /prototype skill

You can now create a **/prototype** skill to define a shared prototype format across agents and collaboration tools. When someone inserts a prototype with this skill:

- The prototype becomes clickable in comments and AI chat.
- The default action is to open and display the prototype in the same context.
- The prototype’s slug is inserted into comments and prompts, making it easy to reference and reuse.
- If the prototype has its own action URL, the UI presents standard context‑appropriate actions:
  - **Comment composer**: click the prototype card to insert its slug; opening the prototype works the same way as other skills.
  - **AI chat**: pick /prototype from the command menu, then engage with the prototype in the same way you would any other skill.

<Aside type="tip">
Use the /prototype skill to streamline reference workflows: embed consistent embed URLs and referenceable slugs for MP4s, PNGs, and hosted prototypes. Agents and collaborators can open, inspect, and reference them without leaving their current flow.
</Aside>

### Use a skill when writing a new task

Press **Ctrl+J**, start your note with the skill's slug (for example `/deeper`), and send it. The AI writes the task using that skill, then opens the task with the AI chat.

As soon as you type `/`, a skill picker opens under your cursor, the same one the AI task writer shows. Keep typing to filter it, use the arrow keys to move, and press **Enter** or **Tab** to insert the skill. **Escape** closes only the picker, so your note stays open.

The chat's first message tells you which skill shaped the task and what changed compared with your note. It then lists concerns, ideas and follow-up questions for this task. Click a suggested question below the message to ask it in the same chat.

If no skill was used, or the skill was edited or removed after the task was written, the chat shows the usual short intro instead.

### Example agent use case

An agent that manages design reviews might:

- Use the /prototype skill to indicate designs under review.
- In a comment, insert the prototype slug to surface the linked prototype card.
- Ready the prototype for quick, context‑appropriate opening by teammates.

### Keyboard workflow

Quickly assign or filter by skill using your keyboard:

- **Ctrl+K** — Command palette; start typing **"Skill"** to find:
  - **Skills** — Open Skill management.
  - **Filter tasks by skill** — Pop up the skill selector.

- Use the skill picker in a board or task detail to click or navigate with arrow keys to select skills.

### Data model (for integrators)

- **Scope** — `personal` | `project` | `team`.
- A skill on a board applies only when that board is opened.
- A project skill applies across all boards in that project.
- A team skill applies automatically to all boards that your team owns.

<CardGrid>
  <Card title="Keyboard Shortcuts" href="/features/keyboard-shortcuts/">
    Use keyboard workflows to surf tasks and filter by skill.
  </Card>
  <Card title="CLI Reference" href="/cli/reference/">
    Manage skills from the terminal with full CRUD and import.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Agent Workflows" href="/mcp/workflows/">
    Patterned ways agents can pick up and complete work scoped by skill.
  </Card>
</CardGrid>

# Slack
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/slack/

The Slack app is not available yet.

What Hypertask connects to today is on [Integrations](/features/integrations/).

# Smart Labels
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/smart-labels/

import { Aside, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

A **smart label** is a label with an AI prompt attached. The AI reads each task and keeps the label assigned to the ones that match your prompt — so a filter or saved view on that label becomes a **prompt-defined view** ("show me small quick wins", "everything touching billing") instead of a hard filter.

## Creating a smart label

<Steps>

1. Open the label modal on a task (or the Manage Tags screen) and type a new label name.

2. Fill the **"Smart label — AI keeps this label on matching tasks"** field with a plain-language description of which tasks belong, e.g. `Small, low-risk changes shippable in under an hour`.

3. Save. The AI immediately classifies the board's existing tasks (up to 500) and labels the matches. Smart labels show a sparkle icon in label lists.

</Steps>

## How it stays current

- **New tasks** are classified when created.
- **Edited tasks** are re-classified when their title or description changes.
- **Prompt changes** re-run classification for the whole board.

Label changes made by the AI appear in the task's activity feed as HyperAI.

<Aside type="note">
The latest AI verdict wins: if you manually add or remove a smart label on a task, the AI may reverse it the next time that task is re-classified. Describe exceptions in the prompt instead ("NOT: schema changes").
</Aside>

## Using it as a view

Filter the board by the smart label (or save that filter as a view) and you have a Kanban/table that only shows AI-matched tasks.

## Details

- Prompts are capped at 1000 characters; setting one requires project membership.
- Classification runs on a fast, low-cost model; usage is logged like other AI features.
- Backfill covers the 500 oldest tasks per run; newer activity is always classified.
- The parser tolerates extra text around the list of labels that the model returns, so smart labels classify more reliably and show fewer parsing errors.

# Superhuman-Style Snippets
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/superhuman-snippets/

import { Aside, Steps, Card, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Quickly insert common responses, templates, and commands into tasks and comments with keyboard shortcuts inspired by Superhuman.

<Aside type="tip">
Mastering these shortcuts keeps you in the flow. Try memorizing three to five for your most common use cases, then gradually expand.
</Aside>

---

### Insert predefined text with `.`

Type a period (`.`) at the start of a task description or comment body to open a menu of predefined snippets. Common examples include:

| Shortcut | Inserts |
|----------|---------|
| `.ack` | Confirmation acknowledgement |
| `.hire remind` | Automated hiring process reminder template |
| `.contact patch format` | Standard format for requesting a patch |
| `.contact address data` | Request for all address details |
| `.oro` | Orchestration request |
| `.oro test` | Orchestration test request |
| Orchestration mention | Appointment scheduling |
| `oro reminder` | Orchestration reminder |
| `oro reminder 10m` | Orchestration reminder at a specific time |
| `oro reminder 10m now` | Orchestration reminder at a specific time with a current timestamp |
| `oro reminderbooking` | Orchestration reminder booking |
| `oro reminder:thanks` | Orchestration reminder closing |
| `oro test reminder` | Orchestration test reminder |
| `oro reminder success` | Orchestration reminder success message |

<Aside type="note">
Snippets are organized by category. Type a few letters to narrow down suggestions, or scroll through the full list.
</Aside>

---

### Create or open snippets with `<kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>`

Press `<kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>` while writing a task or comment to open the command palette. Search for **"Create snippet"** or **"Perform snippet"** to use or save snippets.

**How to create a snippet:**

1. Type the content you want to reuse — a common response, template, or command.
2. Press `<kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>`.
3. Search for **"Create snippet"** and select it.
4. Give the snippet a short name (e.g., "Acknowledgement template" or "Patch request").
5. The page reloads into a fresh full-page snippet view. From there, save the snippet by using the appropriate command or button.

**How to use an existing snippet:**

1. Press `<kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>`.
2. Search for **"Perform snippet"** followed by the snippet name.
3. Typing the snippet name directly (e.g., `.oro`) also inserts the content immediately.

<Aside type="tip">
Say you frequently write a standard acknowledgement like "Thank you for the update. I've noted this and will get back to you by [time].". Instead of typing it every time, save it as a snippet and insert with `.` whenever you need it.
</Aside>

---

### Find and manage snippets

The command palette lists all available snippets, including a search filter to find specific text quickly. Saved snippets appear in your local snippet store and are persisted across sessions.

# Table View
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/table-view/

import { Aside, CardGrid, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## Overview

Table view gives you a grid-based way to organize and manage tasks, similar to Notion or Linear. It adapts to the columns you need and keeps your layout preferences saved across sessions.

**Horizontal scrolling across all columns:** When a table's columns exceed the available width on your device (for example on narrow windows or very wide column sets), a visible horizontal scrollbar appears. This lets you scroll to see remaining columns in the grid without obscured headers or black space, ensuring you can reach every column in the row set.

**Unsaved sort states and saved views:** Sorting the table creates an unsaved view. An "orange Save view + Reset" indication appears in the header. Press Save to capture the sort configuration as a saved view, or Reset to discard it. Existing saved views reopen the table pre-sorted.

**Multiselect via Shift+E:** Press Shift+E to select the current row and add it to the selection set. From any multi-selected row, press Shift+E repeatedly to accumulate or extend the selection for bulk actions.

## Mouse-Accessible New Task Control

At the right end of a table's top row sits a quiet ghost button that creates new tasks. It provides a mouse-based way to add tasks without leaving the grid:

**Behavior:**
- With quick entry enabled, click **+ New task** to open a compact title field for the selected column.
- Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to save each task and keep the empty field open for the next title. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to close it; reopening restores an unsaved title.
- Press <kbd>C</kbd> when you need the full task creator instead.
- Hidden from cross-board My Tasks tables.
- Uses only theme tokens so it matches your current customization.

**Accessibility:**
- Keyboard-focusable (tab into it, and Shift+Tab out).
- Excluded from the cross-board My Tasks table.
- Highlighted on hover and focus to make its purpose clear without taking up screen space.

## Adaptive layout

Table view automatically adjusts to the columns you're using:

- **Flexible title column:** The title column flexes to fill the remaining horizontal space; its width is a minimum, so you can use full width without nested scrolling or cramped visibility.
- **Flexible columns:** The table layout derives from your visible sections and columns, so you see the most relevant information without cramped spacing.
- **Full-title row behavior:** Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to open a task focused on its description; the task detail view updates inline within the row, preserving the table layout without needing to leave the grid.

## Excel-style frozen panes

When you scroll horizontally across a table with many columns, the **Ticket** and **Title** columns stay visible while you view the rest of the grid. This frozen-pane behavior mimics Excel, ensuring the identifier and description of each row are always visible:

- **Ticket column**: Stays fixed on the far left, showing the task number consistently across scrolling
- **Title column**: Stays visible to the right of the Ticket column, keeping the task's primary label in view

This remains true for table layouts, board table views, and subtask tables, so you can always identify rows regardless of how far right you need to scroll.

## Column picker

Customize your table view with the column picker:

1. Press <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> and search for "Configure table" or "Column picker".
2. Select which columns to display and hide.
3. Click **APPLY** to persist your selection across sessions.

The palette in table view is the same one you get on the board, so board commands such as sorting, filter match mode, and board time tracking are all available without switching layouts.

Your column choices are saved per user, so each team member can have their own table layout.

<Aside type="tip">

The column picker and table layout are per-user settings. You can show or hide any column without deleting it, and changes apply immediately to your view.

</Aside>

## Move a task to another section

Drag any row onto another section's card and the task moves into that section. The row is the drag handle and the section card is the drop target, so nothing extra appears on screen; the card you are over takes the normal hover highlight.

Dragging is off in two cases, because a drop would be meaningless or wrong:

- **A column sort is active.** Rows render as one flat list with no section groups to drop into.
- **On /my-tasks.** Rows are grouped by due time or by board, not by a board column, so a move would target the wrong thing.

## The Created column

Turn on **Created** in the column picker to see when each task was opened, and click the header twice to sort oldest first.

It shows a real date rather than an age, because **On board** already gives you the age in days and "412d" does not tell you when something started. Dates outside the current year keep their year (`12 Sep, 2025`), so an old task can never be mistaken for a recent one. Sorting runs on the underlying timestamp, not the displayed text.

## Drag to reorder and resize

Drag columns directly to reorder them in place; the order stays in sync with the Table columns picker dropdown. Drag the column edge to resize each column to your preferred width. The title column remains locked as the leftmost column, with ticket detail keyed by title; the title column still flexes to fill leftover width.

### AMOLED hover and drag

On AMOLED displays, table resize handles are more visible:

- **Hover:** a 2px purple accent line appears on the edge while hovering over a column boundary.
- **Drag:** the guide line extends the full height of the table to show the planned column width.
- **Header feedback:** hovering any column header shows faint separators between columns for better discoverability of the grid.

### Excel-style resize model

Table view resize now follows an Excel-like model that gives you predictable control over column sizes:

- **First resize:** On your first resize of any column, the Title column's flex width is frozen at its rendered pixel width, making it fixed thereafter. All other columns reset to auto-fit width and wait for your next resize action.
- **Subsequent resizes:** After the initial resize, dragging any column edge follows your cursor 1:1 as you expand or shrink the column.
- **Wider grab strip:** Resize handles include a 12px wide grab strip that makes one-touch sizing easier on touch devices or small windows.
- **Reset to default:** Use the Table columns picker (e.g., ...) and click **Reset to default** (or Reset to original) to restore the original auto-fit width for all columns.

This Excel-style resize behavior ensures clearer feedback and deliberate resizing flow, especially when setting up a stable table layout.

## Advanced column configuration

Open the Configure table modal for more control over your table setup:

1. Press <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> and search for "Configure table".
2. In the column picker, click the ⋮ or **edit** icon next to "Columns" to open advanced options.
3. Choose from additional columns:

**Visibility options**
- **Visible columns** — toggle columns on and off without permanently deleting them. The table updates instantly.

**Additional columns**
- **Tags** — render label pills from your tags/column. Shows up to 3 pills, with "+N" expanding the rest. Pill clicks jump to other tasks with the same tag.
- **Comments** — count of comments per task with hover preview (up to 3 lines). Click to open the task.
- **Created** — full timestamp of task creation (e.g., "Jul 26, 2026 at 10:42 AM"). Click to view original creation.
- **Column** — which board section or column a task belongs to. Click to jump to that section on the board.
- **Status** — copy of the board column name for card-based views (e.g., "Done", "In Progress", "Review").
- **Stale** — indicator of task staleness when the board staleness toggle is enabled. Shows up to 7 days amber/red signal, empty when fresh, and hidden when the toggle is off. Click to sort by staleness (sorting column appears between Due and Updated).

**Actions**
- Drag columns by their grip handle to reorder them.
- Drag a column edge to resize to your preferred width.
- Click **Reset to default** or **Reset to original** to restore the original auto-fit layout.

<Aside type="note">

"Reset to default" or "Reset to original" places the Status column immediately after Title and moves Updated header to the right.

</Aside>

### Sort-Driven Columns

While sorting, the View engine adds columns to improve clarity:

- **Status column:** Appears immediately after Title, matching the board column name (e.g., Done, In Progress, Review). It hides when the sort is cleared.
- **Stale column (optional):** Only appears in the headers when sorting by staleness and the board staleness toggle is on. It hides again when staleness sorting is cleared or the toggle is off.

These additions keep the table focused around the sorted criteria without overwhelming you with every board field.

## Keyboard shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> | Open the command palette. Table view has the full board palette, including the column picker |
| <kbd>Shift+F</kbd> | Toggle focused search on the board |
| <kbd>W</kbd> | Start or stop the timer for the selected task |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Open task focused on description and keep the table layout |
| <kbd>Shift+E</kbd> | Select (or extend selection of) the current table row for bulk actions |

## Sorting behavior

When you sort a table, the experience tightens to show you the most useful columns at once:

- **Status column auto-shows** — as soon as you sort, a Status column appears immediately after the Title column, matching the board column name (e.g., Done, AI Review, Bugs). The column hides again when you clear the sort.
- **Updated header right-aligned** — the Updated header stays visibly right-aligned over the rest of the column headers.
- **Stale column option** — when sorting by staleness, a Stale column appears between Due and Updated headers. It hides when staleness sorting is cleared or when the board staleness toggle is off.

This pattern keeps the table focused on the sorted criteria without overwhelming you with every board field.

## Use cases

Table view is great for:

- **Analyzing lots of tasks:** See many items at once in a compact grid without losing readability.
- **Comparing priorities:** Side-by-side visibility of priority, size, and due dates.
- **Quick filtering:** Combine visibility filters with your column choices to surface the exact set of tasks you need.
- **Tracking staleness:** Use the Stale column to identify tasks that haven't been updated recently, especially on boards with staleness detection enabled.
- **Bulk work:** Combine multiselect with bulk actions (e.g., Move, Archive) for rapid processing.

## Scroll positions

**Full-height scroll container:** The scroll container reaches the bottom of the window, so the horizontal scrollbar stays pinned at the bottom regardless of row count. This ensures stable navigation when working with rows of any size.

# Tasks
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/tasks/

---
title: "Tasks"
description: "Create, assign, and manage tasks with rich fields, priorities, relations, and subtasks."
---

import { CardGrid, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

# Tasks

A task represents a unit of work that can be assigned, progressed, and tracked. It supports rich fields, priority levels, relationships, and subtasks.

## My Tasks

**My Tasks** is your personal task list across boards. By default it shows tasks assigned to you.

The list groups by due time: **Overdue**, **Today**, **This week**, **Later**, and **No due date**. Overdue stays at the top. Use **Group** to switch back to board groups. Saved My Tasks views remember the choice. One row of tabs sits on top, your saved views. Use **Scope** to narrow the list to some boards, and **Group: Board** to see one section per board with its count.

### Scope in My Tasks
<span class="label label--brand">Improvement</span> The **Scope** button in My Tasks and the standard **Scope** command in <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> now open the same board picker list. The panel has been redesigned to match the board picker you use throughout the app, with search and standard keyboard navigation for quick filtering and selection. The previous, custom implementation has been replaced with the consistent board picker experience.

### Bulk selection and actions on My Tasks
You can select multiple tasks in the **My Tasks** view using the keyboard shortcut **G**, followed by **M**, to enter multi-select mode. This mirrors the selection behavior from the Kanban board for a consistent workflow.

Once in multi-select mode:
- **Verify your selection**: Each task you want to act on is checked. If viewing a filtered list, only tasks that are both checked and visible are included in the action.
- **Apply bulk actions**: The following actions are available at the bottom of the list:
  - Archive
  - Assign
  - Label
  - Move to column
  - Delete
- **Unselect**: Press **G** again or press **U** to exit multi-select mode.

Selected rows persist until you commit an action, so you can review the working set before bulk-actioning multiple tasks.

> **Tip**: The selection model matches the way you select tasks in Kanban, so if you are comfortable bulk-archiving or moving tasks on a board, the pattern transfers directly to My Tasks.

### Tasks you're snoozed on
To temporarily hide tasks from your My Tasks view, set a **snooze**. When you snooze until a date:
- The task no longer appears in My Tasks until that date passes
- The snooze date sets a calendar reminder so you can resurface the task later

A snooze is per task and independent of other views. Tasks remain otherwise accessible from boards, calendars, and saved views.

### Saved views
You can create and manage saved views on My Tasks to customize what you see. These views support:
- **Full filtering**: Filter by title, assignee, priority, due date, labels, and more. Filter options match the Kanban board filter menu, so you can use familiar screen-level controls directly on My Tasks.
- **Sorting**: Sort by any of the same fields, with priority as the primary sort key.
- **Board selection**: Show tasks from one board or across multiple boards.
- **Done columns hidden by default**: Done columns are hidden within each view to focus on active work.

Saved views persist at the account level and can be used as templates for board filter setups.

### How it works
When you toggle a filter, sort order, or board, your selection is saved with the view. The next time you open that view, the settings are applied automatically. You can create multiple views for example, one for active prioritized tasks, one for a specific project, or any combination that matches your workflow.

To create a saved view, open My Tasks and use the view toolbar to pick filters and sorting options, then select **Save view**. The view appears in the saved views list alongside system views like **Involvement** and **All tasks**.

### Excluding tasks you don't need
To hide distracting or temporary tasks:
- Use **View filters** to show or hide assignments, priorities, or tags that don't match your current focus.
- Create and pin a custom view with the exact criteria you want to see.
- Review tasks by tag or priority and archive or move them away when no longer relevant.

> **Note:** Saved views are scoped to the current team. Cross-board filters and sorting are supported, so you can see, for example, all high-priority inbox tasks across all boards in a single custom view.

### All Tasks view
The **All Tasks** view provides an at-a-glance overview of every active task across the board. It builds split views for each board section (To Do, In Progress, Done, etc.) from a single source of truth.

To access this view, navigate to the board and select **All Tasks** from the view toolbar.

### How All Tasks works
All Tasks uses a single fetch pass that loads rows once and builds board splits from those rows. As a result:
- Each board sees its own split of the task list.
- Quiet boards do not lose splits in favor of busy boards.
- The view is stable and deterministic across sessions.

### Drawing from multiple streams
Since All Tasks is board-wide, it aggregates tasks from all active columns and sections, making it useful for a quick health check or high-level tracking when you need to see everything that matters—not just what's pinned or currently in one section.

**Note:** Unlike **My Tasks** saved views, All Tasks does not automatically filter out onboarding, demo, template, and staging content, so those tasks may appear in the list. For visibility filtering, see [Board & Subtask Visibility](/features/board-visibility/).

### Search filters
When searching within a board or in saved views, you can now narrow results using search operators on fields:
- **from:** Restrict to tasks created by a specific user.
- **assignee:** Restrict to tasks assigned to a specific person.
- **in:** Restrict to tasks in a board, section, or column.
- **label:** Restrict to tasks with a specific label.
- **is:** Narrow by task type; for example, `is:card` to show only standard cards.
- **dates:** Show tasks with dates matching a condition (by default, **by due**), or filter by due date ranges.
  - `dates:2026-09-30` For tasks with that exact due date.
  - `dates:<2026-09-30` For tasks due before.
  - `dates:>2026-09-30` For tasks due after.
  - `dates:in-range 2026-09-01..2026-09-30` For tasks due within the range.
  - `dates:overdue` For tasks marked overdue.
  - `dates:today` For tasks due today.
  - `dates:this-week` For tasks due within the current week.
  - `dates:later` For tasks due later than the current week.
  - `dates:todays` For tasks due on today and the day prior.
- **has:** Show tasks that have a value in a field; for example, `has:due-date` for tasks that have a due date (including empty values) or `has:assignee` for tasks that have someone assigned.
- Combining multiple operators is supported—for example, `from:alice label:urgent dates:>2026-09-30` to find urgent tasks created by Alice after a certain date.

To apply search filters:
1. Open **Kanban** or **Table View**.
2. On the board header (or in the saved view toolbar), select **Filter**.
3. Choose a field and an operator, then enter a value or pick from the options.
4. Repeat for additional filters to narrow the list.

Search filters apply at the board level in Kanban and in saved views. The available operators depend on the board's configuration.

### Chips in the search bar
<span class="label label--brand">New</span> The search bar includes:
- **Chips**: Select or refine filters after your search, then click to apply chips. Click the × on a chip to remove it.
- @ people picker: Start typing the @ symbol to select or create people.
- # board picker: Start typing # to select or create boards.

## My Tasks toolbar
<span class="label label--brand">Behavior change</span> The My Tasks toolbar now uses icon-only controls with tooltips for Involvement, Columns, Scope, Filters, Sort, and Group. Active controls turn blue like Kanban, and Group shows its current choice. Overdue tooltips on red counts now appear over each overdue item. The toolbar also uses the same Save view and Reset controls as Kanban board views.

From the **Ctrl+K** command palette, you can still use **Save view as** to create a saved view, and **Reset view** to revert My Tasks to its default set of built-in filters. Keyboard shortcuts like **Ctrl+S** and **Ctrl+R** no longer open popovers on the board; they now open the Save view and Reset dialogs respectively.

This change makes view management across My Tasks and other board views more consistent, and ensures My Tasks mirrors the primary board interface.

## Creating a task
From a board or inbox, click **New task** (or use the keyboard shortcut **Ctrl+N** / <kbd>Cmd+N</kbd>). This opens the task creator with the following top-level sections:
- **Title**: The name or headline of the work.
- **Description**: Optional text explaining what to do.
- **Assignees**: One or more members to get notified and held accountable.
- **Sections & Columns**: Drag the task to a section or use the section picker dropdown.
- **Due date**: Pick a date or use predictive phrases like "tomorrow," "next week," or relative periods.
- **Priority**: Choose Low, Medium, or High.
- **Estimated time**: Optionally specify hours or a low-high range if needed.

Use **Write with AI** (**Ctrl+K** / <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd>, or the command palette) in the description area to turn a brief task idea into a fleshed-out task.

### New Task creator
<span class="label label--brand">New</span> The task creator window (formerly the "Compose" button) can be opened from any view with **Ctrl+J** / <kbd>Cmd+J</kbd> and is now live for everyone. The window behaves like a task creator with Search and New Task tabs, Ctrl+K and Ctrl+J tooltips, and Tab/Shift+Tab switching. It retains your old window size and grows as you type, and the New Task button is renamed to **New Task**.

On desktop, click the primary **New Task** plus button in the left sidebar to open the same window. Expand the sidebar to see its label. Hover shows **Ctrl+J**, or **Cmd+J** on Mac. Mobile keeps its existing new-task button.

### Edit a task with AI
<span class="label label--brand">New</span> Click **Edit with AI** under a task's description to open the AI chat in the sidebar on that task. It asks "How do you want to edit this task?" and offers ready-made requests: **Rewrite in plain words**, **Shorten the title**, **Add acceptance criteria**, **Split into sub-tasks**, and **Turn the error log into steps to reproduce**. Pick one or type your own, and the chat updates the task in place. The AI button in the description and comment editor opens the same chat. On an open task, **Ctrl+J** / <kbd>Cmd+J</kbd> still opens the New Task window.

### AI writer failure reasons
<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> When the AI writer fails to generate a task, the **Ctrl+J New Task** box and the AI Task Writer now show the real failure reason instead of hiding it; your note is still saved as a task. If AI generation is not available, the text you entered appears without modification. This applies to task creation from boards, the inbox, and description editing in task details.

## Field validation
Some fields are type-checked before submission. For example, the **ranking** parameter must be a string; passing a number will fail with an error.

## OAuth connection flow
When Hypertask connects to a board from an external site or app, Hypertask now shows an **approve screen** first. The screen names the connector and the exact site that will receive access, letting you confirm before any access is granted.

This prevents a signed-in user from inadvertently granting external sites access to their entire board without prior approval.

## Managing task details
Open a task to view and edit all its fields. Unsupported columns or fields may be hidden based on your team's board configuration.

### Priorities
Assign a clear priority (Low, Medium, or High) to reflect the task's importance and replacement cost. Higher priorities should be shown ahead of lower ones in lists, table view, and filters.

### Assignees
- Added assignees trigger notifications to the task's assignees. If no assignee is specified, the task is unassigned.
- Workers can have their own assignee field, tracked separately from human assignees. Workers appear in the Relationships section under the *Workers* relation type.

### Due dates
Click a date to pick another date or remove it. The date affects due date pickers and filter views. Predictive phrases like "tomorrow," "next week," and relative periods also persist.

### Estimated time
Type hours or a low-high range for time-tracking integration.

### Section & column
Drag tasks between sections to change their column. This can trigger auto-assign rules if configured. In Table view, you can also drag any row onto another section's card; the row is the drag handle, the section card is the drop target, and the change surfaces immediately in both views (Column sort must be off for this to work; on /my-tasks, rows are grouped by time or board, so dragging doesn't target a section directly).

### Description edition UX
To edit the task description:
- On desktop: Click or tap the description area, then edit.
- Mobile: Double-tap the description to open the editor; a single tap remains in read mode.

If you are the **Task Reporter** (see below), you can edit the description directly. Only the Task Reporter can edit the description.

### Task Reporter
With the **Task Reporter**, anyone on the task can update the task description directly. The Task Reporter indicator visually appears alongside comment headers, making it clear who has opened the description for editing just like comments.

### Permissions
- **Task Reporter** is available to any human assignee or worker on a task. The feature is not available for closed tasks.
- When you open the description in edit mode, you become the **Task Reporter** for that task.
- Only the Task Reporter can edit the description. This prevents concurrent edits and restores the semantic meaning of "owner of the description field".
- If you close the description without saving any changes, the status clears and the next person to open it becomes the Task Reporter.

This model ensures a clear ownership of the description field, similar to comment ownership, which helps teams coordinate around tasks without stepping on each other's work.

Note: While you are the Task Reporter, you cannot switch to another task description edit until the current edit state closes, preserving a single active description edit at a time.

### Saved attachments
- To remove an attachment, open the description in edit mode, click the attachment you want to remove, and save. Only the items you deselect will be removed; remaining attachments are preserved as one copy each.

<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> A previous bug caused the wrong attachment files to be saved when removing items from a description. When you had two or more description files attached, removing one would incorrectly save a duplicate of the other file. This is now fixed so that always only one copy of each remaining attachment is saved.

<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> Deleting a task no longer creates an invalid undoable state. Undo is now always possible when restoring from deletion, ensuring tasks can be fully recovered and the undo system behaves consistently.

<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> Undo functionality has been consolidated under a single restoring rule. This ensures that restoring tasks after deletion behaves the same whether you use the Undo button or Ctrl+Z, with consistent behavior tracked through the board's undo history.

### Agent lease interactions
When you make manual changes to a task—"moving, assigning, unassigning, archiving, or deleting"—Hypertask cancels any active agent lease on that task and persists the change. Human modifications take priority over agent tasks, but agent-versus-agent collision protection remains in place. This ensures your task updates are never blocked by an agent while you're working.

## Task detail view
Open a task to see:
- Header with title, status section, assignees, workers, priority, and due date.
- Description area with optional attachments.
- Sections: Comments, Relations, Subtasks, Times, and Pages.
- Task Reporter indicator marking who can edit the description.
- **Top bar** with instant navigation and actions:
  - ← **Back to task** — Settings-style back button for navigation. On mobile, the back control matches the app's mobile back style with normal side spacing, making it easy to tap and fully visible up to 390px wide.
  - **Save** — Only right-aligned action remaining in the top bar; **Delete** is now moved to the **Undo** action in the Actions section.

### Linked pull requests
Tasks can link to GitHub pull requests. The pull request section displays each linked PR with its status:
- **Open, Merged, Closed**: Show the current status as reported by GitHub.
- **Last observed**: The last-known status before the page loads.
- **Fetching...**: Indicates a background refresh is in progress.

<span class="label label--brand">Improvement</span> Tasks with linked PRs now show any saved PR status immediately—Open, Merged, or Closed—without waiting for GitHub to respond. Queries to GitHub run in parallel in the background and update the panel once the fetch completes, keeping the page fast and responsive. If you navigate away and come back, the PR panel refreshes again to stay current.

This change eliminates wait times for tasks with linked PRs and provides an instant-open experience even when GitHub fetches are slower than usual.

<span class="label label--brand">Security</span> Hypertask now verifies that incoming PR updates come from known GitHub accounts before accepting them. By default, this restriction applies only to board 15. Except for board 15, an updated PR can link to any public repository, and the update is accepted as long as it originates from a trusted GitHub account. For board 15, only PR updates from three specified accounts are permitted: Valentin Yeo and two others configured by the board team. This prevents unauthorized actors from creating, moving, or commenting on tasks in board 15 via external PRs.

### Comments
The comment thread shows all comments on the task. By default, when you open a task with comments, the newest comment remains expanded so you can see the latest conversation.

<span class="label label--brand">Link handling</span> Plain web addresses in ticket descriptions and comments (http:// or https://) are automatically transformed into clickable links. Detects addresses based on recognized URL patterns, ensuring links in work notes and teammate discussions remain navigable on both desktop and mobile.

<span class="label label--brand">Performance improvement</span> When you open a task, comments now load once instead of twice. The initial SSR data used as the starting point, with React Query configured to skip a second fetch if the data is fresh. This eliminates redundant data handling and speeds up task loads: repeat visits are now approximately 0.6 seconds faster. New and edited comments still appear automatically without a reload, and realtime invalidation, reconnect reconciliation, and window-focus refresh continue to work as expected.

<span class="label label--brand">Improvement</span> Long task pages and comment threads now send their initial snapshot only once, reducing data copies and decoding passes. Repeat visit times drop from roughly 2.2 seconds to about 0.6 seconds. The change applies to tasks with many comments or long descriptions and focuses on the initial load speed, preserving all existing behavior for navigation, real-time updates, and comment handling.

<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> The comment box on ticket pages is now positioned immediately below the last comment instead of appearing in the middle of the task. It previously moved under the task description, causing the interface to split the comment content unnaturally. The comment section now renders after other content and before the top bar, keeping comments at the bottom of the page as expected.

<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> A shared comment link now opens on that comment instead of the ticket top, with the comment visible on screen on both desktop and mobile. The link scrolls directly to the referenced comment when you open it—for example, from Slack or email—making it easier to reference specific points in a conversation. This fix improves navigation for long threads with hundreds of comments and helps ticket descriptions stay readable even on narrow phones.

### Actions
Common actions include:
- **Back**: Navigate back to the board using the ← Back to task button.
- **Move**: Relocate the task to a different section, board, or project.
- **Duplicate**: Create a copy with the same fields. When duplicating a task, the new task includes the full description and can be copied to another board in one step (see board-level Duplicate in the [Boards & Sections](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/boards/) docs).
- **Archive**: Hide the task from current views while keeping it in the archive.
- **Delete**: Permanently remove the task. Undo appears on the notification after deletion, clicking **Undo** restores the task to its previous column and keeps it available for future edits. For bulk deletions, undo restores all affected tasks together and still works with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> / <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd>.

<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> Opening a ticket now downloads its details once, and board cards stay up to date. Before this fix, opening a task from the board or by its link would trigger 2 to 3 redundant data fetches.

<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> On mobile, tapping a board card no longer loads the task page twice. The board now shows the task without redundant data fetches, eliminating a flash or stutter that previously occurred. This fix applies across all boards and resizes, keeping the board-tap experience smooth.

<span class="label label--brand">Security</span> Tasks can link to GitHub pull requests. Board 15 now accepts automatic PR updates only from three known GitHub accounts: Valentin Yeo and two others configured by the board team, preventing outsiders from creating tasks, moving them to review, or commenting via PRs.

<span class="label label--brand">Security</span> A person who is not on a board can no longer add labels to it or modify label assignments on tasks. Outsiders now receive a Forbidden error, while board members continue to manage labels as before.

<span class="label label--brand">Security</span> A team-only share link no longer exposes task content to outsiders. Before, the page sent the whole task and comments to unauthenticated users who only saw blurred content. Now an outsider sees an empty page with a Sign in or Login bar and cannot see task details or comments.

<span class="label label--brand">Security</span> When you attempt to move or nest a task under another task on an inaccessible board, the operation is refused and nothing is saved. Hypertask validates board boundaries before allowing parent-child relationships across unrelated teams, preventing accidental exposure of foreign task titles or context.

## Relations between tasks
Create relationships between tasks to surface context without leaving tasks:
- **Block**: Mark a task as blocking another task.
- **Blocked by**: Identify what indirectly holds a task back.
- **Duplicate**: Link to other tasks that represent the same work item.
- **Workers**: Associate an agent or intelligent agent with the task for scheduling and coordination.

See a task's relations in the **Relations** section of the task detail view.

## Subtasks
Break down a task into smaller units. Subtasks appear in the task detail under the **Subtasks** section. Mark them complete to show progress toward the parent task.

Add one from the parent task's **Subtasks** section. The window lists tasks you can link as a sub-task, and the **New sub-task** button under the search box opens the normal create window with the parent already attached. Typing a name that matches nothing still creates a new sub-task when you press Enter.

## Task property rail
The task detail sidebar includes a rail of properties (title, priority, assignees, labels, etc.). The rail now occupies the full remaining dynamic viewport height, so it uses all available space rather than a fixed maximum and leaves no unused viewport space.

**Task properties no longer scroll with the task thread**, keeping them pinned to the sidebar for easy access while browsing comments and history.

When another browser, the CLI, or an agent changes a task, its open detail page refreshes the title, assignees, labels, priority, dates, status, attachments, and linked pull requests without a reload. If the live connection is unavailable, the page checks for changes every 10 seconds.

## Time tracking
Track work hours on tasks via the **Times** section:
- **B** opens the time entry modal from the task, or use the command palette ("Log time").
- Manual per-day rows let you log time for any calendar day without a timer.
- Export time logs as CSV for payroll or reporting.

See the [Time Tracking](https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/time-tracking/) guide for full details.

## AI Task Writer
The AI Task Writer is a prompt-based task creation flow that generates complete, shippable tickets from paste inputs.

### How it works today
The Task Writer writes tasks in your team's style. It uses board-aware prompts, pulls task templates from boards, and uses search to find related tickets instead of inventing them.

### Using the Task Writer
- From a board: **Ctrl+J** / <kbd>Cmd+J</kbd> and select **Create with AI** — **Task Writer**.
- From the command palette: **Ctrl+K** — search for "Task Write" and select it.
- From a task: Click the AI icon in the task header and select **Task Writer**.

After the Task Writer generates a draft, you can refine it just like any other AI-generated comment or description.

### Board task templates

Save a representative ticket through **Ctrl+K → Save as template**.
Open **Settings → Board → Task templates** to edit its name, title pattern,
and description structure. Use names such as **Bug** or **A/B test** so the
writer can match your request to the right template.

Simple descriptions support headings written with `##` and plain paragraphs.
Rich descriptions remain read-only here to preserve their formatting;
you can still change their names and title patterns.
If someone else saves first, reload before saving your changes.

When you explicitly request ideas, the writer fills them in one pass using
board tickets, documents, memory, and custom instructions. For example,
“Write an A/B test with five headlines” produces five finished headlines,
not placeholders. A matched template's title pattern and headings stay in
place. Required ICE scores include the component scores and mark estimates.
Ordinary editing requests still preserve your source instead of inventing copy.

## Instant ticket opening
<span class="label label--brand">New</span> Tickets now load instantly from cached board data, with no spinner, no "Loading..." text, and no placeholder animation. The entire opening experience is fast and lag-free across desktop and mobile.

### What you see
- **Click to open**: When you tap or click a task, it appears in about 0.15 to 0.3 seconds on both desktop and mobile.
- **No loading animation**: No full-screen spinner, no pulsing grey bars, no brief placeholder state.
