- **Suggested questions right away**: If the AI panel is open, suggested questions appear immediately—not waiting for the API response.

### Browser history
The browser back and forward buttons now behave consistently with the app:
- Press **Back** to return to the board. The board remains loaded and you can stay there.
- Press **Forward** to re-open the last ticket you viewed.

This lets you browse through tasks inside the app while the rest of your session stays tight and fast.

### Performance details
- Median open times are ~0.15 seconds on desktop and ~0.17 seconds on mobile.
- The first open after a board loads takes about 0.25 to 0.33 seconds; subsequent opens are closer to 0.13 to 0.18 seconds.
- The first open after a board loads now paints its cached title and description before expensive editing property controls, so the title and description appear instantly while controls like assignees, status, and priority still warm. This tighter paint-first sequence reduces the first-open delta to about 0.10 seconds—considerably faster than before.

### Visual smoothness
<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> Ticket pages no longer shift or jitter after opening. Visual elements that previously filled in after the initial paint now appear instantly as part of the cached board data, keeping the title, description, and controls in place across desktop and mobile for all test accounts.

### Keyboard shortcuts
We recommend using keyboard shortcuts to navigate:
- **Ctrl+J** / <kbd>Cmd+J</kbd> to jump to a task or open it with the Task Writer.
- **Ctrl+O** / <kbd>Cmd+O</kbd> to jump to a task or link from within the task detail.

These shortcuts preserve the instant-open feel and keep you moving without page spins or wait states.

### Assignee persistence
<span class="label label--brand">Improvement</span> When you assign a task from the assign picker, closing the picker or pressing Escape no longer drops the assignment. The human assignee name stays on the task and persists across page reloads and subsequent checks. This applies whether you assign from the board card or from a direct task link.

### Faster task opening
<span class="label label--brand">Improved</span> Pressing **Back** after opening a subtask now shows the parent task immediately instead of the subtask, with no "Loading..." flash, and **Forward** returns you to the subtask if needed. Opening a task directly from cached data shows it reliably within about 0.3 seconds on both desktop and mobile, eliminating previous delays.

### Navigating to previous titles in Inbox
<span class="label label--brand">Improved</span> Using **J** or the arrow keys to move to the next Inbox item now loads and displays it within about 0.3 seconds on desktop and mobile, removing lag that previously held up the wrong ticket title for up to several seconds.

### No flash of the ticket title after opening a board card
<span class="label label--brand">Fixed</span> Pressing **Back** right after opening a board card now shows the board immediately, with no flash of the ticket title. In at least 19 of 20 quick Backs (within 0.3 seconds of opening a card), you see only the board, not the ticket, and the board is visible within 1 second.

### Task detail downloads once
<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> Opening a ticket now downloads its details once, and board cards stay up to date. Before this fix, opening a task from the board or by its link would trigger 2 to 3 redundant data fetches.

### Board tap loading
<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> On mobile, tapping a board card no longer loads the task page twice. The board now shows the task without redundant data fetches, eliminating a flash or stutter that previously occurred. This fix applies across all boards and resizes, keeping the board-tap experience smooth.

### Faster open on cold phone
<span class="label label--brand">Improved</span> Opening a task on a cold phone with no cached data now shows its title and description sooner (11.8 s vs 14.1 s median, 95th-percentile gap of ~2.3 s). The first load paints the title and description earlier, while controls like assignee and priority still warm up afterward, keeping the experience instant and frictionless.

### Ticket page no longer shifts on mobile
<span class="label label--brand">Fix</span> The ticket page no longer jumps on first load. The comment box appears once and never moves: 20 of 20 fresh loads on two test accounts, on both desktop and phone. Visual elements that previously filled in after the initial paint now appear immediately as part of the cached board data, keeping the title, description, and controls in place across platforms for all test accounts.

### Comments no longer jump with content
<span class="label label--brand">Behavior change</span> The comment box and comment thread no longer shift downward as content loads, so the task layout stays consistent across desktop and mobile from open to load.

### Instant board tap
<span class="label label--brand">New</span> Clicking a board card now initializes the task with a single board interaction instead of triggering redundant rendering. This keeps the opening experience snappy across desktop and mobile, especially after boards have already been reloaded.

Loading address-bar updates that occur as part of the navigation are tracked correctly as navigations within the same page rather than distinct page loads. The change applies across all boards and view types—Kanban, table, and card lists—with consistent, performant behavior.

## Invited-in aspects and board validation

<span class="label label--brand">Improved</span> Pages that use invite links now validate board context before sending requests. **My Tasks** and **Inbox** no longer fire invite-link requests without an associated board, which previously caused console errors for unmatched requests. With this fix, such invalid requests now surface a clear, user-facing message instead of a server error, keeping the console clean and providing explicit feedback when a board context is required.

# Time Tracking
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/features/time-tracking/

import { Aside, Card, Tabs, TabItem, LinkCard, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

### Start a timer or log time manually

Use **/time** from the command palette to open the time tracking interface:
- **Timer mode**: Select a task on a board or table, or open its detail page, then press <kbd>W</kbd> to start or stop its timer
- **Per-ticket time log modal**: Press <kbd>B</kbd> (or <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd> — "Log time") on an open ticket to open an in-place dialog (day-grouped entries with a total and inline add row for any date and duration; total updates in real time as you add rows)

Both modes support saving the entry directly from the form.

### Show task totals on boards and tables

Enable **Settings → General → Time tracking → Show total time on tasks** to see each task's accumulated time without opening it.

- Board cards show the total as quiet text. An active total turns green and advances live.
- Table view adds a sortable **Time** column. Use **Configure table columns** to hide, show, or reorder it.
- Concurrent timers all contribute to the live total. Paused timers remain frozen.
- The setting is board-specific and off by default. Disabling time tracking also hides totals.

### Navigation on the time reports page

The **/time** view includes the standard app navigation rail, giving you quick access to Board, Calendar, Inbox, AI, and Search from anywhere on the time reports page.

### React to the per-ticket time log modal

The per-ticket time log modal in the task detail view links to the broader **/time** view. Click **See all time entries** (or use the link in the modal header) to open `/time?board=<board-id>&task=<ticket>` in a new tab. The /time view then:

- Loads the board and task parameters from the URL
- Shows the time log for that specific task instead of a filtered list
- Includes an add/edit entry form with full Hours/Minutes, date, and note fields
- Displays all existing time entries grouped by date for the selected task

This makes it easy to navigate from a quick check of tracked time on a ticket into a detailed log with bulk actions (add rows, edit, delete).

### Time reports in Light Mode

Time reports render correctly across Light and Dark themes:

- Reports display with clear borders to distinguish rows and columns.
- Light mode backdrops use the container background color (white for Light theme) rather than transparent or missing borders, ensuring legibility on typical white backgrounds.
- Fields like duration, assignee, and note remain fully visible and accessible; related labels and totals are legible without cross-out or missing content.

### Use filters to view reports

The **/time** view aggregates time across your workspace. Board owners and admins can report on everyone’s entries for boards they manage. Regular board members see only their own history.

| Filter | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Team** | Boards you can access in a team |
| **Board** | Specific board or project scope |
| **User** | Individual user, available when you own or administer a board in the selected scope |
| **Range** | Last 7 days, month-to-date, or custom date picker |
| **Group** | By task, board, user, or date |

Filters are saved per prompt so you can quickly reapply the same view.

### Time report date presets

Select a date range from the start of the report:
| Preset | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Yesterday** | Entries from the previous calendar day |
| **Last week** | Entries from the last full 7-day period |
| **Last month** | Entries from the previous full month |
| **Custom** | Open a date picker with <strong>From</strong> and <strong>To</strong> fields |

### Time report interaction

For any filter view that shows a duration:
- **Click a duration** to open an in-depth time log modal for that row, with the full entry history and ability to add or edit entries
- This modal is basically the same view opened from the per-ticket time log on a ticket

### Time report entry form UI

When adding or editing time entries, the time report entry form includes:
- **Duration input**: Accept HH:MM format, integer minutes, or split hours/minutes. A dedicated <strong>Hours</strong> and <strong>Minutes</strong> field makes selecting exact durations easier than combining them.
- **High-precision duration support**: Use h:mm:ss format for exact precision (e.g., `0:45:30` for 45 minutes and 30 seconds). The system stores durations at the second level for accurate reporting.
- **Date picker field**: Fully clickable date field that opens the calendar popover for quick selection
- **Multi-select filters per entry**: Board and User checkboxes toggle per entry; rows can be bulk selected with checkboxes, deleted in bulk, or exported to CSV
- **Entry-level local timestamps**: Each manual entry is stored as local-noon timestamps so logs are correctly associated with the logged day, even across time zones

This UX appears in both the per-ticket time log modal and the broader time report when adding rows. Each entry stays on a single line; the person's name truncates instead of every field wrapping on its own row.

### Time log filters

The time log modal also supports quick filters:
| Filter | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Assignee** | Filter entries by who logged them; real assignee filter helps surface who actually worked on a task rather than who merely received it |
| **All dates** | Show all time entries regardless of date |
| **Today / This week** | Quick-finishing filters for common work periods |

### View and export CSV reports

After applying filters, click **Export** to download a comma-separated values (CSV) file:
- Formatted for Excel and Google Sheets with decimal hours
- No injected formulas or formatting artifacts
- Includes task number, description, user, duration, date, and note

CSV export supports the same range and group filters as the time report.

### Prompt shortcuts

<Aside>
Use these prompt patterns when entering time tracking queries:

<dl>
<dt><code>!time today</code></dt>
<dd>Entries for the current day</dd>
<dt><code>!time task = T-123</code></dt>
<dd>Entries on task T-123</dd>
<dt><code>!time board = Marketing</code></dt>
<dd>Entries on the Marketing board</dd>
<dt><code>!time me last week</code></dt>
<dd>Your entries from the previous week</dd>
</dl>
</Aside>

### Quiet rows mode

Toggle **Quiet rows** in the view toolbar to hide the time cell for less verbose views. This keeps the table compact while preserving edit/delete access to each entry.

### Save a "what is running now" view

**Has a running timer** is a filter like any other, so a saved view can hold it permanently instead of relying on the temporary board toggle. It works in table layout as well as on the board.

The filter needs time tracking enabled on the board; with it off, or with nothing running, it matches nothing rather than everything.

### Pause and resume a timer

On the running-timers overview, **Pause** freezes a timer in place and **Resume** continues the same total. The row stays listed while paused, showing **Paused** where the end time would be, and its elapsed count stops moving everywhere it appears: the overview, the task-detail indicator, and the board card badge.

**A paused gap is never billed.** Stopping a timer while it is paused ends it at the moment you paused, not at the moment you pressed stop, so a timer left paused overnight charges the work rather than the night. Starting a paused timer again resumes it instead of leaving it frozen.

Pause and resume are available in the app and via the MCP API endpoints `/api/time/pause` and `/api/time/resume`. The CLI and MCP surfaces can start, stop, and log time, and their payloads report whether a timer is paused, but they cannot pause or resume one yet.

### Timer indicators

- **Running timer badge**: Appears in the Kanban header (Ctrl+K view) showing the number of active timers on the board
- **Per-board persistence**: Timer state is scoped per board — starting a timer on one board doesn't affect timers on other boards
- **Rail timer icon**: When time tracking is enabled, the App shell rail shows a **Timer** icon that opens the running-timers view

#### Start a timer

1. Select a task on the board or table, or open its detail page
2. Press <kbd>W</kbd> — the timer starts automatically
3. Press <kbd>W</kbd> again to stop and save the entry

#### Log time on an open ticket

1. On an open ticket, press <kbd>B</kbd> (or <kbd>Cmd+K</kbd> — "Log time")
2. Day-grouped time entries appear with rows for each calendar day and a total at the top
3. Click **Add row** to create a new entry for any date; type a duration in HH:MM or minutes (e.g., `1:30` or `90m`)
4. Enter separate **Hours** and **Minutes** values for precise durations (e.g., 1 hour 30 minutes)
5. Adjust the date, duration, and optional note per row; the Board and User fields are multi-select checkboxes per entry
6. Total updates in real time; click **Save** or press <kbd>Return</kbd> to commit all entries

#### See detailed entries for a task

1. Click the time cell on a board card to open the per-ticket time log modal
2. Click **See all time entries** in the modal header to open `/time?board=<board-id>&task=<ticket>`
3. The /time view shows the full time log, edit/add forms, and filters for that specific task
4. Add additional entries directly from the /time view using Hours/Minutes or minutes

#### Refine filter views

1. Open `/time` from the command palette
2. Select filters from the Dropdown panel:
   - **Team**, **Board**, **User**, **Range**, **Group**
3. Click **Save filters** to prompt-saved states
4. Quickly re-open saved filters from the left panel

#### Export data

1. Apply filters you want to export
2. Click **Export CSV**
3. Open in Excel or Google Sheets — times display as decimal hours ready for calculations

### Keyboard shortcut summary

<Aside>
<dl>
<dt><kbd>W</kbd> on a board, table, or task detail page</dt>
<dd>Starts/stops a timer on the selected task</dd>
<dt><kbd>B</kbd> on a ticket (open ticket only)</dt>
<dd>Opens the per-ticket time log modal (in-place dialog; fires only outside text inputs)</dd>
<dt><kbd>Cmd+K</kbd> — "Log time"</dt>
<dd>Time log modal on any open ticket via the command palette</dd>
<dt><kbd>7</kbd> on the App shell rail (when time tracking is enabled)</dt>
<dd>Opens the running-timers overview</dd>
<dt><kbd>Option</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd> or <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd> on an open task</dt>
<dd>Starts/stops the open task timer in the task detail</dd>
</dl>
</Aside>

<Aside>

<details>

<summary>Technical notes</summary>

- The `/time` interface includes an integrated header with no floating back button (consistent with settings-style pages)
- Report API supports query parameters: `?board=<id>&task=<id>&user=me&running`
- Manual entries use integer and decimal hours for duration (you can enter an integer like `3` or HH:MM format like `2h 30m`), then the system converts to decimal hours (e.g., `2h 30m = 2.5h`)
- Timer state is stored as `startTime` and `endTime` timestamps relative to the board scope
- Per-ticket time log entries live under the ticket's time tracking row and are grouped by day with a running total
- Time report now includes date presets (Yesterday, Last week, Last month, Custom), clickable durations, and split Hours/Minutes fields
- The time log modal and /time entry form support Hours, Minutes, h:mm:ss precision, and per-date local-noon storage with multi-select filters per entry
- The `/time` view now includes the standard app navigation rail
- Fixed recurrence date logic: long-abandoned fixed-period recurrences are fast-forwarded instead of stopping at 400 steps, preventing occurrences from spawning in the past

</details>
</Aside>

  title="Inbox & Notifications"
  description="Stay on top of assignments, mentions, and task updates with a unified inbox."
  href="/features/inbox/"
/>

# Mobile and desktop apps
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/apps/

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Hypertask on a phone is the web app at [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai), installed on the device. On a computer, use that same site in a browser, or install it from the browser.

## Is there a mobile app?

### Android

The official Android app is a Trusted Web Activity wrapper of [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai). It opens the web app with its own launcher icon, splash screen, and push notifications. The project README says to download the APK from the [Android releases page](https://github.com/hypertask-ai/android/releases).

<Aside type="note">
That releases page is the download location. If no APK is listed there yet, install the web app with Add to Home Screen until a release is published.
</Aside>

### iPhone and other phones

Install the web app with **Add to Home Screen**.

On an iPhone, open [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai) in Safari, tap **Share**, then **Add to Home Screen**. On other phones, use the browser's **Add to Home Screen** or **Install** command.

The site publishes a web app manifest named Hypertask with `display` set to `standalone`, so the home-screen icon opens Hypertask without the browser toolbar. The live manifest is [app.hypertask.ai/manifest.webmanifest](https://app.hypertask.ai/manifest.webmanifest).

## Is there a desktop app for Windows or Mac?

Use the web app in a browser. Chrome and Edge can also install [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai) as an app from the address bar. That installed window is the same web app.

<Aside type="caution" title="No signed desktop download">
Hypertask does not publish a signed desktop installer for Windows or Mac.
</Aside>

[hypertask-desktop](https://github.com/hypertask-ai/hypertask-desktop) is an early-pilot native client written in Rust with GPUI. It covers Inbox, Board, and Task detail, and you build it from source. The repository has no GitHub release and no signed download.

# Core Concepts
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/concepts/

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

This page covers every core concept in Hypertask. Use it as a reference when building integrations or configuring your workspace.

## Projects

A project is the top-level container for work. Think of it as a board — a single workspace where your team organizes tasks into sections.

Each project has:

- **Name and description** — What the project is about.
- **Prefix** — A short code (e.g., `HT`, `API`) used to generate ticket numbers like `HT-42`.
- **Unique ID** — A numeric identifier used in the MCP API.
- **Members** — The people (and AI agents) who have access.
- **Sections** — The columns that define your workflow.
- **Views** — Saved filter/sort configurations.
- **Labels** — Custom tags for categorizing tasks.

Projects map 1:1 with boards in the UI. When an MCP tool refers to a `board_id`, it means the project ID.

## Sections

Sections are the columns on a project board. They represent stages in your workflow.

**Default sections** when you create a project:

| Section | Typical use |
|---------|-------------|
| Todo | Work that's defined and ready to start |
| Doing | Actively in progress |
| Done | Completed and verified |

You can add, rename, reorder, or remove sections at any time. Common additions include **Review**, **Build**, **Backlog**, or **Blocked**.

Each section has:

- **Name** — Displayed as the column header.
- **Visibility** — Sections can be hidden without deleting them.
- **Rank** — Controls left-to-right ordering on the board.
- **Section ID** — Used by MCP tools to move tasks between sections.

<Aside>
Use `hypertask_projects` with `action: "manifest"` to find the section ID, then `hypertask_tasks` with `action: "update"` and `input.section_id` to move a task into that section.
</Aside>

## Tasks

Tasks are the core unit of work. Every task belongs to exactly one section within one project.

### Properties

| Property | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| **Title** | Short, actionable summary of the work |
| **Description** | Rich HTML content with full context, acceptance criteria, and links |
| **Ticket number** | Auto-generated sequential ID scoped to the project (e.g., `PROJ-123`) |
| **Priority** | `Urgent`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, or `None` |
| **Estimate** | T-shirt sizing: `XS`, `S`, `M`, `L`, `XL`, `XXL`, `XXXL` |
| **Due date** | Optional deadline |
| **Status** | `Normal`, `Archive`, or `Deleted` |
| **Section** | Current column on the board |
| **Assignees** | One or more team members responsible for the work |
| **Followers** | Users who receive notifications (auto-added via @mentions) |
| **Labels** | Custom tags for categorization |
| **Subtasks** | Nested tasks for breaking down work |

### Subtasks

Any task can have subtasks — smaller units of work nested under a parent. Subtasks are full tasks themselves, with their own title, assignee, priority, and status. Use them to break complex work into trackable steps.

### Task relations

Tasks can be linked to each other with typed relationships:

| Relation | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `RelatedTo` | General association between two tasks |
| `BlockedBy` | This task cannot proceed until the linked task is done |
| `BlockedTo` | This task is blocking another task from proceeding |

Relations are bidirectional — creating a `BlockedBy` link on Task A to Task B automatically creates a `BlockedTo` link from Task B to Task A.

## Assignees and followers

### Assignees

A task can have **multiple assignees**. All assignees:

- See the task in their inbox
- Receive notifications when the task is updated or commented on
- Are responsible for completing the work

Use the `hypertask_tasks` (`action: "assign"`) MCP tool to add or remove assignees programmatically.

### Followers

Followers are users who receive notifications about a task without being responsible for it. Users become followers when:

- They are **@mentioned** in a comment or description
- They **manually follow** the task through the UI
- They **create** the task (the creator auto-follows)

## Comments

Comments are threaded discussions attached to a task. They serve as the primary communication channel for async collaboration.

Each comment supports:

- **HTML formatting** — Bold, italic, code blocks, links, lists, and more. All comments use HTML, not Markdown.
- **@mentions** — Reference team members by name. Mentioned users are auto-added as followers and receive inbox notifications.
- **Reactions** — Emoji reactions on any comment for lightweight feedback.
- **Attachments** — Files attached to comments for sharing screenshots, documents, or other artifacts.

<Aside type="tip">
When an AI agent completes a task, best practice is to post a comment summarizing what was done, what changed, and any relevant file paths or URLs. This creates an audit trail that teammates can review async.
</Aside>

## Labels

Labels are custom tags you define at the project level. Use them to categorize tasks by type, area, or any dimension that matters to your team.

Examples:

- `bug`, `feature`, `chore`
- `frontend`, `backend`, `infra`
- `quick-win`, `tech-debt`

Tasks can have multiple labels. Labels are filterable in views.

## Views

Views are saved filter and sort configurations for a project. They let you slice the board in different ways without changing the underlying data.

A view can filter by:

- Section
- Assignee
- Priority
- Label
- Due date

And sort by:

- Priority
- Due date
- Created date
- Ticket number

Each project can have multiple saved views. They're useful for creating focused perspectives like "My tasks", "Urgent items", or "Overdue work".

A label filter can also leave tasks out. Open the tags filter, pick your labels, then set the toggle to **Hide tags**. The view drops every task carrying one of those labels and keeps the rest. Saved views remember it, and asking AI Chat for everything except those labels sets it up for you.

## Inbox

The inbox is a unified notification center for each user. It surfaces work that needs your attention.

You receive inbox notifications when:

| Event | Notification |
|-------|-------------|
| **Assigned to a task** | Task appears in your inbox |
| **Comment on your task** | New comment notification |
| **@mentioned in a comment** | Mention notification |
| **Task due date approaching** | Due date reminder |
| **Task overdue** | Overdue warning |

Inbox items can be **archived** once handled. Use `hypertask_inbox` (`action: "list"`) to check notifications and `hypertask_inbox` (`action: "archive"`) to clear them via MCP.

<Aside>
AI agents should check their inbox at the start of each session to pick up newly assigned work. This is the recommended pattern for agent-driven task execution.
</Aside>

## Teams

Teams are organization-level containers that group projects and members under a shared billing account.

Key aspects:

- **Seat-based billing** — Each team member (human or AI agent account) occupies a seat.
- **Member roles** — Control who can create projects, manage billing, or invite new members.
- **Shared projects** — All projects within a team are accessible to team members based on their role.

A user can belong to multiple teams, each with its own projects, billing, and member roster.

# Get help
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/contact-support/

Start at the [AI help chat](https://help.hypertask.ai). It answers from these docs, and it can hand the conversation to the team in the same chat when it cannot solve something.

- Ask there first, including when you want to talk to a person.
- You can email [help@hypertask.ai](mailto:help@hypertask.ai). The [contact page](https://hypertask.ai/contact/) uses that address for support, partnership, and press.
- Signed in, open **Settings → Help → Send feedback**. That screen says it goes straight to the team. Mark it Bug, Idea, Question, or Praise.
- Free and BYOK list email support. Pro lists priority support.
- For privacy questions, the [privacy policy](https://hypertask.ai/privacy/) names Hypertask Lab Ltd. and links to the same contact page.

# What is Hypertask?
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/introduction/

import { Steps, TabItem, Tabs, Aside, Card, CardGrid } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

# What is Hypertask?

<div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-6 mb-8">
  <Card title="AI-native collaboration" icon="🤖">

  </Card>

    Clean Kanban boards, calendar views, a unified Inbox for mentions and updates, and a Theme picker supporting Light, Dark, AMOLED, and custom Paper theme.
  </Card>

## Setup options

Whether you prefer a browser UI, the command line, or integrating via code, there's a path that fits your workflow.

<Tabs>
<TabItem label="Browser" open>
<p class="lead">Sign in with email on <code>app.hypertask.ai</code> to start collaborating immediately. Invite your team and start adding tasks, boards, and workflows.</p>
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="CLI">
<p class="lead">Manage and create tasks from the terminal with the <code>hypertask</code> CLI. Install via your package manager, login, and start creating.</p>
<Steps>
<ol>
<li>Install the CLI via npm or homebrew.</li>
<li>Run <code>hypertask login</code> and follow the on-screen prompts.</li>
<li>Use commands like <code>hypertask task create</code>, <code>hypertask task list</code>, and <code>hypertask comment add</code> from your shell.</li>
</ol>
</Steps>
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="MCP">
<p class="lead">Connect Hypertask to your AI agents via the Model Context Protocol. The MCP server exposes tools for tasks, boards, chat, and more.</p>
<Steps>
<ol>
<li>Add the Hypertask MCP endpoint to your LM Studio, Claude Desktop, or another MCP-compatible client.</li>
<li>Authenticate with a Bearer token or session cookie.</li>
<li>Use <code>hypertask_tasks</code> for task creation and assignment, and <code>hypertask_comments</code> for replies.</li>
</ol>
</Steps>
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="REST API">
<p class="lead">Use our REST API to build integration or mobile apps. Seeds, boards, views, tasks, comments, and more are all reachable via simple HTTP requests.</p>
<Steps>
<ol>
<li>Get an API key from the Settings sidebar in the app.</li>
<li>Add <code>Authorization: Bearer &lt;key&gt;</code> headers to your requests.</li>
<li>Use endpoints like <code>GET /boards</code>, <code>POST /tasks</code>, <code>POST /messages/chat</code>, and more.</li>
</ol>
</Steps>
</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Core concepts

Here's a quick overview of the key concepts you'll use in Hypertask.

| Concept | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Workspace** | The top-level container for your organization. Board owners can choose whether a board belongs to one workspace or automatically inherits from the owner. |
| **Board** | A flexible surface for organizing work: Kanban columns, tables, lists, or calendars. Boards contain sections, views, and tasks. |
| **Section** | A column on a Kanban board with tasks that share a common state or trigger. Sections support drag-to-reorder. |
| **View** | A custom perspective on a board—filtering, sorting, grouping, or hiding tasks. Views can be pinned, hidden, or deleted as needed. |
| **Task** | A unit of work with a title, description, assignee, tags, subtasks, and relations with other tasks and issues. |
| **Chat** | An in-app AI assistant that understands your context—tasks, boards, messages, and more. You can create and edit saved GPTs, speed up writing, and control agents and time tracking. |
| **Inbox** | A unified feed of mentions, important items, reactions, and updates across your boards. Unread items are highlighted and accessible via keyboard navigation. |
| **Agents** | Autonomous AI agents that can pull context from your board, create and update tasks, respond to comments, run schedules, and interact with your workspace via tools. |

<Aside type="note">
It's Email-native, but not Firebase-dependent. Hypertask uses Better Auth and your own SMTP for signing in, with Firebase kept exclusively for push notifications. You can also integrate via CLI, MCP, or REST without going through the app UI at all.
</Aside>

## Getting started

<Steps>
<ol>
<li>Create an account or sign in with email/app password at <a href="https://app.hypertask.ai">app.hypertask.ai</a>.</li>
<li>Request a new sign-in link if your browser session expires or is shared; links are single-use, so each click gives you a fresh sign-in.</li>
<li>Request a new verification link when creating a new account; never reuse old verification emails.</li>
<li>Set your preferred theme using the <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> command palette or the Theme picker in Settings (Light, Dark, System, AMOLED, Paper).</li>
<li><strong>For email signups:</strong> You land directly on a board and receive a welcome email containing install steps for Claude Code / Cursor MCP along with a link to your board.</li>
<li>Invite teammates to your workspace and create your first board (Kanban, Table, List, or Calendar).</li>
<li>Start adding tasks, tagging them for organization, and assigning them.</li>
<li>Use <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> to access the command palette for quick navigation and actions.</li>
<li>Chat with the AI assistant to create tasks, summarize boards, or brainstorm without leaving the page.</li>
<li>Optional: install the CLI or set up an MCP agent for programmatic control over your tasks.</li>
</ol>
</Steps>

## Keyboard shortcuts

Hypertask has a rich set of keyboard shortcuts across surfaces. Press <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> to open the command palette and search for shortcuts by name.

<Aside>
Depending on your OS, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> is <kbd>Control</kbd> on Windows/Linux and ⌘ on macOS.
</Aside>

<code>Ctrl+K</code> — Open command palette for shortcuts and actions.

<code>Ctrl+G</code> — Navigate surfaces (Inbox → Boards → My Tasks → Chat), as needed.

### Live shortcuts

The command palette shows all shortcuts relevant to your current context, such as boards, tasks, inbox, and chat. Hover over a shortcut to see its location (modal, board surface, or button).

### Keyboard hints in the UI

The header's **Login** button shows a "Press L to log in" tooltip when you hover over it or focus it with the keyboard. This hint highlights the visual keycap style for improved discoverability and accessibility.

## Onboarding

First-time users see an <strong>Onboarding Tour</strong> when they sign in. You can replay it at any time by pressing <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>, searching for "Onboarding tour", and selecting the replay option.

The tour walks you through connecting AI, creating your first board, and using key features. Invited teammates see a trimmed version that skips heavy setup but still introduces essential workflows.

## Security, auth, and permissions

Hypertask uses server-side authentication and ensures that other users' data never leaks into your boards or views. Here are some key principles:

- <strong>Email sign-in & Better Auth</strong>: Sign in is handled server-side. Email login takes you directly to your board; magic-links and sign-out remain functional.
- <strong>Firebase for push only</strong>: Firebase Auth is not used for login or signup. Firebase is strictly for FCM push notifications.
- <strong>Route cleanup</strong>: Dead authentication routes that no longer exist (e.g. old signup or password reset paths) return 404, and CORS carve-outs are removed for production security.
- <strong>Session integrity via signed ht_session cookies</strong>: API routes validate signed <code>ht_session</code> cookies alongside <code>nookies_user</code>, ensuring that forging cookies cannot be used for cookie spoofing.
- <strong>PostHog cross-domain visitor identity</strong>: Signin and load attribution between <code>hypertask.ai</code> and <code>app.hypertask.ai</code> use signed ht_session cookies, avoiding client-side cookie dependency.
- <strong>Strict account linking</strong>: Linking a Google login to an unverified local account is blocked, ensuring verified local accounts are not orphaned.
- <strong>Multi-tenant isolation</strong>: By design, boards, views, and tasks belong to the user. Archive and other features show only your data unless explicitly shared.
- <strong>Single-use login and verification links</strong>: When you request a new sign-in link or account verification email, the link is valid for one use only. Attempting to reuse a link shows an "invalid or expired" message and does not grant a session.
- <strong>Board-level access for files</strong>: Only people who can see a ticket can download its attachments. Access is scoped to the task: observers outside the ticket cannot reach files and previews, even if they can view the board.

<Aside type="tip">
For finer-grained security, you can use the REST API to enforce claims, tokens, and additional checks for your integrations.
</Aside>

## Frequently asked questions

<details>
<summary>Is Hypertask free?</summary>

The Free plan includes unlimited members and unlimited open tickets. You can own up to 3 boards. Archived boards are not counted. A paid or comped plan has no board limit. See [Billing & Seat Management](/features/billing/) for details.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Can I export my tasks?</summary>

Yes. Export options include CSV, JSON, and integrations with IDEs, build tools, and CI/CD pipelines using the CLI and REST API.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Is there a mobile app?</summary>

Yes. Android has an official app, and iPhone and other phones install the web app with Add to Home Screen. See [Mobile and desktop apps](/getting-started/apps/).
</details>

<details>
<summary>Is there a desktop app for Windows or Mac?</summary>

Use the web app in a browser, or install it as an app. There is no signed desktop download. See [Mobile and desktop apps](/getting-started/apps/).
</details>

# Quick Start
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/quickstart/

import { Steps, Tabs, TabItem, Aside, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## For humans

<Steps>

1. **Sign up** at [hypertask.ai](https://hypertask.ai) using email or Google.

2. **Get onboarded.** Visitors landing at [hypertask.ai/demo](https://hypertask.ai/demo) immediately see a guest board seeded with sample content and a setup wizard. On desktop, the AI Task Writer opens by default; press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>K</kbd> and select "Create board" to open the Board creation assistant, which walks you through naming, adding columns, and inviting people.

3. **Create a project** from the dashboard. Give it a name and a short prefix (e.g. `HT` for "Hypertask") - this prefix is used for ticket numbers like `HT-1`, `HT-2`.

4. **Set up sections.** Every new project starts with default sections. A typical workflow uses:

   | Section | Purpose |
   |---------|---------|
   | Todo | Work that's ready to be picked up |
   | Doing | Actively in progress |
   | Review | Completed, awaiting review |
   | Done | Shipped and verified |

   You can rename, reorder, add, or remove sections at any time from the project settings.

5. **Create your first task.** Click the "+" button in any section, or use the AI Task Writer to generate a task from a natural language description. Fill in:
   - **Title** - Keep it short and actionable (e.g. "Add password reset flow")
   - **Description** - Rich HTML content with context, acceptance criteria, links
   - **Priority** - Urgent, High, Medium, Low, or None
   - **Estimate** - XS, S, M, L, XL, XXL, XXXL

</Steps>

<Aside type="note">
<strong>Email sign-in links are single-use.</strong> Once you click a sign-in or verification link in your email, the link expires and can't be clicked again. If you miss it or accidentally open it in a browser, requesting a fresh link sends you another valid, single-use link.
</Aside>

## For AI agents (MCP)

Hypertask exposes an MCP server over Streamable HTTP. Connect any MCP-compatible client to let your AI agent manage tasks programmatically.

### Get your API key

<Steps>

1. Open [app.hypertask.ai](https://hypertask.ai) and go to **Settings**.
2. Navigate to the **API Keys** section.
3. Click **Generate API Key** and copy the token.

</Steps>

<Aside type="caution">
Treat your API key like a password. It grants full access to your projects and tasks. Never commit it to version control.
</Aside>

### Connect your client

Add the Hypertask MCP server to your client's configuration:

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Claude Code">

Add to your Claude Code MCP settings (`.claude/settings.json` or project-level `.mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hypertasks": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Claude Desktop">

Open **Settings > Developer > Edit Config** and add to `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hypertasks": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Restart Claude Desktop after saving.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Cursor">

Open **Settings > MCP Servers > Add Server** and configure:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hypertasks": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

Replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with the token from the previous step.

### Verify the connection

Ask your client to call `hypertask_user_context` with the `hello` action:

```json
{
  "action": "hello",
  "input": {}
}
```

This returns your user details and accessible boards. Authentication comes from the bearer token in your client configuration, not from a connection tool.

Next, ask:

```text
List all my Hypertask projects.
```

The agent calls `hypertask_projects` with `action: "list"`. If you see your boards, the connection is working. Use the current resource tools and pass action-specific fields in `input`.

## Your first task workflow

Here's a typical task lifecycle - whether you're working through the UI or via an AI agent:

<Steps>

1. **Create a task** in the Todo section. Give it a clear title and description.

2. **Assign it** to a team member or AI agent. The assignee receives an inbox notification.

3. **Move to Doing** when work begins. This signals to the team that someone is actively working on it.

4. **Post comments** as work progresses. Use HTML formatting for code snippets, links, or structured updates.

5. **Move to Review** when the work is complete. Add a comment summarizing what was done.

6. **Move to Done** after review passes. The task is archived and the ticket number remains for reference.

</Steps>

<Aside>
AI agents follow this same workflow. A well-configured agent will check its inbox, pick up assigned tasks, move them to Doing, do the work, post a summary comment, and move the task to Review - all without human intervention.
</Aside>

# Security and privacy
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/security-and-privacy/

## Do you support SSO or SAML login?

No. Hypertask does not offer SSO, SAML, or SCIM.

You can sign in with Google, with email, or with a passkey. Email sign-in sends a temporary login link and a verification code. The login page shows **Sign in with a passkey** when the browser supports passkeys. Add or remove a passkey in **Settings → Profile → Accounts**.

A signed-in session lasts 30 days. Using Hypertask refreshes that session about once a day, which starts the 30 days again.

## Is Hypertask GDPR compliant, and where is my data stored?

The [privacy policy](https://hypertask.ai/privacy) is from Hypertask Lab Ltd. in London. It describes your right to request access to the personal information Hypertask holds, and to ask for a correction when that information is inaccurate, incomplete, or out of date. Third parties named in the policy include Google Analytics, Gmail, and Stripe. Google Calendar is included only if you connect it.

These docs do not state a data hosting region, and they do not include a data processing agreement. For data-processing questions, [contact support](https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/contact-support/).

## Can I delete my account?

Yes. Open **Settings → Profile → General**. Under **Danger zone**, choose **Delete account**.

The screen says this wipes your boards and data, and that your email can sign up again from scratch. Confirming shows that this cannot be undone and that everything you own is wiped. Hypertask then signs you out.

Cancel your subscription before you delete the account. If a subscription is still active, deletion is refused, and the screen says it could not delete your account.

## Can I export my data?

There is no data export in the app. You can read tasks with the [REST API](/api/rest-api/) and the [CLI](/cli/reference/) (`hypertask task list`).

# Profile & Settings
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/settings-profile/

import { Aside, Steps, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Your Profile page in Hypertask is split into three dedicated sections: **General**, **Appearance**, and **Task page**. Each has its own navigation point and can be accessed directly from anywhere in the app via `Ctrl+K`.

---

## General

The **General** tab contains your identity settings:

- **Avatar** — Upload or change your profile picture.
- **Display name** — The name shown to others in tasks, comments, and activity feeds.
- **Email** — Your primary email address; used for notifications and logins.
- **Bio** (optional) — A short description shown in your profile card.

Use these fields to manage how you appear across the platform.

## Session settings

Hypertask uses Better Auth server-side authentication with configurable login session duration:

- **Session length** — Choose between 7 days and 30 days when signing in. This controls how long your session stays active before requiring re-authentication.
- **Persistent sign-in links** — Access a persistent sign-in link that doesn't expire until used.
- **Clean sign-out** — All flows support immediate session invalidation and cookie clearing.

## Privacy & cookies

Hypertask respects your right to control how your data is collected. By default, tracking is disabled until you make an explicit choice:

- **No tracking until consent** — Tracking cookies and IP lookups are not stored or performed until you select an option.
- **Consent banner** — Every visitor sees a cookie banner on login, signup, and when you open a signed-in board.
- **Shared consent choice** — Your tracking preferences on hypertask.ai are shared across all Hypertask products and tracked behavior follows your choice.

This ensures your data is not collected without your knowledge or agreement.

---

## Appearance

The **Appearance** tab controls the visual look of your interface:

- **Theme** — Choose between Light, Dark, or System theme (automatically follows your OS preference).
- **Font size** — Adjust text size across the app for better readability.
- **Reduced motion** — Reduce animations for a calmer environment.

## Task page

The **Task page** tab configures behavior specific to how tasks display:

- **Show task scroll** (on/off) — When enabled, Hypertask automatically scrolls to the full task description and details when opening a task.
- **Subtask depth** — Control how many levels of subtasks are visible by default.
- **Expand inline details** — Show fields like due date, assignee, and labels inline on the task card.

These settings apply to the task detail view and the task editor across all boards.

## AI settings

The **AI Settings** tab in the Task page section allows you to configure how the AI assistant behaves across your tasks and comments:

- **Custom instructions** — Provide board-level instructions that the AI follows when helping with tasks on that board. Enter your instructions directly into the text box, which fills the page to give you maximum writing space and easy visibility of full context.

These instructions are applied automatically when the AI drafts responses, edits descriptions, or proposes next steps in chat or comments.

## Ask the AI to change a setting

On any Settings page you can ask the AI chat, in plain words, for a change on that page:

- Say what you want: "switch me to the dark theme", "turn off email notifications for comments", or "make Anna an admin on this board".
- The reply carries one **Setting change** card showing the setting, its current value and the new value. Nothing changes until you press **Apply**; press **Cancel** and nothing happens.
- Once a change lands, the card offers **Undo**, which puts the previous value back.
- The card also shows **Open setting**, so you can go to the control yourself.

The AI uses your own rights, exactly as if you clicked. A board member cannot change what only the board owner may change, and access and people changes always go through the same card. If a change is not something it can make, it tells you where the setting lives and opens that page.

## User profile caching

On authenticated startup, Hypertask reuses a fresh account-scoped user profile cached at the app shell layer. The cached profile remains valid for about 5 minutes, reducing repeated `/api/users/getById` refetches and improving cold start performance. The cache is automatically invalidated and refreshed as needed.

## Preferences via signed login

Preferences now load and save correctly with a signed login alone, without requiring the older profile cookie. As long as your session is signed in, the Preferences page can read and write settings such as Play GIFs, text size, and theme, and changes persist across reloads.

```bash
# Signed in with your session only
# Navigate to Settings → Task page
# Toggle Play GIFs or adjust a setting
# The change is saved immediately and survives navigation
```

This simplifies session handling so a single authentication flow serves all content and settings across the app.

## Management keys

Management keys let API, CLI, MCP, and AI chat clients manage agents and credentials. Create them under **Settings → Connect → Management keys**, next to MCP, CLI, and REST API.

<Steps>

1. Open [app.hypertask.ai](https://app.hypertask.ai) and sign in.
2. Open **Settings**, then **Connect**, then **Management keys**.
3. Enter a name, choose a scope, and choose an expiry.
4. Choose **Create key**. Copy the key immediately. It is shown once.

</Steps>

**Scope** is **Management**, **Usage**, or **Full access**. Full access stays on the whole account. Usage reads team AI usage and spend. Management manages agents and keys.

**Expiry** is **Never**, **30 days**, **90 days**, or **365 days**. A new management key starts on **Never**. The list shows **Expires** and a date, or **Never**.

When team-scoped keys are available, Management and Usage can be limited to one team. Full access cannot. A team key stops working if you lose access to that team.

REST API keys are on the same **Connect** screen, under **Developer access**. They use the same four expiry choices, and a new REST API key starts on **90 days**.

If a client is refused after a key's date, see [MCP troubleshooting](/mcp/troubleshooting/).

## Common Actions

### Change your avatar or name

1. Open your Profile page in the app.
2. Switch to the **General** tab.
3. Upload a new image or edit your name under the Avatar or Display name fields.
4. Click **Save** to apply changes.

See [Keyboard Shortcuts](/features/keyboard-shortcuts/) for cmd-k access to Profile and General.

| `Ctrl+K` then type "General" | Jump to General tab |
| `Ctrl+K` then type "Appearance" | Jump to Appearance tab |

# Switching from Trello, Jira, or Asana
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/switching/

Switching from Trello, Jira, or Asana usually starts with two questions: whether existing tasks can move over, and how Hypertask differs from Linear or Jira.

## Importing tasks

Hypertask has no task import. There is no one-click import from Trello, Jira, Asana, or Linear. The import routes in the product import [AI skills](/features/skills/), not tasks.

Export a CSV from the old tool. Connect an agent over [MCP](/mcp/overview/) or the [CLI](/cli/reference/), and ask it to create the tasks from that file.

- CLI: [`hypertask task create`](/cli/commands/#hypertask-task-create) creates one task. It needs a project id and a title.
- MCP: [`hypertask_tasks`](/api/tools-reference/#hypertask_tasks) with action `create` creates one task the same way.

[Agent workflows](/mcp/workflows/) describe how an agent lists board work and creates tasks.

## How Hypertask differs

- **Keyboard-first UI.** The [search screen](/features/search-screen/) is a keyboard-first way to find tasks, and the app publishes its [keyboard shortcuts](/features/keyboard-shortcuts/).
- **AI agents.** Agents [pick up board work](/mcp/workflows/) over MCP and the CLI.
- **BYOK plan.** [Bring Your Own Key](/features/byok/) uses your own model keys. [Included AI](/features/ai-features/#included-ai-allowance) describes the Free, Pro, and BYOK allowances.

# Troubleshooting Login
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/getting-started/troubleshooting-login/

## Getting stuck at the login page

If the page appears stuck or doesn't finish loading, check these conditions:

- **Browser cookies are blocked**: Clear cookies or open the site in an incognito window to test if the issue resolves
- **Popup blockers are enabled**: Allow popups for `hypertask.ai` to ensure authentication flows complete
- **Network proxy or VPN**: Temporarily disable your proxy and try again

Some privacy-focused browser extensions and add-ons lock built-in Error objects to protect you from JavaScript errors. In rare cases this blocks Hypertask from properly creating error messages.

To work around this, try one of the following:

- Disable privacy extensions during login, then re-enable them once you've signed in
- Open Hypertask in an Incognito window with extensions disabled — this is the quickest way to verify the issue is related to an extension

## "Email not found" or "Invalid email"

Create a free account or contact your team administrator if you don't see an option to sign up.

## Resetting password

1. Click **Log in**
2. Select **Forgot password**
3. Enter your email address and follow the password-reset link sent to your inbox
4. If you don't receive a reset email, check your spam folder or [get help](/getting-started/contact-support/)

## Account switching behavior

When you start a new login for a different account from the same browser:

- All authentication cookies are properly invalidated after a sign-out (Max-Age=0)
- New session cookies are set for the new account
- Both Better Auth and user identity cookies are refreshed correctly
- You're immediately redirected to a board as the new user

Your logged-in state persists across sessions; hiding or closing the browser doesn't automatically log you out unless you explicitly sign out. Authentication is verified server-side on each request via the signed `ht_session` cookie.

## Sign-in security improvements (hypertask.ai login)

- The sign-in email endpoint no longer returns verification codes or magic-link tokens to callers. This prevents callers from using the response to reset or take over an email account without direct access to the inbox.
  - <div style="aspect-ratio: 16/9; margin: 0.75rem 0;"><iframe style="width: 100%; height: 100%;" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/J7GYxffM7FE" title="Hypertask Live Demo" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen></iframe></div>
- Legacy API routes requiring only a non-authenticated session are now protected with signed login checks. Logged-out requests are now refused on all legacy routes, and the system uses verified `ht_session` cookies for all route access.
- A valid sign-out invalidates login cookies in the browser and refreshes Better Auth sessions on the server, preventing copied or reused cookies from granting continued access after a user signs out.
  - <div style="aspect-ratio: 16/9; margin: 0.75rem 0;"><iframe style="width: 100%; height: 100%;" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/T4JnbqyPovw" title="Hypertask Quickstart" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen></iframe></div>

Your credentials and login processes otherwise remain unchanged; simply use your email and password or the password reset flow as usual. If you receive password reset emails or confirmations, verify they were sent by `hypertask.ai`; invalid or forwarded reset links are not sent by Hypertask.

---

If none of these steps resolve your issue, [get help](/getting-started/contact-support/).

# Agent SDK
Source: https://docs.hypertask.ai/mcp/agent-sdk/

import { Aside, CardGrid, Card, LinkCard, Steps, Tabs, TabItem, Code } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

This SDK is behind the feature flag <code>htpr-6115-agent-sdk</code>, available by default only to your account.

The <code>@hypertask/agent-sdk</code> lets you build autonomous agents programmatically with a small TypeScript library that follows the same shape as Linear and Plane:

- **Agent** = app with a bot identity
- **Run** (AgentSession) = one session per interaction
- **Typed activity stream** = thought, action, response, ask, error
- **Signals** = stop, select, auth_request
- **Fast acknowledgement** = post a thought within 10 seconds or the run becomes stale after 5 minutes

This SDK is the client-side counterpart to your agent infrastructure: it handles webhooks, signature verification, and typed activity recording so you can stand up a working agent in an afternoon.

## Install

```bash
npm install @hypertask/agent-sdk
# or
yarn add @hypertask/agent-sdk
```

<Aside type="tip">
The SDK is published under the <code>@hypertask</code> namespace. Install globally with <code>npm install -g @hypertask/agent-sdk</code> so the CLI generates boilerplate quickly.
</Aside>

## Adapters

The SDK includes adapters for common web frameworks and runtime environments. Use the webhook handler compatible with your stack.

| Adapter | Setup | Notes |
|---------|-------|-------|
| **Node** | Assign a TCP port to your Node server. | Built-in; robust for single-process deployments. |
| **Express** | app.use(webhookHandler) on an Express app. | Classic middleware integrations. |
| **Hono** | app.use('*', webhookHandler) on a Hono app. | Lightweight web framework. |
| **Next.js API route** | Attach to the default export route. | Plugged into framework routing. |
| **Cloudflare Workers** | Enable automatic route at the Worker entry. | Background support required; deduplication and buffering handled by the SDK. |
| **Plain Node** | Route manually using raw request bytes and background support. | Fully dependency-free but more manual wiring. |

<Aside type="tip">
Verify which adapter matches your runtime. The stamped header <code>X-Hypertask-Signature</code> is always used for verification, independent of your transport choice.
</Aside>

## Quick Start

Create a simple agent that replies when mentioned and files its responses as activity rows in the ticket thread.

```tsx
// server.ts
import { createAgent } from '@hypertask/agent-sdk';
import express from 'express';

async function main() {
  const app = express();

  const { client, webhookHandler } = createAgent({
    token: process.env.AGENT_TOKEN!,
    secret: process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
  });

  // Attaches signature-verifying webhook handling to the Express app
  app.use(webhookHandler);

  // Your agent logic wired into events
  client.on('mention', async (run) => {
    await run.thought(`Being mentioned on ticket ${run.ticket.id}`);
    await run.respond(`Noted: this is ticket ${run.ticket.id}.`);
  });

  client.on('assigned', async (run) => {
    await run.thought(`Assigned to ticket ${run.ticket.id}`);
  });

  app.listen(3000, () => {
    console.log('Agent running on port 3000');
  });
}

main().catch(console.error);
```

<Aside type="tip">
See <a href="/mcp/agent-webhooks/">Agent webhooks</a> for how to expose this Express app publicly, or use the agent-dev CLI's local tunnel for local development.
</Aside>

For a complete example that works in under 30 minutes, check out the included <code>reply-only</code> template in the templates package:

```jsx
// templates/replyOnly.ts
import { createAgent } from '@hypertask/agent-sdk/templates/replyOnly';
```

## Run Objects

Every event handler receives a <code>run</code> object that represents the current interaction. The run tracks the ticket, thread, status, and type-safe activity stream.

### Status

A run has one of these statuses during its lifetime:

| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `active` | Running and processing events |
| `stopped` | User requested stop or error occurred |
| `stale` | No activity for 5 minutes after start |
| `done` | Completed successfully |

### Activity Stream

The run records all agent communication as typed activities in the thread, with muted styling like tool calls. Use these methods to write to the activity stream:

| Method | When to Use |
|--------|-------------|
| [`run.thought(text)`](#runthinktext) | Internal reasoning or planning |
| [`run.action(text, link)`](#runactiontext-link) | Tool execution or file attachment |
| [`run.respond(text)`](#runrespondtext) | Agent response to the user |
| [`run.error(text)`](#runerrortext) | Handling failures or errors |
| [`run.ask(question, options)`](#runaskquestion-options) | UX flows that require user input |

All activity is persisted automatically when the SDK receives the <code>mentioned</code> or <code>assigned</code> event. You can also call activity methods on <code>run</code> directly.

#### run.thought(text)

Record an internal reasoning step.

```tsx
client.on('mention', async (run) => {
  await run.thought('Deciding which section to move the ticket to...');
});
```

#### run.action(text, link)

Record an external action executed by the agent, with an optional file upload link.

```tsx
await run.action('Test run started', 'https://hypertask.app/file/test-run-123.md');
```

#### run.respond(text)

Record the agent's user-facing response.

```tsx
await run.respond("I'll move it to the Bug Severity 2 section.");
```

#### run.error(text)

Record an error that you handled gracefully.

```tsx
try {
  // ...
} catch (err) {
  await run.error('Failed to fetch from external API: ' + err.message);
}
```

#### run.ask(question, options)

Create a multi-choice prompt for user interaction. The return value is a promise that resolves to the user's choice.

```tsx
const choice = await run.ask('Which section should this go to?', {
  options: [
    { value: 'urgent', label: 'Urgent Priority' },
    { value: 'normal', label: 'Standard Priority' },
  ],
});

await run.respond(`Moving to ${choice.label}.`);
```

### Ticket Helpers

The run object gives you helper methods for the current ticket. These all include built-in lease management, so you don't need to call heartbeat manually.

| Helper | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| [`run.task.move(section)`](#runtaskmovesection) | Move the task to a different section |
| [`run.task.assign(userId)`](#runtaskassignuserId) | Assign the task to a user |
| [`run.task.comment(text)`](#runtaskcommenttext) | Add a comment to the ticket |
| [`run.task.update(fields)`](#runtaskupdatefields) | Update task fields |
| [`run.task.attach(link)`](#runtaskattachlink) | Attach a file or link |

All helpers auto-heartbeat to keep your claim alive while work is in progress.

#### run.task.move(section)

Move the current task to a different board section.

```tsx
await run.task.move('Bug Severity 2');
```

#### run.task.assign(userId)

Assign the task to a user by ID, email, or display name.

```tsx
await run.task.assign(' me ');
await run.task.assign('john@example.com');
```

#### run.task.comment(text)

Add a comment to the task, which also appears in the thread.

```tsx
await run.task.comment('Routing this through to the triage team.');
```

#### run.task.update(fields)

Update any task fields by writeable property name.

```tsx
await run.task.update({
  description: 'Updated based on the agent analysis...',
  priority: 'High',
});
```

#### run.task.attach(link)

Attach a file or external link to the task.

```tsx
await run.task.attach('https://hypertask.app/file/analysis-123.md');
```

## Event Types

Your agent can subscribe to one or more incoming events. All events provide a <code>run</code> object with ticket, thread, and helpers.

```typescript
type EventHandler = (run: Run) => Promise<void>;

// Subscribe to all event types
client.on('*', handler);

// Subscribe to specific events
client.on('mention', mentionHandler);
client.on('assigned', assignedHandler);
client.on('chat', chatHandler);
client.on('stop', stopHandler);
```

### mention

Triggered when the agent is <code>@mentioned</code> in any comment or chat. Includes the full thread so far, the original prompt, and all existing activity.

```tsx
client.on('mention', async (run) => {
  // run.ticket: the ticket being mentioned
  // run.thread: messages before this event
  // run.prompt: the current task description or additional context
});
```

### assigned

Triggered when the agent is assigned directly to a ticket via the interface.

```tsx
client.on('assigned', async (run) => {
  // run.ticket: the newly assigned ticket
});
```

### chat

Triggered when a message is sent in the Agent Chat. Useful for bots that respond in chat rather than on tickets.

```tsx
client.on('chat', async (run) => {
  // run.ticket: the task chat belongs to
  // run.thread: all messages so far
});
```

### stop

Triggered when the agent's run is explicitly stopped by the user (e.g., via the agent control panel or chat interface). Use this for cleanup actions or confirmation posts.

```tsx
client.on('stop', async (run) => {
  await run.respond('Stopping work. Let me know if you need more.');
});
```

<Aside type="caution">
If you don't post a thought within 10 seconds of receiving <code>mention</code> or <code>assigned</code>, the run becomes stale after 5 minutes. Always call <code>await run.thought(...)</code> or <code>await run.respond(...)</code> on entry.
</Aside>

## Signals

The SDK automatically emits signals that your agents can respond to. These are part of the run type and include request-and-response forms.

### stop

Users can request the agent to halt (via the agent control panel or chat). A stop signal clears the lease and stops further activity.

```tsx
client.on('stop', async (run) => {
  await run.respond('Stopped. No further actions.');
});
```

### select

One-shot user choice prompts. Use <code>run.ask(...)</code> explicitly to get a promise-based choice, which renders as a multi-selector in the thread.

```tsx
const choice = await run.ask(...);
```

### auth_request

Requests for additional authentication (e.g., missing OAuth tokens). Handled through your custom auth logic when the SDK can't automatically authenticate.

## Templates

The SDK includes three ready-made templates you can use as starting points. All templates are available in the <code>@hypertask/agent-sdk/templates</code> package.

### Reply-Only Assistant

A minimal agent that only responds to mentions and chat, without touching tasks. Perfect for FAQs and bots that offer information but never modify state.

```tsx
// templates/replyOnly.ts
import { createAgent } from '@hypertask/agent-sdk/templates/replyOnly';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';

export async function createReplyOnly(
  token: string,
  secret: string,
  onRespond: (text: string) => void
): Promise<{ app: Express.Application }> {
  const { client, webhookHandler } = createAgent({ token, secret });
  const app = express();

  app.use(webhookHandler);

  client.on('mention', async (run) => {
    const response = await getBotResponse(run.prompt);
    onRespond(response);
    await run.respond(response);
  });

  client.on('chat', async (run) => {
    const response = await getBotResponse(run.prompt);
    onRespond(response);
    await run.respond(response);
  });

  return { app };
}
```

### Ticket Worker

An agent that receives assigned tickets, updates progress, and files accurate activity. Works well for triage bots, status reporters, and project workflow helpers.

```tsx
// templates/ticketWorker.ts
import { createAgent } from '@hypertask/agent-sdk/templates/ticketWorker';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';

export async function createTicketWorker(
  token: string,
  secret: string,
  onAnalyze: (ticket: any) => Promise<string>
): Promise<{ app: Express.Application }> {
  const { client, webhookHandler } = createAgent({ token, secret });
  const app = express();

  app.use(webhookHandler);

  client.on('assigned', async (run) => {
    await run.thought(`Analyzing ticket ${run.ticket.id}`);

    const summary = await onAnalyze(run.ticket);
    await run.task.comment(summary);

    await run.thought('Completed analysis');
    await run.respond('Analysis complete. See comment for details.');
  });

  return { app };
}
```

### Scheduled Bot

A bot that runs only on a cron schedule, without webhooks. Good for summaries, reports, or regular monitoring agents.

```tsx
// templates/scheduledBot.ts
import { createAgent } from '@hypertask/agent-sdk/templates/scheduledBot';
import { MemoryDeliveryScheduler } from '@hypertask/agent-sdk';

export async function createScheduledBot(
  token: string,
  secret: string,
  onTick: (run: Run) => Promise<void>
): Promise<{ app: Express.Application; scheduler: MemoryDeliveryScheduler }> {
  const { client, webhookHandler } = createAgent({ token, secret });
  const scheduler = new MemoryDeliveryScheduler();

  const app = express();

  app.use(webhookHandler);

  if (scheduler) {
    await scheduler.schedule('0 */6 * * *', async () => {
      const run = await client.createRun(COMMENT_MENTION);
      await run.thought('Scheduled bot tick');
      await onTick(run);
    });
  }

  return { app, scheduler };
}
```

<Aside type="tip">
The agent-dev CLI wraps these templates and can generate boilerplate files for your project. Install the CLI with <code>npm install -g @hypertask/agent-dev</code>.
</Aside>

## Features

- **Signature verification** — The SDK validates all incoming webhooks with HMAC signatures so you don't need to.
- **Fast acknowledgement** — Always post a thought within 10 seconds after receiving <code>mention</code> or <code>assigned</code>. If the run goes stale after 5 minutes, it automatically stops.
- **Retry-safe delivery IDs** — The SDK supports record-and-retry workflows so you can handle webhook delivery without duplicating actions.
- **Typed activity stream** — All activity (thought, action, response, error, ask) is recorded in the thread as muted rows that look like tool calls, making the agent's reasoning visible.
- **Built-in lease management** — All task helpers include heartbeat logic, so your agent never loses its claim to a ticket.
- **HTTP transport flexibility** — The SDK generates a webhook handler compatible with Express, Hono, Next.js API routes, Cloudflare Workers, and plain Node.js.

## Agent Lifecycle

1. **Create the SDK client** — Call `createAgent({ token, secret })`. The SDK wraps your existing routes and injects signature verification.
2. **Register event handlers** — Subscribe to <code>mention</code>, <code>assigned</code>, <code>chat</code>, and <code>stop</code> as needed.
3. **Handle events with a run** — Each handler receives a <code>run</code> object with ticket, thread, and helpers.
4. **Record activities** — Use <code>run.thought</code>, <code>run.action</code>, <code>run.respond</code>, <code>run.error</code>, <code>run.ask</code> to build the typed activity stream.
5. **Update tickets with helpers** — Use <code>run.task.move</code>, <code>assign</code>, <code>comment</code>, <code>update</code>, <code>attach</code> to modify tickets without managing leases manually.

The SDK automatically:
- Starts a new run on <code>mention</code> or <code>assigned</code>
- Checks the signature on every webhook
- Bounces the run if no activity occurs for 5 minutes
- Records all activity in the thread when the SDK receives the webhook

## Next Steps

| If you want to… | See |
|-----------------|-----|
| Configure webhooks | <a href="/mcp/agent-webhooks/">Agent webhooks</a> |
| Run agents on a schedule | <a href="/mcp/scheduling/">Schedule an agent</a> |
| Define patterns for multi-step workflows | <a href="/mcp/workflows/">Agent Workflows</a> |
| Learn about the infrastructure powering runs | <a href="/features/agents-dashboard/">Agents Dashboard</a> |
